10_1007_s43236_022_00530_x.key_1:
- Identity & Domain: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) for electric vehicle applications, specifically analyzing electromagnetic vibration characteristics and control system performance
- Material / Medium: Electrical steel stator core, permanent magnet rotor material; prototype parameters include 8 poles/36 slots, 2.2 kW rated power, stator outer radius 65 mm, rotor outer radius 54 mm, stator inner radius 102 mm, axial length 90 mm
- Application & Importance: Suppress electromagnetic vibration generated by supply current harmonics at different frequency bands while improving comprehensive control performance; critical for electric vehicle motors where vibration and noise significantly affect system performance
- Geometry / Domain: 8-pole, 36-slot radial flux PMSM with cylindrical geometry; analysis includes 2D finite element model of motor cross-section and 3D stator core model for vibration analysis, operating at 2000 r/min with 6 Nm load torque and 10 kHz switching frequency
10_1007_s43236_022_00530_x.key_2:
- Boundaries & Constraints: Operating condition set to 2000 r/min with 6 Nm load torque; switching frequency fs = 10 kHz; stator outer radius 65 mm, rotor outer radius 54 mm, stator inner radius 102 mm, axial length 90 mm; frequency band for sideband analysis with fU = 11333 Hz, fL = 8400 Hz, N = 42; for sideband SCH analysis, a = 1 and b = 4
- Loads / Excitations: Motor starts in no-load state with given speed of 2000 r/min; at 0.2 s, load torque of 6 Nm is applied; RFSVPWM switching frequency defined as fs = f1f(t) + Gfc where f1 = 2500, f(t) = sin(133*2π*t), G is Gaussian random number in [-1,1], and fc is a constant
- Interactions / Interfaces: Multi-physics coupling between 1D PMSM control system, 2D finite element PMSM model, and 3D stator structure; electromagnetic force load transferred from finite element model to stator structure; modal superposition applied for vibration analysis; REF introduced into 3D stator core model
- Simulation Type: Multi-physics coupled simulation including 1D control system modeling, 2D finite element analysis, and 3D vibration analysis; transient simulation for speed and torque response; harmonic response analysis using ANSYS Workbench; temporal and spatial 2D distributions of radial electromagnetic force (REF) analyzed
10_1007_s43236_022_00530_x.key_3:
- Physics Solved: Radial electromagnetic force (REF) distribution, supply current harmonics (SCH), electromagnetic vibration spectrum, modal response of stator structure, multi-physics coupling between electromagnetic forces and structural vibration
- Target Outputs (Metrics): Vibration acceleration (m/s²) at 2fe (0.190), 4fe (0.169), 6fe (0.131), 8fe (0.092), and 72fe (0.352); Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) at 13.56%; torque ripple (Tr) at 13.75%; speed overshoot (σ) at 11.45%; adjusting time (ts) at 0.0283 s; sideband current harmonic amplitude (Ab) at 1.281%; sideband vibration acceleration (Vb) at 0.043 m/s²; electromagnetic force density for (0,72fe) at 1662 N/m² and (0,78fe) at 1494 N/m²
- Optimization Goal: Reduce maximum vibration acceleration by 59.1% (from 0.352 to 0.144 m/s² at 72fe); reduce sideband vibration acceleration average amplitude by 76.7% (from 0.043 to 0.010 m/s²); reduce speed overshoot by 11.4% (from 11.45% to 0.05%); reduce torque ripple by 9.57% (from 13.75% to 4.18%); suppress 5th and 7th supply current harmonics and high-frequency sideband supply current harmonics near switching frequency
10_1007_s43236_022_00530_x.key_4:
- Geometric/Design Space: 8-pole, 36-slot PMSM prototype with fixed geometry; stator outer radius 65 mm, rotor outer radius 54 mm, stator inner radius 102 mm, axial length 90 mm; rated power 2.2 kW; spatial order constraints where v = 3k1 + 1 (k1 = 0, ±1, ±2, ...)
- Performance/Physics Limits: Operating condition constrained to 2000 r/min with 6 Nm load torque; switching frequency fs = 10 kHz; stator core resonance frequency around 9600 Hz; vibration at 2fe is unavoidable due to fundamental wave magnetic field interaction; analysis limited to specific harmonic components (4fe, 6fe, 8fe for low frequency and sideband vibrations near switching frequency)
- Process/Manufacturing: RFSVPWM parameters constrained to f1 = 2500, G (Gaussian random number) in range [-1,1], f(t) = sin(133*2π*t); inverter dead zone and nonlinearity causing unavoidable high-frequency sideband supply current harmonics; spread spectrum modulation increases switching loss of switching devices; switching frequency increase from spectrum spreading increases risk of motor resonance in other frequency bands

10_4028_www_scientific_net_msf_575_578_1.key_1:
- Identity & Domain: Forging processes including backward extrusion, closed-die forging, counter pressure forming, and pipe extrusion
- Material / Medium: JIS S25C annealed steel, aluminum alloy (for thin fins), slightly compressible material per plasticity theory formulation
- Application & Importance: Simulating plastic flow in precision forging to achieve 10µm dimensional accuracy; analyzing material flow patterns, forming load history, surface pressure distribution, and defects like lapping and folding
- Geometry / Domain: Two-dimensional axi-symmetric and plane-strain models; isoparametric quadrilateral elements with four nodal points; workpiece dimensions φ20 and φ16 in backward extrusion example; fixed mesh analytical zone with particle markers representing workpiece material
10_4028_www_scientific_net_msf_575_578_1.key_2:
- Boundaries & Constraints: Fixed analytical zone with Euler's fixed meshing; Tool boundaries defined by repositioning nodal points to nearest tool segments; Axi-symmetric symmetry planes in relevant models; Contact boundaries between punch/die and workpiece; Counter pressure pins as additional contact boundaries in counter pressure forming
- Loads / Excitations: Punch load up to approximately 450 kN; Punch stroke up to 8 mm; Upper tool force; Counter pressure from pins in counter pressure forming; Backward extrusion punch movement
- Interactions / Interfaces: Material markers flowing between fixed mesh elements; Tool-workpiece contact at all tool surfaces; Counter pressure pins interacting with workpiece material; Particle markers carrying equivalent strain and temperature information
- Simulation Type: Two-dimensional rigid-plastic finite element method; Axi-symmetric and plane-strain models; Slightly compressible material model (g = 0.01-0.0001); Nonlinear transient incremental analysis; Euler's fixed meshing method with isoparametric quadrilateral elements having four nodal points; Rigid-plastic formulation based on plasticity theory for slightly compressible material
10_4028_www_scientific_net_msf_575_578_1.key_3:
- Physics Solved: Plastic flow of material in forging processes; Large deformation behavior of workpiece; Material flow patterns in die cavities; Stress and strain distribution; Material defect formation (lapping, folding); Slightly compressible material behavior with small pressure sensitivity (g=0.01-0.0001)
- Target Outputs (Metrics): Punch load (kN) up to 450 kN; Punch stroke (mm) up to 8 mm; Material flow pattern via marker distribution; Forming load history; Surface pressure distribution; Equivalent strain; Sharp surface profile of extruded parts; Deformed workpiece shape; Material defects (lapping, folding)
- Optimization Goal: Achieve 10µm dimensional accuracy in precision forging; Proper filling of material inside die cavity without defects; Uniform height of extruded fins without further machining; Control material flow precisely to eliminate post-forging machining/grinding; Simulate material flow in die cavities with sharp edges; Simulate extrusion of slender parts like fins without remeshing
10_4028_www_scientific_net_msf_575_578_1.key_4:
- Geometric/Design Space: Precision forging requires exact size with dimensional accuracy of 10µm; Maximum 800 elements and 2000 markers used in simulation; Two-dimensional models serve as approximations for three-dimensional processes; Simulation of thin layer flashes and thin fins with sharp edges; Backward extrusion dimensions specified as φ20 and φ16
- Performance/Physics Limits: Material modeled with slight compressibility parameter g = 0.01-0.0001; High contact pressure during die cavity filling at process end; Computing time increases drastically when increasing elements and markers; Conventional methods cannot simulate element overlapping due to material folding/lapping defects
- Process/Manufacturing: Simulation performed on personal computer with Pentium Celeron 600MHz and 192 KB RAM; Conventional methods require remeshing at every incremental step for sharp edges and long extruded fins; Goal to omit post-forging processes like machining and grinding; Two-dimensional simulation is practical but limited compared to full three-dimensional processes; Material flow must be controlled precisely to achieve finished product without additional processing

10_1016_j_powtec_2024_119581.key_1:

- Field harvesting of King Grass silage requires proper mixing of stalk particles with additives to improve fermentation quality; existing machinery lacks in-field mixing capability for King Grass due to its high water content (80-85%)
- Silage mixing bin (0.8 m³ working volume, 1 m height, 1.2 m top diameter, 0.8 m bottom diameter); impeller blender with different-length blades (600 mm and 780 mm) in same-up orientation; cylindrical and semi-cylindrical stalk particles (diameters: 15.7 mm, 18.3 mm, 21.2 mm); 18-layer volume space divided into 12 radial grids per layer
10_1016_j_powtec_2024_119581.key_2:

- Blade inclination angles: 30°-60° range tested (specifically 34.4°, 45.0°, 55.6° in experimental design)
- Silage mixing bin dimensions: 0.8 m³ working volume, 1 m height, 1.2 m top diameter, 0.8 m bottom diameter

- Experimental validation: Bench tests with dyeing method using undyed and dyed stalks (2:1 volume ratio)

10_1016_j_powtec_2024_119581.key_3:

10_1016_j_powtec_2024_119581.key_4:

- Blade inclination angle range: 30°-60° for optimization testing
- Mixing speed range: 60-100 r/min for optimization testing

10_1016_j_heliyon_2024_e25994.key_1:
- Topology optimization of 2D structural components using finite element method
- Steel structures with Young's modulus E = 2×10¹¹ Pa and Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3 for C-clip, J-hook, and derrick examples
- MBB-beam with E = 1 unit and ν = 0.3 for validation cases
- C-clip: rectangular domain 120 mm × 100 mm × 3 mm with U-shaped notch (55 mm parallel length, 10 mm width, 5 mm radius)
- J-hook: 275 mm × 430 mm bounding box with 5 mm thickness, 40 mm hole radius, and 50 mm concave region radius
- Derrick: structural component with two top holes for load application
- MBB-beam: half-beam with 60 units width, 20 units height, and 1 unit thickness
- Volume fraction constraints: 0.3 for MBB-beam, 0.6 for C-clip, 0.5 for J-hook, 0.6 for derrick
- Boundary conditions include zero-displacement constraints and applied point loads (1125 N for C-clip, 1200 N for J-hook, 12000 N and 18000 N for derrick)
- Optimization objective: minimize compliance while maintaining specified volume fraction
- Material yield stress: 252 MPa used for Von Mises stress analysis
- Mesh types: both structured and unstructured quadrilateral (Q4) meshes used
- Unstructured meshes contain elements with aspect ratios ranging from 1.0014 to 3.4731 and skewness from 0.02 to 0.48
- Wall elements can be frozen to maintain structural integrity during optimization
- Optimization convergence threshold: maximum relative density change ≤ 0.01
10_1016_j_heliyon_2024_e25994.key_2:
- MBB-beam: Symmetry boundary condition along left edge (zero displacement in x-direction), zero-displacement at bottom-right corner in y-direction, vertical load of 1 unit at top-left corner
- C-clip: Tip of U-notch constrained to zero displacement in both x- and y-directions, left-middle point constrained to zero displacement in y-direction, two 1125 N point loads (upward on right-top, downward on right-bottom of U-notch)
- J-hook: Inner wall of hole constrained in x- and y-directions, three 1200 N point loads applied to structure
- Derrick: Bottom constrained in x- and y-directions, 12000 N force on outer hole, 18000 N force on inner hole
- Material properties: E = 2×10¹¹ Pa, ν = 0.3 for C-clip, J-hook, and derrick; E = 1 unit, ν = 0.3 for MBB-beam
- Volume fraction constraints: f = 0.3 for MBB-beam, f = 0.6 for C-clip, f = 0.5 for J-hook, f = 0.6 for derrick
- Penalization power: 3
- Maximum relative material density change threshold for convergence: ≤ 0.01
- Maximum iteration limit: 250
- Element thickness: 3 mm for C-clip, 5 mm for J-hook
- Mesh types: Both structured and unstructured Q4 meshes with varying element counts (1200-2960 elements, 1281-3117 nodes)
- Plane stress formulation with linear quadrilateral elements
- Static structural analysis with linear elastic material behavior
- Frozen elements feature to maintain specific structural features during optimization
- Minimum relative material density x_min is a small positive number to avoid numerical singularity
10_1016_j_heliyon_2024_e25994.key_3:
- Static structural mechanics analysis with plane stress formulation
- Displacement field calculation using finite element method
- Compliance (c) as the primary performance metric
- Relative material density (xₑ) for each element
- Maximum relative material density change between iterations
- Von Mises stress distribution for structural safety assessment
- Volume fraction (f) as constraint parameter
- Minimize compliance (c) while maintaining specified volume fraction
- Maximize structural stiffness with minimal material usage
- Optimization stops when maximum relative density change ≤ 0.01
- Achieve optimal material distribution within design domain
- Ensure final structure has Von Mises stress below material yield stress (252 MPa)
10_1016_j_heliyon_2024_e25994.key_4:
- Volume fraction constraint: f = 0.3 for MBB-beam, f = 0.6 for C-clip, f = 0.5 for J-hook, f = 0.6 for derrick

- Design domain boundaries: Fixed outer shape for each component (C-clip, J-hook, derrick)
- Mesh requirements: Quadrilateral (Q4) plane stress elements required
- Compliance minimization objective: Minimize structural compliance while maintaining volume fraction constraint
- Structural safety requirement: Optimized structures must have maximum Von Mises stress below yield stress (252 MPa)

10_1007_s00158_023_03704_8.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Continuum structural topology optimization results converted to beam structures using a computational framework
- **Material / Medium:** Aluminum (Young's modulus 100 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.3 for cantilever beam); Steel (Young's modulus 210 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.3, density 7800 kg/m³ for bicycle frame); Material with Young's modulus 69 GPa and Poisson's ratio 0.3 for 3D L-shaped bracket
- **Application & Importance:** Converting topology optimization results to parameterized beam finite element models to speed up design process, reduce computational effort in FE analyses, and bridge the gap between topology optimization and subsequent structural optimization
- **Geometry / Domain:** 2D cantilever beam (80×50×1mm); MBB beam with 600mm span; Bicycle frame with support at (0,100) and (1100,100); 3D L-shaped bracket (2000×1000×1200mm) with left top face constrained and right end loaded with 1N/mm² pressure
10_1007_s00158_023_03704_8.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** 
  - 2D cantilever beam: Left side fully constrained; 80×50×1mm size; 80×50 four-node plane stress elements
  - MBB beam: Right half treated as design domain due to symmetry; 600mm span; element size 2mm
  - Bicycle frame: Point (0,100) modeled as roller support; Point (1100,100) modeled as pinned support; 40×25 four-node plane stress elements with 25mm element size
  - 3D L-shaped bracket: Left top face fully constrained; Dimensions 2000×1000×1200mm; 40,000 eight-node cubic elements with 40mm element size

- **Loads / Excitations:** 
  - 2D cantilever beam: Downward vertical load F = 100N applied to middle of right side
  - MBB beam: Downward vertical force F = 1N applied to middle of upper edge
  - Bicycle frame: F1 (225,600): 142N x-axis, 956N y-axis; F2 (650,25): 7500N x-axis, -5000N y-axis; F3 (825,625): 150N x-axis, -1000N y-axis
  - 3D L-shaped bracket: Downward vertical pressure P = 1N/mm² applied to right end

- **Interactions / Interfaces:** 
  - Boundary conditions updated for joint vertices to ensure consistency with topology optimization model
  - All branches have the same cross-sectional area during initial beam structure evaluation
  - Sensitivity filter radius used in topology optimization (3mm for cantilever, 6mm for MBB, 50mm for bicycle frame, 60mm for 3D bracket)

- **Simulation Type:** 
  - Compliance minimization topology optimization with volume constraint
  - 2D plane stress analysis for cantilever beam, MBB beam, and bicycle frame
  - 3D structural analysis for L-shaped
10_1007_s00158_023_03704_8.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** 
  - Structural topology optimization of continuum materials
  - Beam finite element analysis of reconstructed structures
  - Strain energy distribution calculations
  - Displacement field analysis
  - Compliance minimization

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** 
  - Compliance values (e.g., 2.99 mJ for topology optimization result, 3.06 mJ for automatically obtained beam structure, 2.92 mJ for optimized beam structure)
  - Strain energy distribution (measured in mJ, shown in color scales from 0.017-0.077 mJ before sizing optimization)
  - Displacement fields (e.g., maximum nodal displacement of 0.063 mm in 3D L-shaped bracket)
  - Cross-sectional radii of beam members (e.g., optimal solution [1.196, 1.190, 1.255, 1.091, 0.878, 1.251, 0.855, 1.074] mm)
  - Volume constraints (e.g., volume fraction constraint set to 0.3 for cantilever beam)

- **Optimization Goal:** 
  - Minimize compliance subject to volume constraint in topology optimization
  - Achieve uniform strain energy distribution across beam members through sizing optimization
  - Minimize total mass while maintaining allowable stress (50 MPa) in bicycle frame example
  - Reduce compliance from topology optimization result to final optimized beam structure (e.g., from 0.00563 mJ to 0.00609 mJ in MBB beam example)
10_1007_s00158_023_03704_8.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**
  - Volume fraction constraints: 0.3 (cantilever beam), 0.2 (MBB beam), 0.35 (bicycle frame), 0.04 (3D L-shaped bracket)
  - Sensitivity filter radius: 3mm (cantilever), 6mm (MBB beam), 50mm (bicycle frame), 60mm (3D bracket)
  - Element discretization: 80×50 elements (cantilever), 2mm elements (MBB), 40×25 elements (bicycle frame), 40,000 elements (3D bracket)
  - Evolutionary ratio ER = 0.02 and maximum admission ratio ARmax = 0.01 for all examples
  - Maximum component size in partitioning: ns = 50 (standard), ns = 15 for bicycle frame due to coarse mesh
  - For bicycle frame: inner radius constrained to be 0.9 times outer radius

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - Allowable stress constraint of 50 MPa for both tensile and compressive stress in bicycle frame example
  - Compliance minimization as primary objective in topology optimization
  - Strain energy distribution must be more uniform after sizing optimization
  - Homotopy preservation requirement (same number of components and holes as original model)
  - Centeredness requirement (minimizing deviation from ideal centerlines of components)
  - Convergence criterion for sizing optimization: |Ck - Ck-1|/Ck ≤ τ where τ = 0.01

- **Process/Manufacturing:**
  - Method limited to beam-like structures only (stated: "it can be only used to interpret beam-like structures")
  - Topology optimization results with large junctions lead to poor homotopy
  - Requires pure 0-1 design (binary topology optimization result)
  - Density-based topology optimization results need post-processing (density thresholding) to convert to pure 0-1 design
  - Method not robust for arbitrary structures (stated: "further investigation is necessary to improve the robustness of the skeleton extraction of arbitrary structures")
  - Component merging required when adjacent joint components exist to maintain proper homotopy
  - Only applicable to continuum structural topology optimization results (not directly to ground structure methods)

10_1016_j_powtec_2021_06_004.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Die compaction process of hollow spherical particles analyzed via multi-particle finite element method (MPFEM); specifically focuses on pharmaceutical powder compaction behavior at particle level
- **Material / Medium:** Hollow spherical particles of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate (HPMCAS); elastic-perfectly plastic material properties with E/σ_y = 100 and Poisson's ratio = 0.3; d/w (diameter/shell-thickness) ratios of 2.5, 5, 6.25, 8, 10, and 12.5 investigated
- **Application & Importance:** Understanding how particle geometry (size and shell thickness) affects powder compaction behavior in pharmaceutical tablet manufacturing; critical for optimizing tablet formation process where high relative densities are required for mechanically stable tablets
- **Geometry / Domain:** Hollow spherical particles arranged in cylindrical die; two particle sizes (r1 = unit radius, r0.75 = 75% unit radius); compaction domain includes upper punch, lower punch, and die boundaries; particle arrangements studied at relative densities up to 0.9; cross-sectional analysis of Mises stress distribution at 1s, 2.5s, and 5s compaction time points
10_1016_j_powtec_2021_06_004.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Die and lower punch fixed in all degrees of freedom; upper punch velocity boundary condition to reach 90% relative density in 5 seconds; die, upper punch, and lower punch modeled as rigid bodies with no deformation; total particle mass maintained constant across models
- **Loads / Excitations:** Gravity force in DEM die filling simulation; Coulomb friction coefficient of 0.1 applied to all contact interfaces; upper punch velocity boundary condition (5-second compaction duration)
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Friction coefficient of 0.1 applied to particle-particle, particle-punch, and particle-die wall interactions; general explicit contact detection algorithm with penalty formulation; mass scaling applied to particle density to reduce computational time while maintaining energy balance ratio below 1% at RD ≥ 0.6
- **Simulation Type:** 3D transient multi-particle finite element method (MPFEM); Abaqus explicit algorithm with double precision; compaction simulation duration of 5 seconds to reach 90% relative density; elastic-perfectly plastic material model with E/σ_y = 100 and Poisson's ratio = 0.3
10_1016_j_powtec_2021_06_004.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Particle deformation mechanics during die compaction; contact interactions between hollow spherical particles; stress distribution evolution (Von Mises stress); elastic-perfectly plastic material response; particle rearrangement and buckling behavior during compression; relative density development
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Compaction stress (Σy) calculated from punch reaction forces; relative density (RD) evolution; yielded volume ratio (YV/TV); normalized contact area; Mises stress distribution; buckling behavior; initial die fill relative density; particle deformation patterns; time to reach specific relative densities; energy balance ratio (kinetic to potential energy)
- **Optimization Goal:** Understanding the influence of particle size and shell-thickness ratio (d/w) on compaction behavior; determining how reduced shell-thickness affects required compaction stress to achieve equivalent relative density; characterizing the relationship between shell thickness and yield behavior; identifying buckling phenomena in hollow particles during compaction for pharmaceutical tablet manufacturing applications
10_1016_j_powtec_2021_06_004.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Die radius constrained to 10rL (10× large particle outer radius); particle size limited to two options (rL = unit radius, r0.75 = 75% unit radius); d/w ratios restricted to specific values: 2.5, 5, 6.25, 8, 10, and 12.5; maximum particle count limited to under 2000 due to computational intensity; mesh element count per particle ranges from 600 to 3363 in sensitivity analysis; particle models designed with three thickness sections (two outer layers at 0.05 thickness each, remaining layer with global seeding size of 0.125)
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Elastic-perfectly plastic material with fixed E/σy ratio of 100; Poisson's ratio constrained to 0.3; friction coefficient fixed at 0.1 for all contact interfaces; energy balance ratio maintained below 1% at RD ≥ 0.6; compaction duration fixed at 5 seconds to reach 90% relative density; target relative density of 0.9 RD for all simulations; total mass kept constant across all models for consistency
- **Process/Manufacturing:** Compaction process duration limited to 5 seconds (matching experimental setup); experimental die fill height set to 16 mm; wall clock time constrained to <60 hours; cohesive elements excluded (only compaction and unloading simulated, not ejection); monomodal particle size distribution used (no size variation); no variation in frictional properties between different contact interfaces; simulation limited to gravity forced random die filling with DEM particle generator allowing only one particle type at a time

10_1016_j_engfracmech_2010_08_002.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Reinforced concrete (RC) beams with multiple cohesive crack propagation using hybrid finite element–scaled boundary finite element method (FEM-SBFEM)
- **Material / Medium:** 
  - Concrete: Compressive strength (f_c) = 23.7 MPa (Beams 1-2), 34.2 MPa (Beam 3); Tensile strength (f_t) = 2.37 MPa (Beams 1-2), 2.77 MPa (Beam 3); Fracture energy (G_f) = 0.15 N/mm (Beams 1-2), 0.088 N/mm (Beam 3); Young's modulus (E_c) = 24 GPa (Beams 1-2), 28.854 GPa (Beam 3); Poisson's ratio (ν_c) = 0.18
  - Reinforcement steel: Young's modulus (E_s) = 200 GPa; Poisson's ratio (ν_s) = 0.3; Diameters: 28.7 mm (Beams 1-2), 20 mm and 14 mm (Beam 3)
  - Cohesive interface elements with Petersson's bilinear softening law for crack modeling
- **Application & Importance:** Predicting load-carrying capacities and crack patterns in RC structures; Capturing both slip (bond shear stress-slip) and split (confining stress-crack opening) failure mechanisms at concrete-reinforcement interface which significantly affect structural response
- **Geometry / Domain:** 
  - Beam 1: 5010 mm total length, 4570 mm span, 466 mm height, 95 mm cover, 305 mm thickness, 5 reinforcing bars (28.7 mm diameter)
  - Beam 2: 4100 mm total length, 3660 mm span, 461 mm height, 95 mm cover, 310 mm thickness, 4 reinforcing bars (28.7 mm diameter)
  - Beam 3: 4100 mm total length, 3520 mm span, 450 mm height, 40 mm cover, 200 mm thickness, 1×20 mm + 2×14 mm reinforcing bars
  - Hybrid discretization: Finite elements for concrete bulk and reinforcement, SBFEM rosettes for crack-tip areas, Cohesive Interface Elements (CIEs) for crack modeling
  - Mesh composition: 780 concrete elements/52 reinforcement elements/104 CIEs (Beams 1-2); 884 concrete elements/52 reinforcement elements/104 CIEs (Beam 3)
10_1016_j_engfracmech_2010_08_002.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** 
  - Symmetry boundary condition (only half of beams modeled)
  - Simple supports at beam bottom edges
  - Local arc-length constraint with updated normal plane for nonlinear analysis
  - Convergence tolerance β = 0.001 for nonlinear iterations (||R(U)||/(γ₀||Fₑ||) ≤ β)

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Point load P applied at top of beams (2505 mm from left support for Beam 1; 2050 mm for Beam 2; two loads 1000 mm apart for Beam 3)
  - Displacement-controlled loading with monitoring of load-deflection response

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Concrete-reinforcement interaction modeled with Cohesive Interface Elements (CIEs)
  - Bond-slip relation: τ = τ_max(s/s₁)^0.4 for 0 ≤ s ≤ s₁; τ = τ_max - (τ_max - τ_f)(s-s₁)/(s₂-s₁) for s₁ ≤ s ≤ s₂; τ = τ_f for s ≥ s₂ with τ_max = 2.5√f_c, τ_f = 0.15τ_max, s₁ = 0.6 mm, s₂ = 1.0 mm
  - Splitting tensile crack model: σ_c = (f_ct₀/κ)(φ_p/φ_a)(w/φ_p + 1) with f_ct₀ = 1.5 MPa, κ = 150
  - Maximum aggregate size = 20 mm
  - Damage parameter D = 1 - (k_i/k_i⁰) with limiting value D = 0.75 for severe interface damage

- **Simulation Type:**
  - Nonlinear analysis with local arc-length method
  - 2D symmetric modeling (half-beam representation)
  - Cohesive crack propagation using Petersson's bilinear softening law
  - Failure defined at peak load of load-deflection curve
  - Discrete multiple crack propagation modeling with automatic insertion of cohesive interface elements
10_1016_j_engfracmech_2010_08_002.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:**
  - Multiple cohesive crack propagation in reinforced concrete
  - Concrete fracture with fracture process zone (FPZ) modeling
  - Concrete-reinforcement interaction mechanisms including both slip (bond-shear stress) and split (tensile splitting) failure
  - Stress intensity factor (SIF) extraction at crack tips
  - Nonlinear softening behavior of cohesive cracks using Petersson's bilinear curve

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**
  - Load-deflection (P-d) curves for RC beams
  - Ultimate failure load (P_u) and corresponding displacement
  - Number, location, and propagation paths of cracks along beam span
  - Stress intensity factor K_I for crack propagation criterion
  - Damage parameter D = 1 - (k_i/k_i⁰) at concrete-reinforcement interface
  - Crack initiation and propagation sequences
  - Computational time (e.g., 1h 49min 9.8s for Beam 1 on 3.4GHz PC)
  - Number of equilibrium iterations per load step

- **Optimization Goal:**
  - Accurate prediction of ultimate failure loads by properly modeling both slip and split failure mechanisms at concrete-reinforcement interface
  - Validation of load-deflection responses against experimental data (e.g., Beam 1: P_u = 355.4kN vs experimental 356kN)
  - Realistic simulation of crack patterns by capturing both bond-slip and splitting tensile crack development
  - Demonstration that excluding either slip or split mechanism leads to inaccurate structural response predictions
10_1016_j_engfracmech_2010_08_002.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**
  - Only half of beams modeled due to symmetry in geometry and boundary conditions
  - Crack propagation restricted to element edges (new crack tip location determined at element edge intersections)
  - Rosette generation cannot overlap or share common nodes with existing rosettes
  - Crack coalescence not considered; crack propagation arrested if it overlaps with existing SBFEM rosette or crack path
  - Initial mesh density affects crack location prediction due to discrete nature of method (one crack per element)
  - Out-of-plane thickness for reinforcement layer calculated from total area of reinforcing bars

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - Crack initiation when maximum principal stress σ₁ exceeds concrete tensile strength f_t
  - Crack propagation criterion: K_I ≥ 0 (mode-I stress intensity factor)
  - Convergence tolerance for nonlinear iterations: ||R(U)||/(γ₀||Fₑ||) ≤ 0.001
  - Damage parameter threshold D = 0.75 indicates severely damaged concrete-reinforcement interface
  - Failure defined at peak load of load-deflection curve
  - Only flexural cracks considered in analysis
  - Method cannot model concrete plasticity under compression (limits failure mode prediction)
  - Method unable to predict closely spaced cracks due to minimum rosette spacing requirements

- **Process/Manufacturing:**
  - Remeshing required for crack propagation (unlike XFEM/meshless methods)
  - Simulation time dependent on mesh density (e.g., Beam 1: 1h 49min 9.8s on 3.4GHz PC with 630 elements + 90 CIEs)
  - Number of iterations per load step varies from 1 to 480, increasing upon new crack initiation
  - Requires specific mesh structure with 4-noded quadrilateral elements for concrete bulk and reinforcement
  - Cohesive Interface Elements (CIEs) must be inserted with specific area calculations based on reinforcement configuration
  - Limited to 2D symmetric modeling (no 3D implementation presented)

10_1016_j_jmrt_2024_03_226.key_1:
- Wire-arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) process for disc-shaped components
- Substrate material: SNCrW stainless steel (C 0.25-0.30%, Si 1%, Mn 1%, P ≤0.040%, S ≤0.030%, Ni 10%, Cr 20%, W 2%, Fe balance)
- Deposited material: Inconel 625 alloy welding wire (C 0.1%, Mn 0.5%, P 0.015%, S 0.015%, Si 0.5%, Cr 20-23%, Mo 8-10%, Cb 3.65%, Ti 0.4%, Al 0.4%, Fe 5%, Ta 0.05%, Ni balance)
- Single-bead-on-plate substrate dimensions: 100 mm × 100 mm × 12 mm
- Disc substrate dimensions: 100 mm diameter, 12 mm thickness
- Weaving deposition pattern creates wider (19 mm) and shallower (2.53 mm) molten pool compared to non-weaving pattern (12 mm wide, 3.43 mm deep)
- Four deposition path strategies analyzed: In-out consistent (Case 1), Out-in alternate (Case 2), Out-in consistent (Case 3), In-out alternate (Case 4)
- Weaving pattern heat source oscillates with 6 mm width and 0.9 Hz frequency
- Welding parameters: 30 V arc voltage, 120 A welding current, 1.2 mm wire diameter, 180 mm/min welding speed
- Residual stress analysis includes radial, circumferential, and axial stress components
- Maximum warping deformation measured: 1.5 mm (Case 1), 0.8 mm (Case 2), 1.0 mm (Case 3)
- Out-in alternate (Case 2) identified as optimal deposition path strategy
- Weaving pattern produces more uniform deformation and lower residual stress compared to non-weaving pattern
- Dual ellipsoid heat source model parameters: a_f = 6, a_r = 12, b = 6, c = 1, f_f = 0.6, f_r = 1.4
- Substrate constrained with three-point constraint to prevent rigid displacement while avoiding additional stress
- Thermal efficiency η = 0.7 for heat input calculation
10_1016_j_jmrt_2024_03_226.key_2:
- Substrate plates subjected to three-point constraint to prevent rigid displacement while avoiding additional stress
- Center of lower surface of disc fully constrained; three non-collinear nodes on lower surface constrained in Y-direction
- Heat radiation and thermal convection boundary conditions applied to entire surface of plates
- Dual ellipsoid heat source model with parameters: a_f = 6, a_r = 12, b = 6, c = 1, f_f = 0.6, f_r = 1.4

10_1016_j_finel_2009_03_003.key_1:
- Continuum-based (CB) beam element for explicit finite element analysis of long thin structures
- Material properties for tension/compression tests: Young's modulus 1000 MPa, Poisson's ratio 0.3, density 2700 kg/m³
- Material properties for cantilever beam: Young's modulus 71000 MPa, Poisson's ratio 0.34, density 2700 kg/m³
- Concrete block material: Young's modulus 14 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.1, yield stress 30.5 MPa (tension)/2.75 MPa (compression), density 2400 kg/m³, friction angle 20°, dilatancy angle 20°
- Reinforcing bar material: Young's modulus 180 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.33, yield stress 300 MPa, density 7860 kg/m³
- Tension/compression test geometry: 2m × 1m × 0.1m structural bar
- Cantilever beam geometry: 1m × 0.1m × 0.1m
- Pullout specimen: concrete block meshed with 250 quadrilateral elements with steel reinforcing bar of 8 CB elements
- CB element structure: master nodes at intersection of lines connecting slave nodes and reference line; slave nodes define the continuum element
- Tension test used 2 CB elements; compression test used 8 CB elements; cantilever beam used 8 CB elements
- Applied loads: 2kN for tension/compression tests; 20kN and 200kN for cantilever beam tests; 100kN for pullout test
- CB element thickness is variable, allowing dilation/contraction during large deformation processes
- Cantilever beam deflection under 20kN load shows analytical solution agreement with Timoshenko elements
- Cantilever beam deflection under 200kN load shows analytical solution agreement with Timoshenko elements
- Pullout test models steel reinforcement bar surrounded by concrete block with perfect bond assumption
10_1016_j_finel_2009_03_003.key_2:
- Tension test: external force of 2kN distributed between two slave nodes at extreme edge
- Compression test: compressive force of 2kN applied at extreme edge
- Cantilever beam: lateral tip load of 20kN (first case) and 200kN (second case) applied at extreme edge
- Pullout test: 100kN loading applied to steel reinforcing bar
- Boundary nodes of concrete block in pullout test fully fixed (indicated by shaded area)
- Perfect bond assumed between steel and concrete components in pullout test
- Displacements in steel bar match surrounding concrete block in pullout test
- Selective-reduced integration with five quadrature points through thickness for 20kN cantilever test
- Normal integration with nine quadrature points uniformly distributed for 200kN cantilever test
- Rayleigh damping technique used with damping matrix proportional to diagonalized mass matrix
- Alternative damping combining stiffness and mass proportionality implemented for problematic cases
- Explicit dynamic analysis framework used throughout
- Adaptive time stepping scheme employed to overcome stability limitations
- 2D plane stress/strain analysis as evidenced by displacement components in x and y directions
- Nonlinear analysis accounting for large deformations and rotations
- Dynamic relaxation strategy used to obtain static solution through attenuation of transient response
10_1016_j_finel_2009_03_003.key_3:
- Large deformation beam mechanics including tension, compression, and bending behavior
- Displacement fields in x and y directions for beam structures
- Internal force evolution over time for tension, compression, and bending cases
- Deflection profiles along beam length compared to analytical solutions and Timoshenko elements
- Axial stress calculations (20 kPa for tension test, -20 kPa for compression test)
- Elongation measurements (4×10⁻⁶ m for tension, -4×10⁻⁶ m for compression)
- Internal force-time histories for cantilever beam under 20kN and 200kN loads
- Vertical and horizontal displacement-time histories for cantilever beam tests
- Verification of CB element accuracy against analytical solutions and Timoshenko beam elements
- Computational performance metrics showing improved CPU-time and convergence
- Demonstration of variable element thickness capability for dilation/contraction during large deformations
- Validation of CB element suitability for subcycling algorithms in embedded structures
10_1016_j_finel_2009_03_003.key_4:
- CB element must maintain master-slave node relationship with slave nodes defining continuum element
- Shear locking must be prevented through selective-reduced integration technique
- Critical time step limitations in explicit schemes require adaptive time stepping implementation
- Poor conditioning of semidiscretised system of equations for continuum elements limits stability/accuracy
- Classical beam elements in explicit simulations suffer from severely restricted critical time step
- Concrete yield stress constrained to 30.5 MPa (tension) and 2.75 MPa (compression)
- Steel reinforcing bar yield stress constrained to 300 MPa
- Mohr-Coulomb concrete model requires friction angle (20°) and dilatancy angle (20°) parameters
- CB element thickness hκ must remain variable to allow dilation/contraction during large deformations
- Selective-reduced integration with specific quadrature points required (5 points for 20kN cantilever, 9 points for 200kN cantilever)
- Rayleigh damping technique must maintain damping matrix proportional to diagonalized mass matrix
- Dynamic relaxation strategy required to obtain static solution through transient response attenuation
- Perfect bond assumption required between steel and concrete components in pullout test
- CB element must be based on rectangular continuum element for formulation
- Explicit central difference scheme requires specific time derivative approximations (stencils for velocity and acceleration)

10_1016_j_microrel_2024_115345.key_1:
- Microwave RF coaxial connector solder joints (SMA-KFD5742 model)
- Solder material: Eutectic SnPb
- Inner conductor: Beryllium bronze with 2μm nickel plating
- Pad/microstrip material: Copper (Cu)
- Dielectric material: PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene)
- Shell material: Aluminum (Al)
- Inner conductor diameter: Φ 1.3 mm
- Two structural parameters: lap length (L) and lap height (H)
- Initial parameters: L = 2.6 mm, H = 0.15 mm
- Optimal parameters: L = 3.9 mm, H = 0.2 mm
- Solder joint models: Model 1 (solder below cylinder axis), Model 2 (solder above cylinder axis), Model 3 (solder fully enveloping cylinder)
- Thermal cycling conditions: -55°C to 125°C, cycle time = 3000 s, 8 cycles
- High-temperature storage tests at 150°C for 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49 days
- Solder volume range tested: 0.8-3.0 mm³
- Intermetallic compounds: Cu₆Sn₅ and Cu₃Sn at solder-pad interface, (Cu,Ni)₆Sn₅ at solder-cylinder interface
- IMC thickness growth formulas: h_Cu₆Sn₅ = 0.93t⁰·⁵ + 0.529, h_Cu₃Sn = 0.309t⁰·⁵, h_(Cu,Ni)₆Sn₅ = 0.40t⁰·⁵ + 0.08 (h in μm, t in days)
- Maximum stress reduction after optimization: 44%
- Average stress reduction after optimization: 55%
- Predicted solder joint life: 2.1 × 10⁵ cycles
- No microcracks observed after 1000 thermal cycles with optimized design
- Stress concentration location: Contact region between solder heel and lowest edge of inner conductor
- Optimal solder morphology: Partially enveloped shape with solder wetted above inner conductor axis
- Optimal solder volume: 1.5 mm³
- Element diffusion follows Fick's law with quadratic relationship to time
- Kirkendall voids diameter range: 200-450 nm in Cu₃Sn layer
- Element diffusion activation energy used for IMC thickness prediction at various temperatures
10_1016_j_microrel_2024_115345.key_2:

- Fixed constraint at center of symmetry node
- Thermal cycling load: -55°C to 125°C temperature range (IPC9701 TC4)
- Thermal cycling profile: 50-minute cycle time with 10-minute dwell time
- 8 thermal cycles applied to model (5-7 cycles to reach stable inelastic strain state)
- High-temperature storage test at constant 150°C for 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, and 49 days
- Lap height (H) parameter values: 0.0, 0.1, and 0.2 mm
- Lap length (L) parameter values: 1.3, 2.6, and 3.9 mm
- Element density maintained at approximately 25,000 mm⁻³ for solder joint mesh
- All bonded interfaces assumed to be tightly integrated
- Thermal-mechanical indirect coupling analysis
- 3D simulation using tetrahedral meshing
- CTE mismatch between pad-solder-inner conductor materials
- Plastic strain difference (Δε) stabilized at 0.0019 per cycle
- Zero potential energy surface defined for gravitational potential energy calculations
- Solder volume constraints: 0.8, 1.1, 1.5, and 3.0 mm³ for different morphology models
- Material properties varied with temperature
- Homogeneous and dense material assumption for all components
10_1016_j_microrel_2024_115345.key_3:
- Thermal-mechanical stress and strain distribution under thermal cycling
- Intermetallic compound (IMC) growth kinetics at solder interfaces

- Maximum stress in solder joint (MPa)
- Average stress in solder joint (MPa)

- Minimize average stress (achieved: 55% reduction)

- Optimize lap length (L) and lap height (H) parameters

10_1016_j_microrel_2024_115345.key_4:
- Lap length (L) constrained to values: 1.3 mm, 2.6 mm, and 3.9 mm (with 3.9 mm as optimal)
- Lap height (H) constrained to values: 0.0 mm, 0.1 mm, and 0.2 mm (with 0.2 mm as optimal)
- Inner conductor diameter fixed at Φ 1.3 mm

10_1016_j_cryogenics_2024_103836.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Central Solenoid (CS) Cable In Conduit Conductor (CICC) jacket for compact fusion device
- **Material / Medium:** N50H austenitic steel with chemical composition (wt.%): C:0.009, Si:0.3, Mn:5.28, P:0.005, S:0.002, Cr:22.2, Ni:14.6, Mo:2.1, V:0.19, Nb:0.09, N:0.31, O:0.0018; Yield Strength >1500 MPa @4.2 K; Room temperature properties: 509 MPa yield strength, 845 MPa tensile strength, 195 GPa Young's modulus; Cryogenic properties: 205 GPa Young's modulus, 78.8 GPa shear modulus, 0.3 Poisson ratio, 0.29% thermal expansivity
- **Application & Importance:** Withstands electromagnetic force up to 20 T magnetic field in CS magnet; Prevents stress concentration that could cause weld failure; Critical for safe operation and long-term stability of fusion magnets
- **Geometry / Domain:** Circle-in-square structure; Before compression: 43.0 mm width, Φ34.0 mm inner diameter, R5 corner radius; After compression: 41.0 mm width, Φ32.0 mm inner diameter, R3 corner radius; Corner radius range analyzed: 5-10 mm (7.5 mm selected as optimal); Tensile specimen dimensions: 55 mm length, 2.5 mm thickness, 14 mm side sections, 16 mm central section, R5.5 curve with 3±0.1 mm height
10_1016_j_cryogenics_2024_103836.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Room temperature preload to prevent magnet loosening after cooling; Strain rate below 5 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ for tensile tests; 10% strain range clip-on extensometer for strain measurement; Corner radius range 5-10 mm; Tensile specimens cut along longitudinal axis of jacket; Tensile specimen dimensions: 55 mm length, 2.5 mm thickness
- **Loads / Excitations:** 20 T maximum magnetic field; 45 kA magnet energization current; Thermal stress during cool-down from room temperature to 4.2 K; Electromagnetic stress at maximum field; Preload at room temperature; Compressing process loads
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Fine structure model containing each turn of conductor; Interface between cable, jacket, and inter-module spacer; Contact between jacket sections A and B; Insulation interfaces: turn insulation, layer insulation, ground insulation, pancake insulation, fillet; N50H parameters at 4.2 K: 205 GPa Young's modulus, 78.8 GPa shear modulus, 0.3 Poisson ratio, 0.29% thermal expansivity
- **Simulation Type:** Finite element method for conductor compressing process; 3D mechanical magnet model; Stress intensity analysis; Equivalent (von-Mises) stress analysis
10_1016_j_cryogenics_2024_103836.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Mechanical stress distribution in CS CICC jacket during manufacturing (compressing process) and operation; Stress concentration analysis; Interaction between compressing stress and electromagnetic stress
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Compressing stress (760-920 MPa range); Electromagnetic stress (1055-1095 MPa range); Equivalent (von-Mises) stress; Stress intensity; Yield Strength at 4.2 K; Ultimate Tensile Strength; Elongation; Corner radius effect on stress distribution (5-10 mm range)
- **Optimization Goal:** Balance between minimizing compressing stress (decreases with larger corner radius) and minimizing electromagnetic stress (increases with larger corner radius); Select optimal corner radius (determined as 7.5 mm) to alleviate stress concentration while maintaining sufficient electromagnetic force resistance; Achieve N50H jacket with Yield Strength >1500 MPa @ 4.2 K
10_1016_j_cryogenics_2024_103836.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Circle-in-square jacket structure; Width range: 41.0-43.0 mm; Inner diameter range: Φ32.0-Φ34.0 mm; Corner radius range: 5-10 mm (7.5 mm selected as optimal); 2 mm gap reserved between inner diameter and cable for cable passage; Wall thickness decreases by 18.3% when corner radius increases from 5 mm to 10 mm; Cross-sectional area decreases by 7% when corner radius increases from 5 mm to 10 mm
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Must withstand 20 T magnetic field; Must achieve Yield Strength >1500 MPa @ 4.2 K; Electromagnetic stress must remain below material limits (max 1091 MPa at 10 mm radius); Compressing stress must be minimized (760-920 MPa range); Stress concentration at corners must be managed; Aged jacket must maintain YS p0.2 and UTS with <5% degeneration; Aged welds must maintain YS p0.2 and UTS with <5% degeneration; Must withstand thermal stress during cool-down from room temperature to 4.2 K
- **Process/Manufacturing:** Conductor manufacturing requires compressing, bending, and straightening processes; Four-roller compression process deforms jacket; Tensile test strain rate must be <5×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; One jacket cut into two parts (A and B) for comparative testing (one compressed, one not); Tensile specimens must be 55 mm length × 2.5 mm thickness; Welds identified as weak spots sensitive to stress concentration; Preload must be applied at room temperature to prevent magnet loosening after cooling; Must accommodate Nb3Sn coil heat-treatment requirements

10_1088_1757_899x_469_1_012011.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Surface crack growth in aluminum alloys under fatigue loading; S-version Finite Element Model (S-FEM) for four-point bending and three-point bending scenarios
- **Material / Medium:** Aluminum alloy A7075-T6 (aircraft parts); Aluminum alloy A2017-T3 (aircraft components, screw machine products)
- **Material Properties (A7075-T6):** Critical stress intensity factor KIC = 29 MPa·√m; Fatigue power parameter n = 2.88; Yield strength = 691 MPa; Young's modulus E = 71.7 GPa; Paris coefficient C = 6.54×10⁻¹³; Threshold value ΔKth = 5.66 MPa·√m; Maximum crack growth increment damax = 1.3 mm; Initial crack length c = 4.5 mm; Initial crack depth a = 3.5 mm
- **Material Properties (A2017-T3):** Critical stress intensity factor KIC = 26 MPa·√m; Fatigue power parameter n = 2.93; Yield strength = 333 MPa; Young's modulus E = 70.2 GPa; Paris coefficient C = 2.66×10⁻¹⁰; Threshold value ΔKth = 6.7 MPa·√m; Initial crack length c = 2.85 mm; Initial crack depth a = 5.00 mm
- **Geometry (Four-point bending):** Dimensions 2b = 65 mm, 2h = 160 mm, t = 25 mm; Initial crack aspect a = 3.5 mm and 2c = 4.5 mm; Loading = 45 kN; Stress ratio = 0.1
- **Geometry (Three-point bending):** Dimensions 2h = 150 mm, 2b = 50 mm, t = 15 mm; Initial crack aspect a = 5 mm and 2c = 2.85 mm; Loading = 9 kN; Stress ratio = 0.1
- **Crack Geometry:** Semi-elliptical crack shape maintained during propagation; Local area (Ωᴸ) for crack tip meshing; Global area (Ωᴳ) for whole model meshing
- **Analysis Purpose:** Fatigue crack growth prediction to prevent catastrophic failure; Validation of S-FEM against experimental results; Simulation of three fatigue stages (crack initiation, fatigue crack propagation, fatigue failure propagation)
10_1088_1757_899x_469_1_012011.key_2:
- **Boundary Conditions:** Constraint displacement (Γᵘ) at bottom support; Force boundary (Γᵗ) at loading points; Overlay boundary (Γᴳᴸ) between local and global meshes; Stress ratio = 0.1 for both bending models
- **Loads:** Four-point bending: 45 kN cyclic load; Three-point bending: 9 kN cyclic load
- **Mesh Configuration:** Global area (Ωᴳ) with coarser mesh for entire model; Local area (Ωᴸ) with finer mesh for crack tip region; Local mesh enveloped onto global mesh
- **Displacement Relationship:** u(x) = uᴳ(x) for x ∈ Ωᴳ - Ωᴸ; u(x) = uᴳ(x) + uᴸ(x) for x ∈ Ωᴸ
- **Strain Relationship:** ε(x) = εᴳ(x) + εᴸ(x) in overlaid area
- **Crack Propagation Criteria:** Paris' Law (da/dN = C(ΔK)ⁿ); Energy release rate calculated via Virtual Crack Closure Method (VCCM)
- **Simulation Type:** 3D S-version Finite Element Method (S-FEM); Transient fatigue analysis; Linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM); Three-stage fatigue modeling (crack initiation, propagation, failure)
10_1088_1757_899x_469_1_012011.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Surface crack growth under cyclic fatigue loading; Linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM); Stress intensity factor (SIF) calculation; Energy release rate determination; Three-dimensional crack propagation behavior
- **Target Outputs:** Fatigue life (cycles to failure); Crack length vs. cycles (N); Crack depth vs. crack length; Beach mark patterns; Equivalent stress intensity factor (ΔK_eq); Crack growth rate (da/dN); Crack propagation angle; Stress intensity factors (K_I, K_II, K_III)
- **Simulation Goal:** Accurate prediction of surface fatigue crack growth behavior; Validation of S-FEM results against experimental data; Simulation of three fatigue stages (crack initiation, fatigue crack propagation, fatigue failure propagation); Characterization of arbitrary crack shapes using meshing techniques
10_1088_1757_899x_469_1_012011.key_4:
- **Geometric Constraints:** Four-point bending model dimensions: 2b = 65 mm, 2h = 160 mm, t = 25 mm; Three-point bending model dimensions: 2h = 150 mm, 2b = 50 mm, t = 15 mm; Initial crack dimensions for A7075-T6: a = 3.5 mm, 2c = 4.5 mm; Initial crack dimensions for A2017-T3: a = 5 mm, 2c = 2.85 mm; Maximum crack growth increment for A7075-T6: damax = 1.3 mm
- **Physics Constraints:** Stress ratio = 0.1 for both bending models; Critical stress intensity factor KIC = 29 MPa·√m (A7075-T6); Critical stress intensity factor KIC = 26 MPa·√m (A2017-T3); Threshold value ΔKth = 5.66 MPa·√m (A7075-T6); Threshold value ΔKth = 6.7 MPa·√m (A2017-T3); Loading constraints: 45 kN for four-point bending, 9 kN for three-point bending
- **Process Constraints:** SIF calculation difficulty at 3D crack front nodes; Meshing distortion noted in four-point bending S-FEM model; Three-stage fatigue process constraint (crack initiation, fatigue crack propagation, fatigue failure propagation); Beach mark generation requires stress ratio of 0.1; Paris' Law implementation with material-specific C and n parameters (C = 6.54×10⁻¹³, n = 2.88 for A7075-T6; C = 2.66×10⁻¹⁰, n = 2.93 for A2017-T3)

10_1108_ec_09_2015_0268.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Ten-noded composite tetrahedral (COMPTet) finite element for combined finite-discrete element method (FDEM); validation cases include 1 m cube models, infinite plate with circular hole, and notched cylindrical samples; analysis focuses on volumetric locking problems in constant strain tetrahedral (CSTet) elements
- **Material / Medium:** Acrylic with E=3.3 GPa, ν=0.38, ρ=1,200 kg/m³; materials with Poisson's ratios ν=0.0, ν=0.25, ν=0.499, ν=0.4999; Young's modulus values E=1.0e9 Pa, E=30 MPa; 1 m cube models
- **Application & Importance:** Designed to eliminate volumetric locking in constant strain tetrahedral elements; intended for dynamic fracture propagation simulations and hydrofracture experiments; validated through comparison with analytical solutions and experimental results from acrylic fracturing experiments
- **Geometry / Domain:** 1 m cube loaded with compressive load (p=1,000 Pa) on four surfaces; 1 m cube with concentrated load at point A (f=[1.0e6, 1.0e6, 1.0e6] N); infinite plate with circular hole (a=0.1 m) under plane strain; notched cylindrical samples with Model 1 (D=H=25.4 mm, R=5.0 mm, d=3.81 mm, δ=0.15 mm) and Model 2 (D=H=25.4 mm, R=11.0 mm, d=9.4 mm, δ=0.17 mm); ten-noded COMPTet composed of eight four-noded sub-tetrahedrons; x-y plane analysis domain size L=1.0, m=10a for infinite plate case
10_1108_ec_09_2015_0268.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Fixed back, left and bottom faces for the 1 m cube with concentrated load; analytical displacements from Equation (29) applied to remote sides of infinite plate domain; nodes on sides constrained to x-z plane movement; nodes on top/bottom constrained to x-y plane movement; symmetry condition allowing simulation of only one quadrant; compressive load applied to four surfaces of 1 m cube; analytical displacements applied to remote boundaries for infinite plate with circular hole
- **Loads / Excitations:** Compressive pressure p=1,000 Pa on four surfaces of 1 m cube; concentrated force f=[1.0e6, 1.0e6, 1.0e6] N at point A; tensile stresses at ends of infinite plate; quadratic displacement field with kx=1e-6 (x̃=x+kx·x², ỹ=y, z̃=z); three stress fields for notched samples: axial confining stress (p1), lateral confining stress (p2), and notch opening stress (p3)
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Ten-noded COMPTet element composed of eight four-noded sub-tetrahedrons; generalized material element at center of each sub-tetrahedron; multiplicative decomposition approach separating deformation into translation, rotation, plastic stretches, elastic stretches, volumetric stretches, and shear stretches
- **Simulation Type:** Static solution with proper damping included; 3D analysis; convergence studies with decreasing element size; comparison between COMPTet and CSTet elements; linear and quadratic convergence observed depending on case; near-incompressible conditions tested with ν=0.4999; elastic material behavior assumed for validation cases
10_1108_ec_09_2015_0268.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Elastic deformation in nearly incompressible materials; volumetric locking behavior; stress distribution under compressive loads; displacement fields in cubic and notched cylindrical geometries; fracture initiation mechanics in hydrofracture experiments
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Relative error in displacement (e_Δ); relative error in stress (e_σ); Cauchy stress components (σ_xx, σ_yy); pressure (p); displacement distribution; volumetric stretches; linear and angular stretches; convergence rates with element size; stress values at notch bottom (σ_Axx, σ_Ayy)
- **Optimization Goal:** Eliminate volumetric locking in constant strain tetrahedral elements; achieve smooth stress distribution without checkerboard patterns; provide accurate stress state estimation at notch bottom for hydraulic fracture initiation; maintain linear convergence for stress with element size reduction; achieve quadratic convergence for displacement with element size reduction; enable accurate modeling of near-incompressible materials (ν=0.4999)
10_1108_ec_09_2015_0268.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Analysis domain for infinite plate with circular hole limited to size L=1.0, m=10a; only one quadrant simulated due to symmetry; notched cylindrical samples with Model 1 dimensions (D=H=25.4 mm, R=5.0 mm, d=3.81 mm, δ=0.15 mm) and Model 2 dimensions (D=H=25.4 mm, R=11.0 mm, d=9.4 mm, δ=0.17 mm); 1 m cube models with dimensions 1m × 1m × 1m; mesh size constraints for Models 1 and 2: L1 (0.3r), L2 (0.2r), L3 (0.15r) where r=δ/2; nodes on plate sides constrained to x-z plane movement; nodes on plate top/bottom constrained to x-y plane movement

- Aluminum alloy 2XXX (6 mm, 8 mm, 12 mm thicknesses) with E=74.7 GPa, ν=0.3, A=352 MPa, B=440 MPa, n=0.42

- C3D8R finite elements with 0.5 mm mesh size in impacted area

10_1016_j_compstruct_2024_118073.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Unidirectional fibre reinforced composites (UD FRP) with focus on transverse modulus (E₂₂) prediction under humid conditions
- **Material / Medium:** Glass fibre/epoxy composites with three-phase structure (fibre, matrix, interphase); fibre volume fractions from 10-60%; interphase thickness 0-1000 nm; constituent elastic moduli: Eₘ [1.2-5.07 GPa], Eբ [12.97-73 GPa], Eᵢ [1.1-2.7 GPa]; Poisson's ratios: νₘ [0.3-0.4], νբ [0.22-0.35], νᵢ [0.35-0.4]
- **Application & Importance:** Predict long-term transverse performance degradation under humid environmental conditions (relative humidity 80-100%, temperature 25-70°C, duration 3-76 weeks); address moisture-induced property degradation including reduced shear strength, flexural strength, and stiffness
- **Geometry / Domain:** 2D periodic representative volume elements (RVEs) with randomly distributed circular fibres; fibre diameter mean 13.2 μm (std 0.8 μm); RVE length to fibre diameter ratio (L_RVE/D_fibre) ≥ 10 for convergence; CPE4 element mesh size 1.5×1.5 μm²; periodic boundary conditions applied to RVE edges
10_1016_j_compstruct_2024_118073.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Periodic boundary conditions applied to opposing edges of RVE; Node N₁ fixed along x- and y-axis; Node N₂ constrained along x-axis; Node N₄ subjected to positive displacement δₓ; Homogenous and linear material behavior with isotropic mechanical properties; Plain strain condition; Mesh size 1.5×1.5 μm² using CPE4 elements
- **Loads / Excitations:** Uniaxial tensile loading parallel to x-axis; Relative humidity (RH) 80-100%; Temperature 25-70°C; Exposure duration 3-76 weeks; Fibre volume fraction 10-60%; Interphase thickness 0-1000 nm
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Perfectly tied interface between fibre and matrix; Interphase region between fibre and matrix; Stress concentration at regions where fibres are close together
- **Simulation Type:** 2D finite element analysis; Linear static analysis; Plain strain formulation; Periodic representative volume element (RVE) with L_RVE/D_fibre ≥ 10 for convergence; CPE4 element meshing
10_1016_j_compstruct_2024_118073.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Transverse mechanical behavior of unidirectional fibre reinforced composites; Micromechanical interactions between fibre, matrix, and interphase regions under humid environmental conditions; Stress distribution and concentration effects in composite microstructures; Moisture-induced degradation of mechanical properties
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Transverse elastic modulus (E₂₂) as primary output; Root-mean-square error (RMSE); Goodness of fit (R²); Mean squared error (MSE); von Mises stress distributions; Stress concentration patterns; Prediction accuracy within ±10% for optimal model; Cumulative variance captured by principal components
- **Optimization Goal:** Minimize prediction error of transverse modulus (E₂₂) using Bayesian optimization with 10-fold cross-validation; Achieve maximum prediction accuracy with RMSE ≤ 0.054 and R² ≥ 0.999; Establish efficient structure-property linkage between microstructural features and mechanical performance under humid conditions; Optimize ANN architecture to minimize cost function while maximizing generalization capability across different dataset sizes
10_1016_j_compstruct_2024_118073.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Jamming limit of RSA algorithm restricts fibre volume fractions to ≤ 55%; RVE length to fibre diameter ratio (L_RVE/D_fibre) must be ≥ 10 for consistent results; Fibre volume fraction range limited to 10-60%; Interphase thickness constrained to 0-1000 nm; Fibre diameter mean 13.2 μm (standard deviation 0.8 μm); RVEs generated with 570×570 pixel resolution images
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Glass fibre composite ultimate stress in transverse direction is 30-40 MPa (exceeded in modeling); Interphase region assumed to be softer than matrix; Perfect interface tie between fibre and matrix assumed (no damage initiation criteria considered); Homogeneous, linear, isotropic material behavior with plain strain conditions applied; No consideration of interface failure or fibre-matrix debonding; Matrix bulk and shear moduli constrained by constituent properties
- **Process/Manufacturing:** Random sequential adsorption (RSA) algorithm used for fibre placement with overlap prevention (d_i ≥ φ[2(R+e)] where φ > 1); Periodic boundary conditions required to avoid edge effects; CPE4 elements with 1.5×1.5 μm² mesh size used for FE simulation; Three-phase structure (fibre, matrix, interphase) must be maintained; Python script used for RVE generation integrated with Abaqus CAE; Two-point correlation functions applied to 570×570 pixel microstructure images; Dimensionality reduction to 20 principal components from 649,800 TPC values

10_1016_s0045_7825_02_00524_8.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Stationary heat conduction problem with discontinuous conduction coefficient across smooth internal interface; elliptic interface problem in two dimensions
- **Material / Medium:** Conduction coefficient α constant in each subdomain with α₁ > 0 and α₂ > 0; Example 1: α₁ = 1/2, α₂ = 3; Example 2: α₁ = 1, α₂ = 1000; Example 3: α_min = 1 inside ellipsoidal inclusion, α_max = 6 outside
- **Application & Importance:** Avoids costly repeated remeshing when interface moves in time-dependent or non-linear problems; enables optimal convergence without requiring mesh alignment with interface; prevents suboptimal convergence behavior seen in standard unfitted methods
- **Geometry / Domain:** Bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ² with convex polygonal boundary ∂Ω; smooth internal boundary Γ dividing Ω into Ω₁ and Ω₂; domain discretized with non-degenerate triangulations independent of interface location; Example 1: 2D domain (0,1)×(0,1) with interface at x=1/2; Example 2: Domain (0,1)×(0,1) with circular interface; Example 3: Domain (0,1)×(0,1) with ellipsoidal inclusion
10_1016_s0045_7825_02_00524_8.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Dirichlet boundary condition u=0 on ∂Ω; Zero Neumann boundary conditions at y=0 and y=1 (Example 1); Symmetry boundaries at x=0 and y=0 (Example 2); Dirichlet boundary conditions corresponding to exact solution at x=1 and y=1 (Example 2); Zero Dirichlet boundary conditions (Example 3)
- **Loads / Excitations:** Body force f∈L²(Ω) with f=-4 (Example 2); Interface conormal derivative condition [α∇ₙu]=g on Γ; For Example 1: g=α₁u₁'(1/2)=α₂u₂'(1/2); Right-hand side f in equation −∇·(α∇u)=f in Ω₁∪Ω₂
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Continuity condition [u]=0 on Γ; Discontinuity in conduction coefficient α across interface Γ; Interface Γ divides domain Ω into Ω₁ and Ω₂; Interface condition [α∇ₙu]=g on Γ; Method allows discontinuities internal to elements across interface
- **Simulation Type:** Steady-state; Two-dimensional; Elliptic interface problems; Unfitted finite element method with non-degenerate triangulations; Linear problems with discontinuous coefficients; Examples solved using piecewise linear finite elements on conforming triangulations independent of interface location
10_1016_s0045_7825_02_00524_8.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Stationary heat conduction with discontinuous conduction coefficient across internal interface; Solution of elliptic interface problems governed by −∇·(α∇u)=f in Ω₁∪Ω₂; Unfitted finite element approximation of functions with discontinuous gradients across interface
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** L² error norm; Maximum norm error; A posteriori error estimators E_K(U) and E(U); Element-wise error contributions including h_K²∥f+∇·(α∇U)∥₀,K¹∪K²², h_K∥[α_i∇U_i]∥₀,K², h_K∥g−[α∇U]∥₀,Γ_K², and h_K⁻¹∥[U]∥₀,Γ_K²; Convergence rates (specifically second order in L²)
- **Optimization Goal:** Achieve optimal order of convergence without mesh-interface alignment constraints; Avoid suboptimal convergence behavior of standard unfitted methods; Control functionals of the error through adaptive mesh refinement; Refine one-third of elements with highest error contribution in each iteration; Maintain second order L² convergence with unfitted meshes independent of interface location
10_1016_s0045_7825_02_00524_8.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Triangulation must be non-degenerate (h_K/ρ_K ≤ C ∀K∈T_h); Interface Γ intersects each element boundary ∂K exactly twice and each open edge at most once; Interface must be smooth with bounded curvature; Domain Ω must be bounded with convex polygonal boundary ∂Ω; For intersected elements, Γ_K must be a function of length on Γ_K,h (straight line segment connecting intersection points)
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Conduction coefficient α constant in each subdomain with α_i > 0; f∈L²(Ω) and g∈H^(1/2)(Γ) required for problem well-posedness; Parameter λ must be sufficiently large in the bilinear form; A priori estimate constraint: ∥u∥₁,Ω + ∥u∥₂,Ω₁∪Ω₂ ≤ C(∥f∥₀,Ω + ∥g∥₁/₂,Γ); Current implementation limited to piecewise linear approximations in two dimensions
- **Process/Manufacturing:** Implementation requires splitting each standard basis function on interface-intersected elements into two new basis functions; Numerical integration uses centroid quadrature on intersected elements and two-point Gaussian quadrature on interface; Adaptive refinement limited to refining one-third of elements with highest error contribution per iteration; Current method does not have theoretical backing for maximum norm convergence rates despite observed second-order behavior

10_1016_j_jpowsour_2015_04_065.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Three-electrode cell for impedance measurements in lithium-ion rechargeable batteries (LIRBs)
- **Material / Medium:** Positive electrode: LiCoO₂ active material with Al current collector; Negative electrode: spherical graphite active material with Cu current collector; Electrolyte: ethylene carbonate/ethyl methyl carbonate (3:7 v/v) with 1 M LiPF₆; Specific resistance values: 12.5 Ω m and 125 Ω m; Electric conductivities: 1.1 mS cm⁻¹ (positive), 30 S cm⁻¹ (negative); Relative permittivities: 19 (positive), 1 (negative)
- **Application & Importance:** Determining proper reference electrode placement to prevent impedance spectrum distortion and artifact inductive loops; enabling accurate separation of positive and negative electrode time constants; avoiding reference electrode dissolution during measurements
- **Geometry / Domain:** Symmetrical face-to-face disk electrodes (5 mm radius, 25 μm thickness); 25 μm electrolyte thickness (100 μm with reference electrode); Reference electrode dimensions: 1 mm width, 25 μm thickness; FEM simulation domain includes calculation points at r = 0 mm, r = 5 mm, and r = 6 mm; Reference electrode positions tested: center (r = 0 mm), edge (r = 5 mm), and outside (r = 6 mm)
10_1016_j_jpowsour_2015_04_065.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Direct potentials of positive and negative electrodes set at 0 V; 2D axisymmetric model representing half of LIRB cell; Electrode radius = 5 mm; Electrode thickness = 25 μm; Electrolyte solution radius = 8 mm; Electrolyte thickness = 25 μm (100 μm with reference electrode); Calculation points at r = 0 mm, r = 5 mm, and r = 6 mm; Magnetic field-induced current neglected; Potential distributed homogeneously in electrolyte solution (Laplace's equation ∇²V = 0)
- **Loads / Excitations:** Alternating potential of 10 mV applied to positive electrode; Frequency range from 1 mHz to 100 kHz (5 frequencies per decade); Charge-transfer resistance: Rct,P = 10 Ω, Rct,N = 5 Ω; Double-layer capacitance: Cdl,P = 10 mF, Cdl,N = 0.5 mF; Double-layer thickness d = 1 nm; Specific resistance values: ρ = 12.5 Ω m and ρ = 125 Ω m
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Boundary layer assigned to electrode/solution interface; Impedance calculated as ZP = (VP - VR)/ITotal and ZN = (VR - VN)/ITotal; Electric conductivity: σP = 1.1 mS cm⁻¹, σN = 30 S cm⁻¹, σRE = 11 MS m⁻¹; Relative permittivity: εr,P = 19, εr,N = 1, εr,RE = 1
- **Simulation Type:** Finite element method (COMSOL Multiphysics); 2D axisymmetric model; Frequency domain analysis; AC impedance analysis
10_1016_j_jpowsour_2015_04_065.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Current distribution and potential distribution in three-electrode lithium-ion battery cell; Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy behavior; Frequency-dependent AC response in electrolyte and electrode interfaces
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Impedance spectra of positive and negative electrodes; Artifact inductive loop diameter; Loop distortion in impedance spectra; Time constants (τp,inductive, τp,loop, τn,loop, τn,inductive); Current density distributions; Potential gradient across electrode interfaces
- **Optimization Goal:** Minimize distortion of impedance spectra and artifact inductive loops; Position reference electrode outside the area between positive and negative electrodes to prevent current flow through reference electrode and eliminate potential modulation at reference electrode location
10_1016_j_jpowsour_2015_04_065.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Electrode radius fixed at 5 mm; Electrode thickness fixed at 25 μm; Electrolyte solution radius fixed at 8 mm; Electrolyte thickness fixed at 25 μm (100 μm with reference electrode); Reference electrode width fixed at 1 mm, thickness fixed at 25 μm; Calculation points constrained to radial positions r = 0 mm, r = 5 mm, and r = 6 mm; Reference electrode constrained to three positions: center (r = 0 mm), edge (r = 5 mm), and outside (r = 6 mm); 2D axisymmetric model representing half of the cell
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Direct potentials of positive and negative electrodes constrained to 0 V; Alternating potential amplitude constrained to 10 mV; Frequency range constrained from 1 mHz to 100 kHz; Specific resistance values constrained to ρ = 12.5 Ω m and ρ = 125 Ω m; Charge-transfer resistance constrained to Rct,P = 10 Ω and Rct,N = 5 Ω; Double-layer capacitance constrained to Cdl,P = 10 mF and Cdl,N = 0.5 mF; Double-layer thickness constrained to d = 1 nm; Reference electrode must be placed where there is no potential modulation and gradient; Reference electrode must be positioned outside the area between positive and negative electrodes to prevent current flow through it
- **Process/Manufacturing:** Electrolyte solution constrained to ethylene carbonate/ethyl methyl carbonate (3:7 v/v) with 1 M LiPF₆; Reference electrode constrained to lithium metal or similar material; Simulation constrained to use FEM (COMSOL Multiphysics); 5 frequencies per decade used in frequency domain analysis; Commercial electrode sheets used (LiCoO₂/Al positive, graphite/Cu negative)

- **Loads / Excitations:** Time-dependent heat fluxes modeling guide friction; time-dependent external temperatures and heat transfer coefficients for environmental convection; heat fluxes at table center and tool tip modeling process heat
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** 15 moving contacts between sledges; fluid-structure interfaces; nonlinear Hertzian deformation behavior at contact partners; surrogate models for rolling parts; face-face contact thermal coupling; MPC184 bushing elements for elastic contact
- **Simulation Type:** Transient thermoelastic simulation (10,000 s operation time); quasi-static deformation field calculation; sequential integration of thermal (Eq. 6a) and elastic (Eq. 6b) domains; 3D model with 700k elements and 1.4 million nodes; Model Order Reduction (MOR) applied to reduce computational cost
10_1007_978_3_031_34486_2_11.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Thermoelastic behavior of machine tools with relatively moving parts; temperature field distribution; deformation/displacement field distribution; sequential thermal-elastic coupling (thermal solution followed by elastic solution); moving contact mechanics between linear guides and ball screw drives
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Temperature distribution after 10,000 s operation; deformation field distribution after 10,000 s operation; Tool Center Point (TCP) displacement; system behavior prediction for digital twins
- **Optimization Goal:** Accelerate development process by reducing prototype testing; enable model predictive control of machine tools; increase simulation efficiency through Model Order Reduction while preserving accuracy; facilitate process parallel simulation of production processes; enable online correction of tool center point displacement; allow parameter studies and optimization runs with reduced computational cost
10_1007_978_3_031_34486_2_11.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Fixed table rotation axes (reduced to 3-axes model from original 5-axes capability); 700k elements and 1.4 million nodes in FE discretization; contact zones segmented for moving contacts with accuracy/computational cost trade-off; detailed modeling of linear guide wagons and ball screw drive nut assemblies not feasible due to excessive DOF increase
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** MOR must preserve model accuracy while reducing system degrees of freedom; numerical stability issues with large time steps; nonlinear Hertzian deformation behavior creates computational overhead; finite element couplings slow simulation due to expensive contact searching; large relative movements per time step cause errors; contact searching becomes problematic with large time increments
- **Process/Manufacturing:** 15 moving contacts require specialized modeling approaches; 17 fluid system interfaces modeled as simplified convection boundaries; rolling parts and contact behavior replaced with surrogate models of varying complexity; thermal coupling realized using face-face-contact elements; elastic contact modeled using linear MPC bushings; friction heat in guides modeled by time-dependent heat fluxes; process heat modeled by heat fluxes at table center and tool tip

10_1016_j_finel_2011_01_008.key_1:

10_1016_j_finel_2011_01_008.key_2:

- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Frictionless contact modeled with quadratic node-to-segment elements and C²-continuous surface representation; explicit slave contact area modeling; residual imprint data incorporated into objective function; indenter deformation accounted for by measuring displacement at conical top rather than tip
- **Simulation Type:** Axisymmetric nonlinear transient FEM; elasto-viscoplastic material model with non-linear isotropic and kinematic hardening; multiple mesh refinement levels (highly refined: 41727 specimen/630 indenter elements; coarse: 100/54 elements; fine: 1891 specimen elements); incremental solution procedure with multiplicative decomposition of deformation gradient
10_1016_j_finel_2011_01_008.key_3:

10_1016_j_finel_2011_01_008.key_4:

10_1007_s11265_008_0195_5.key_1:

10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2017_03_002.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Metallic structural components subjected to cyclic loading; specifically specimens with preset pits and fuselage structures with openings for fatigue life prediction
- **Material / Medium:** Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al titanium alloy (E=104,000 MPa, ν=0.3, σ_y=1128 MPa) and 2024-T351 aluminium alloy (E=73,000 MPa, ν=0.3, σ_y=385 MPa); both materials exhibit elastic-plastic behavior with damage evolution under cyclic loading
- **Application & Importance:** Fatigue life prediction of aircraft structural components; critical because "more than sixty per cent of structure failure is caused by cyclic loadings" and fatigue failure is a common engineering concern requiring accurate total life prediction (crack initiation + propagation)
- **Geometry / Domain:** Specimens with preset pit (4mm thickness, 0.25mm pit depth, 3mm pit radius); fuselage structure with oval opening (1400mm×500mm overall, 700mm×500mm opening); smooth specimens with curved gauge section (4mm thickness); all components subjected to uniaxial cyclic loading with stress ratios R=0.02 (specimens) and R=0.06 (fuselage structure)

- **Loads / Excitations:** Maximum nominal stresses of 560MPa, 650MPa, and 800MPa with stress ratio R=0.02 (specimens with preset pit); maximum stress of 115.46MPa with stress ratio R=0.06 (fuselage structure); cycle frequency between 125-128Hz (smooth specimen fatigue experiments); loading frequency of 0.33Hz (fuselage structure); loading error less than 2% of maximum load
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Damage-coupled elastic-plastic constitutive model representing interaction between damage evolution and material behavior; XFEM used for crack propagation without remeshing; experimental setup includes connection to actuating cylinder and fixed end
- **Simulation Type:** 3D analysis with 8-node solid elements (3 degrees of freedom per node); symmetry reduction (quarter-model for specimen with preset pit, half-model for fuselage structure); two-phase simulation (crack initiation life prediction using damage mechanics followed by crack propagation life prediction using XFEM); nonlinear analysis accounting for elastic-plastic damage evolution
10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2017_03_002.key_3:

- **Optimization Goal:** Accurate prediction of total fatigue life (crack initiation + propagation) for metallic components; precise determination of crack initiation location and direction; validation of predicted crack propagation paths against experimental results; achieving predictions within acceptable engineering error bounds (demonstrated by data falling within twice error band in comparison plots)
