10_1016_j_compbiomed_2021_104261.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Human heel biomechanics with offloading support configurations for diabetic foot ulcer prevention/treatment
- **Material / Medium:** 
  - Bones: isotropic linear-elastic (7300 MPa, ν=0.3)
  - Achilles tendon: isotropic linear-elastic (0.173 MPa, ν=0.49)
  - Skin: viscoelastic Neo-Hookean (0.0954 MPa, ν=0.495)
  - Soft tissues: viscoelastic Neo-Hookean (0.306 MPa, ν=0.495)
  - Cartilage: elastic (1.01 MPa, ν=0.4)
  - Foot supports: Ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) compressible Neo-Hookean (10 MPa, ν=0.3)
- **Application & Importance:** Minimize mechanical loads in ulcer-prone regions while reducing stress concentration at wound peripheries to prevent secondary ulceration
- **Geometry / Domain:**
  - 3D anatomically realistic heel model with bones, cartilage, Achilles tendon, soft tissue, and skin
  - Offloading hole parameters: radius (5-30 mm), radius of curvature (2-230 mm), depth (1-15 mm)
  - Two VOIs: High-risk-VOI (cylindrical area ~2 cm² under calcaneus apex) and Peripheral-VOI (surrounding soft tissue)
  - Heel strike position with 10° initial angle between heel and support
  - Ground reaction force of 320 N applied during heel strike simulation
10_1016_j_compbiomed_2021_104261.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**
  - Superior surfaces of tibia, fibula, and soft tissues fully fixed
  - Initial angle between heel and support: 10° (simulating foot position at heel strike)
  - Support displacement range: 7–10 mm toward the heel
  - Friction coefficient between foot and support: 0.6

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Ground reaction force (GRF): 320 N applied to heel during heel-strike
  - Displacements applied to flat support to simulate required GRF

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Frictional contact between foot and support (coefficient 0.6)
  - Interface between foot tissues and offloading support

- **Simulation Type:**
  - 3D finite element analysis
  - Tetrahedral mesh elements
  - Viscoelastic material behavior with Prony-series stress relaxation
  - Nonlinear analysis (compressible Neo-Hookean material model for EVA)
  - Heel strike simulation (static analysis for specific gait phase)
10_1016_j_compbiomed_2021_104261.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:**
  - Volumetric distribution of von Mises (effective) stress in heel soft tissues
  - Volumetric distribution of shear stress in heel soft tissues
  - Stress concentration patterns in soft tissues surrounding offloading holes

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**
  - Total Stress-Concentration Exposure (TSCE) for two VOIs
  - Normalized TSCE values (0-100 scale) for high-risk-VOI and peripheral-VOI
  - Volumetric exposure to von Mises stress in high-risk-VOI (cylindrical area ~2 cm² under calcaneus apex)
  - Volumetric exposure to von Mises stress in peripheral-VOI (surrounding soft tissue)
  - Multiplication of normalized high-risk-VOI TSCE and peripheral-VOI TSCE

- **Optimization Goal:**
  - Minimize the product of normalized high-risk-VOI TSCE and peripheral-VOI TSCE
  - Find offloading hole geometry parameters (radius, radius of curvature, depth) that simultaneously reduce stress in high-risk-VOI while minimizing stress concentration at wound peripheries
  - Identify two optimal configurations: (1) large offloading radius, large ROC, and large depth; (2) large offloading radius, large depth with relatively small ROC
10_1016_j_compbiomed_2021_104261.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**
  - Offloading hole radius constrained to 5–30 mm range
  - Offloading radius of curvature (ROC) constrained to 2–230 mm range
  - Offloading depth constrained to 1–15 mm range
  - Hole geometry limited to round-shaped design in posterior region of flat rectangular support
  - High-risk-VOI fixed as cylindrical area with ~2 cm² skin projection area under calcaneus apex
  - Model based on CT scan of single non-diabetic individual (not patient-specific)

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - Ground reaction force fixed at 320 N for all simulations to ensure consistent comparison
  - Friction coefficient fixed at 0.6 between foot and support
  - Initial angle between heel and support fixed at 10° to simulate heel strike position
  - Analysis limited to upper 90% of stress range for high-risk-VOI and upper 60% for peripheral-VOI in TSCE calculation
  - Study focused exclusively on heel strike phase (not full gait cycle)

- **Process/Manufacturing:**
  - Support material constrained to Ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA)
  - Hole geometry simplified to three parameters (radius, ROC, depth)
  - No consideration of time-dependent viscoelastic effects of EVA foam
  - Analysis limited to walking activity (excludes stair climbing, rising from chair)
  - Only 150 random offloading configurations examined within parameter ranges
  - No physical prototyping or clinical validation performed in this computational study

10_4028_www_scientific_net_aef_23_104.key_1:
• Gear bearing: planetary gearing integrated with roller bearings where sun gear (inner racer), ring gear (outer racer), and satellite gears (rollers) each have gears with rollers on end faces
• Material: AISI-1010 cold drawn steel with polish-quality grease surfaces
• Initial contact gap: 5µm between every contact pair
• Engagement type: involute with pitch/action angle α = 20°
• Teeth counts examined: 16-to-74 internal and 16-to-42 external gear bearing engagements
• Engagement variants: herringbone, arc (arched), and skew end faces
• Friction coefficients: static F_S = 0.15, dynamic F_D = 0.06, decay coefficient D_C = 10
• Speed deviation: 1.8-1.3% for internal engagements, 0.6-0.3% for external engagements
• Efficiency: η ~ 98% at external force up to F = 5N
• Mass characteristics: satellite gear mass s_2 = 0.197 kg, spinning inertia J_2Z = 0.568e-4 kg·m², orbital inertia J_0Z = 0.112e-2 kg·m²
• Friction coefficients in dynamical model: hysteresis f_H = 0.1, rolling f_R = 0.02, sliding f_S = 0.2
• Drag coefficients: f_F2 = 2e-7, f_F0 = 6e-6
• Maximum tested rotation speed: 600 rot/min
• Kinematical average reaction momentum: M_z1 = 0.376 N·m
• Axial load effect: skew end faces show less reaction force than arc/herringbone, but reaction forces on skew profiles saturate at higher loads
• Radial load effect: causes smallest reaction forces compared to thrust/twist loads
• Manufacturing constraints: cutting methods inapplicable due to hard edges; alternatives include knurling, electrical-discharge, and electrochemical machining
• Key application: nested planetary double-row gearings for watch mechanisms (e.g., 1 rotation per minute, hour, day, week)
10_4028_www_scientific_net_aef_23_104.key_2:
• Initial gap: 5µm between every contact pair
• Prescribed rotation speed applied to smaller gear (gear 2), output speed measured on bigger gear (1 or 3)
• Zero initial conditions: d₀|t=0 = 0, d₂|t=0 = 0, ψ₀|t=0 = 0, ψ₂|t=0 = 0, d(d₀)/dt|t=0 = 0, d(d₂)/dt|t=0 = 0
• Constant acceleration up to 600 rot/min at 0.1 sec applied to ring gear (gear 3)
• Involute engagement with pitch/action angle α = 20°
• Friction contact model: μ = F_D + (F_S − F_D) ∙ e^(−D_C|v_rel|) with F_S = 0.15, F_D = 0.06, D_C = 10
• Axial load in Z direction (thrust loading)
• Torque around Y-axis (twist loading)
• Radial force application (pressure loading)
• Constant external force up to F = 5N
• Topological hexahedral meshing with symmetry and circular cyclicity
• Air environment for drag force calculations up to 10,000 rot/min
• Stationary process analysis excluding dynamical acceleration components for misalignment studies
• Fixed axial rod constraint for sun bearing gear in reaction momentum calculations
• Piecewise contact force equations with angular distance gaps δ₀ = π/(φ·Z₃) + π/(φ·Z₁) and δ₂ = (2·π)/(φ·Z₂)
• Young's modulus (E) and contact area coefficient (A_f) in penalty force formulation
• Mass characteristics of ring and sun gears neglected in specific momentum calculations
10_4028_www_scientific_net_aef_23_104.key_3:
• Physics solved: kinematic relationships of planetary gear bearings with roller engagements, contact force dynamics, mechanical hysteresis, rolling/sliding friction phenomena, harmonic response, and self-stabilization behavior
• Target outputs: speed deviation (1.8-1.3% internal, 0.6-0.3% external engagements), efficiency (η ~ 98% at F ≤ 5N), reaction momentum (M_z1 = 0.376 N·m), friction coefficients (f_H = 0.1, f_R = 0.02, f_S = 0.2), drag coefficients (f_F2 = 2e-7, f_F0 = 6e-6), reaction forces under thrust/twist/pressure loading
• Optimization goals: maximize efficiency by minimizing friction losses, achieve self-stabilization to suppress harmonic excitations, select optimal engagement type (skew end faces for efficiency, herringbone/arc for smooth torque transfer), minimize speed deviation while preventing axial jamming, balance rigidity with operational smoothness for specific applications
10_4028_www_scientific_net_aef_23_104.key_4:
• Initial gap constraint: 5µm between contact pairs to prevent axial jamming
• Roller effective area diameters must correspond to pitch circles of respective gears
• Cavity width must exceed tooth width to prevent axial shifting
• Engagement types limited to herringbone, arc (arched), and skew end faces for axial stabilization
• Maximum tested rotation speed: 600 rot/min (though drag effects negligible up to 10,000 rot/min)
• Efficiency decreases linearly beyond F = 5N external force
• Reaction forces on skew end faces saturate at higher loads while arc/herringbone increase linearly
• Cutting methods inapplicable due to hard edges of closed cavities between gears and rollers
• Manufacturing limited to knurling, electrical-discharge, or electrochemical machining for skew edges
• Assembly constrained to symmetry parts in axial direction or segments of teeth with rollers in radial direction
• Minimum gap required to avoid jamming at smallest loads
• Sliding friction creates main strength of tying at compression loads, especially with arc/herringbone engagements

10_4028_www_scientific_net_amm_846_372.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Unsaturated seepage in porous media with variable boundary conditions including seepage face evolution
- **Material / Medium:** Unsaturated soils (Hostun Sand specified in Fig. 3a); liquid phase (water) with variable saturation; gas phase; soil-water characteristic curve; hydraulic conductivity dependent on saturation; liquid retention model with hysteresis capability
- **Application & Importance:** Modeling transient seepage face evolution during rain/flooding; capturing transitions between unsaturated and saturated states; simulating free surface movement; handling space-time variable boundary conditions on earthen slopes; enabling accurate transient analysis without mesh adaptivity
- **Geometry / Domain:** Slope geometry with multiple benches (terraces) shown in Fig. 1; 2D and 3D domains including quarter of a 3D pond (Fig. 6); impermeable boundaries; free surface as boundary between saturated/unsaturated zones; water level boundaries with time-varying conditions; mixed boundary conditions allowing transitions between Dirichlet, Neumann, and Signorini types
10_4028_www_scientific_net_amm_846_372.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**  
  - Unsaturation face: $\bar{q}_\ell = 0$, $q_\ell = w_\ell \cdot \hat{n} = 0$, $p_\ell \leq 0$  
  - Infiltration (e.g., rain): $\bar{q}_\ell \leq 0$, $q_\ell - \bar{q}_\ell \geq 0$, $p_\ell \leq 0$  
  - Ponding: $p_\ell(\boldsymbol{x}) = p_\ell^{max}(\boldsymbol{x})$  
  - Seepage return with ponding possibility: $q_\ell \geq 0$, $q_\ell - \bar{q}_\ell \geq 0$, $p_\ell - p_\ell^{max} \leq 0$  
  - Far boundaries: impermeable with $q_\ell = \bar{q}_\ell = 0$  
  - Hydraulic head (pressure) specified as variable  
  - Mixed boundary conditions with hydraulic head specified as variable  
  - Impermeable boundaries on slope geometry  

- **Loads / Excitations:**  
  - Rain infiltration (e.g., from rain)  
  - Water level lowering at right-hand side  
  - Varying flux applied at external surfaces for infiltration  
  - Irrigation from above and to sides  
  - Reduction in liquid pressure at boundaries  
  - Gas pressure assumed zero  

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**  
  - Signorini/ambiguous boundary conditions enabling transition between Dirichlet, Neumann, and seepage face conditions  
  - Seepage face with outward flow  
  - Free surface as boundary between saturated ($s_\ell = 1$) and unsaturated ($s_\ell < 1$) zones  
  - Transition between unsaturated and saturated states  

- **Simulation Type:**  
  - Transient analysis  
  - 2D and 3D simulations  
  - Implicit transient formulation  
  - Enriched finite element method  
  - Capable of handling continuous transitions between unsaturated and fully saturated states
10_4028_www_scientific_net_amm_846_372.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:**  
  - Transient fluid flow in unsaturated porous media  
  - Evolution of seepage face during drainage/imbibition  
  - Free surface movement (region with $s_\ell < 1$)  
  - Transition between unsaturated ($s_\ell < 1$) and fully saturated ($s_\ell = 1$) states  
  - Variable boundary conditions including rain infiltration and ponding  

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**  
  - Free surface location and evolution  
  - Seepage face position and evolution  
  - Liquid pressure distribution (shown in Figs. 5b, 6a, 6b)  
  - Saturation distribution (shown in Fig. 5b with black/white dots)  
  - Relative velocity field (arrows in Fig. 5b)  
  - Hydraulic conductivity as function of saturation  
  - Liquid retention behavior with hysteresis capability  

- **Optimization Goal:**  
  - Accurate modeling of variable boundary conditions without iterations or mesh adaptivity  
  - Capturing smooth transition between unsaturated and fully saturated states (and vice-versa)  
  - Enabling transient analysis of evolving seepage face crossing element edges  
  - Maintaining numerical robustness during transitions between Dirichlet, Neumann, and Signorini boundary conditions  
  - Preserving continuity of material models for liquid retention and hydraulic conductivity
10_4028_www_scientific_net_amm_846_372.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**  
  - Slope geometry with multiple benches/terraces  
  - 3D domain limited to quarter of a pond for symmetry  
  - Seepage face must be able to cross element edges (as shown in Fig. 5a)  
  - Enrichment applied only to edges/faces of elements where seepage face is expected  
  - Free surface defined as boundary between saturated ($s_\ell = 1$) and unsaturated ($s_\ell < 1$) zones  

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**  
  - Unsaturation face: $\bar{q}_\ell = 0$, $q_\ell = w_\ell \cdot \hat{n} = 0$, $p_\ell \leq 0$  
  - Infiltration condition: $\bar{q}_\ell \leq 0$, $q_\ell - \bar{q}_\ell \geq 0$, $p_\ell \leq 0$  
  - Ponding condition: $p_\ell(\boldsymbol{x}) = p_\ell^{max}(\boldsymbol{x})$  
  - Seepage return with ponding possibility: $q_\ell \geq 0$, $q_\ell - \bar{q}_\ell \geq 0$, $p_\ell - p_\ell^{max} \leq 0$  
  - Far boundaries: impermeable with $q_\ell = \bar{q}_\ell = 0$  
  - Gas pressure assumed zero  
  - Liquid saturation constrained to $0 \leq s_\ell \leq 1$  
  - Material models must be continuous to represent transitions between saturated and unsaturated states  
  - Kuhn-Tucker conditions must be satisfied for Signorini boundary conditions  

- **Process/Manufacturing:**  
  - Enriched finite element method requires additional degrees of freedom only at expected seepage face locations  
  - Implicit transient formulation with consistent tangent operators required  
  - Material models must be calibrated based on experimental data (Hostun Sand parameters shown in Fig. 3a)  
  - Ramp function in boundary condition implementation may be substituted by smooth version  
  - Simulation requires continuous liquid retention and hydraulic conductivity models for numerical robustness

10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2019_01_010.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Elastic-plastic characterization of thin film coatings on substrates using indentation testing with finite element analysis and optimization algorithms
- **Material / Medium:** 
  - Coating materials: Hydroxyapatite (HA), Chromium (Cr), Aluminum Oxide (Al₂O₃)
  - Substrates: Ti-6Al-4V, Stainless Steel (SS), Aluminum (Al)
  - Extracted properties: Young's modulus (E), yield stress (σ_y), work hardening exponent (n), Poisson's ratio (ν)
- **Application & Importance:** Determining intrinsic material properties of coated thin films where substrate deformation influences thin film behavior; overcoming complications in characterization due to film-substrate interaction effects
- **Geometry / Domain:** 
  - Axisymmetric conical indenter model: 30 μm × 30 μm substrate with 3 μm thin film, 70.3° half-angle indenter, 550 nm maximum penetration
  - 3D Berkovich indenter model: 100 μm high substrate with 40 μm radius, 10 μm thin film, 900 nm maximum penetration
  - Refined mesh under indenter tip with coarser mesh in substrate; frictionless indenter-film contact with perfectly bonded film-substrate interface
10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2019_01_010.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**
  - Roller boundary conditions on symmetry axis
  - Fixed boundary conditions at substrate bottom
  - Frictionless contact between indenter tip and thin film surface
  - Perfectly bonded film-substrate interface (no delamination, no slippage)
  - Mesh refinement beneath indenter tip with coarser mesh in substrate
  - Symmetry plane in axisymmetric models
  - Element types: CAX3 (axisymmetric), C3D6 (Berkovich tip), C3D4 (coated material)

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Loading step applied over 1 second to maximum penetration depth
  - Unloading step taking 1 second to return indenter to original position
  - Maximum penetration depth: 550 nm (axisymmetric conical model), 900 nm (3D Berkovich model)
  - 70.3° half-angle conical indenter (axisymmetric model)
  - Berkovich indenter with perfectly sharp tip and infinite Young's modulus (3D model)

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Master surface defined for indenter tip and slave surface for thin film top
  - Perfectly bonded film-substrate interface (F/SPB)
  - Two separate steps for loading and unloading behaviors
  - No pile-up, sink-in, or crack propagation considered during material property extraction

- **Simulation Type:**
  - Nonlinear finite element analysis with geometric and material nonlinearity
  - Axisymmetric conical indenter model (2D)
  - 3D Berkovich indenter model (half-substrate)
  - Time-dependent transient simulation with 2-second total duration (1s loading, 1s unloading)
  - Elastic-plastic behavior with nonlinear isotropic hardening
  - Lagrange linear interpolation polynomial (LLIP) for axisymmetric conical model
  - Cubic B-Spline approach for 3D Berkovich model
  - Optimization framework using trust-region-reflective and interior-reflective Newton approach
10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2019_01_010.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Elastic-plastic deformation behavior of thin film coatings on substrates under indentation loading/unloading, including nonlinear isotropic hardening, stress distribution (Von Mises and axial stress), load-displacement relationship, and plastic zone development

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** 
  - Thin film Young's modulus (E_f)
  - Thin film yield stress (σ_y,f)
  - Thin film work hardening exponent (n_f)
  - Load-displacement (P-h) curves
  - Residual penetration depth after unloading
  - Objective function value (least squares error between FE and target data)
  - Stress distributions (Von Mises, axial stress) at critical locations
  - Coefficient of determination (R-squared)

- **Optimization Goal:** Minimize the least squares error between finite element analysis results and target indentation load-displacement data to extract unique elastic-plastic material properties (E_f, σ_y,f, n_f) of thin film coatings, achieving convergence with less than 0.7% deviation from target values even when initial guess values differ significantly from actual properties
10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2019_01_010.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**
  - Axisymmetric model: 30 μm × 30 μm substrate with 3 μm thin film thickness
  - 3D Berkovich model: 100 μm high substrate with 40 μm radius, 10 μm thin film thickness
  - Maximum penetration depth: 550 nm (axisymmetric), 900 nm (3D)
  - Mesh density: 13,079 elements (axisymmetric), 22,288 four-node tetrahedron elements (3D)
  - Minimum element size beneath indenter: 0.149 μm
  - Film thickness to penetration depth ratio: h_m/t_f ≤ 9% (shallow indentation)

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - Material property boundaries: 0 < E < 10 × 10^5 MPa, 0 < ν < 0.5, 0 < σ_y < 10^4 MPa, 0 < n < 0.5
  - Frictionless contact between indenter tip and thin film surface
  - Perfectly bonded film-substrate interface (no delamination, no slippage)
  - No pile-up, sink-in, or crack propagation considered during material extraction
  - Maximum penetration depth restricted to approximately 10% of film thickness
  - Loading/unloading duration: 1 second each (total 2 seconds)
  - Optimization convergence tolerance (SSE) as low as 10^-16 for 3D Berkovich model

- **Process/Manufacturing:**
  - Optimization uses multiple starting points with ±10% perturbation for global solution verification
  - Five initial work hardening exponent values tested (n_0 ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4}) for parallel optimization
  - ABAQUS used for FE analysis with specific element types (CAX3, C3D6, C3D4)
  - MATLAB for pre-processing and optimization algorithm
  - Python for post-processing to extract load-displacement data from ABAQUS output
  - Two separate simulation steps for loading and unloading behaviors
  - No consideration of friction coefficient between film and substrate (assumed perfectly bonded)

10_1016_j_tws_2025_113060.key_1:
- Bio-inspired vertex-offset lattice metamaterials, specifically Vertex-Offset Face-Centered-Cubic (VOFCC) lattices
- 316 L stainless steel base material with density ρ = 7.98 g/cm³, Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3, yield stress σ_ys = 367 MPa, ultimate stress σ_u = 436 MPa, Young's modulus E = 150 GPa
- Unit cell dimensions L₀ = 5 mm with 64 unit cells arranged in 4 × 4 × 4 array, overall size L = 20 mm
- Strut radius set at 0.35 mm for all lattice specimens
- Relative densities: FCC = 0.181, BCC = 0.178, VOFCC = 0.197
- Vertex offset distance L₁ defined with offset ratio m = L₁/L₀, studied at m = 1/6, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 5/6
- Three lattice types analyzed: Face-Centered Cubic (FCC), Body-Centered Cubic (BCC), and transitional VOFCC
- Fabricated using Selective Laser Melting (SLM) additive manufacturing with SimpNeed MS180 system
- Strut diameter variations studied: R = 0.25 mm, 0.30 mm, 0.35 mm, 0.40 mm, 0.45 mm
- Strut length variations studied: L₀ = 3.5 mm, 4.0 mm, 5.0 mm, 5.5 mm, 6.0 mm
- Designed to overcome stress drops and fluctuations caused by localized deformation failures
- Engineered to resolve trade-off between high stress and structural stability in traditional lattice metamaterials
- Applications in aerospace, automotive, and marine engineering for energy absorption and load-bearing components
- Deformation modes include delocalized deformation (VOFCC) versus localized shear bands (FCC and BCC)
- Stretching-dominated (Octet-Truss) and bending-dominated (Kelvin) structural behaviors analyzed
- Energy absorption metrics: Energy Absorption (EA), Specific Energy Absorption (SEA), Crush Force Efficiency (CFE)

• **Identity & Domain:** Linear permanent magnet generator for wave energy conversion; direct-drive system where translator moves relative to stator; analyzed via time-stepping finite element method; component of wave energy conversion chain with primary (mechanical motion), secondary (electrical energy production), and tertiary (grid power conversion) stages.

• **Material / Medium:** Neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) permanent magnets in translator; M-36 electrical steel for stator and translator core; copper windings; slot-less stator configuration; quasi-halbach magnetization pattern.

• **Application & Importance:** Wave energy conversion with 88.20% efficiency; lightweight design achieved by reducing mass; eliminates mechanical interfaces (gearbox, hydraulic pump) of conventional rotating generators; analyzes copper loss, core loss (hysteresis, eddy current, excess), and their impact on efficiency; 2-3 kW/m² power density of wave energy compared to 0.4-0.6 kW/m² for wind and 0.1-0.2 kW/m² for solar.

• **Geometry / Domain:** Linear (non-rotational) configuration; translator with series of quasi-halbach magnetized permanent magnets; stator with full-pitch winding; outer radius (Re) of stator analyzed from 42.8 mm to 72.8 mm; components include steel core, supporting tube, coil, and permanent magnets; three-dimensional model with slot-less configuration.

• **Loads / Excitations:** Excitation current injected into windings (varied to analyze copper loss); frequency range 10–100 Hz (for core loss analysis); stator outer radius (Re) varied from 42.8 mm to 72.8 mm (affecting induced-EMF and copper loss).

• **Interactions / Interfaces:** Direct mechanical coupling between WEC and translator (no gearbox/hydraulic pump); electromagnetic interaction between translator (quasi-halbach magnetized NdFeB magnets) and stator (copper windings); slot-less stator configuration enabling sinusoidal air-gap flux distribution.

• **Simulation Type:** Time-stepping finite element method; three-dimensional (3D) transient electromagnetic analysis.

• **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Efficiency (88.20%); copper loss; core loss (hysteresis, classical eddy current, and excess components); induced-EMF; core loss at frequencies 10–100 Hz; copper loss under varying excitation currents; induced-EMF and copper loss versus stator outer radius (Re) from 42.8 mm to 72.8 mm.

• **Optimization Goal:** Maximize efficiency by optimizing dimensional ratios (e.g., stator outer radius) that significantly influence electromagnetic performance and loss characteristics.

- Interfacial shear stress defined as τ_k = (Δσ_fk/Δl_k)h_fe
- Slip defined as s_k = Σ(ε_j+ε_j+1)/2 Δl_j
- Lap lengths tested: 12.5-300 mm (specifically 50 mm, 100 mm, 150 mm)
- Activation temperature range: 150-400°C for Fe-SMA
- Mesh specifications: Adhesive layer (1×1 mm), Fe-SMA (2×0.6 mm), Steel plate (2×2.86 mm)
- Element types: C3D8R for steel plate and Fe-SMA, COH3D8 for adhesive layer
- Damage initiation criterion: Quadratic nominal stress criterion
- Damage propagation criterion: B-K criterion
- Mixed-mode CZM (Cohesive Zone Model) response accounting for Mode 1 and Mode S
- Numerical modeling in ABAQUS with 3D finite element approach
- True stress-strain curves used for Fe-SMA (Q355, Q460, Q690, Q960) and steel materials
10_1016_j_istruc_2025_109386.key_3:
- Bond strength (F_u) prediction of Fe-SMA/steel single lap joints using machine learning models with Cohesive Zone Model (CZM) damage mechanics
- Primary output: Bond strength (F_u) in kN
- Evaluation metrics: Root mean square error (E_r), mean absolute error (E_m), determination coefficient (R²), mean absolute percentage error (E_p)
- Optimization objectives: Minimize E_r (1.789-2.222 for unoptimized, 0.852-1.208 for optimized), minimize E_m (1.264-1.741 for unoptimized, 0.558-0.816 for optimized), maximize R² (0.965-0.977 for unoptimized, 0.991-0.997 for optimized)
- Feature importance ranking to identify critical parameters affecting bond strength
- Determination of effective lap length (125 mm) for optimal stress transfer
- Hyperparameter optimization of RF and BPNN using SSA, PSO, GTO, and AVOA algorithms
- Maximization of prediction accuracy for unaged and aged conditions (23°C, 55°C/98% RH, 55°C tap water with aging times 30-110 days)
10_1016_j_istruc_2025_109386.key_4:
- Lap length (l₀) constrained to 12.5–300 mm with effective length approaching 125 mm (beyond which increasing length yields minimal F_u improvement)
- Fe-SMA thickness (h_fe) limited to 1–5 mm range
- Fe-SMA width (b_fe) constrained to 25–70 mm range
- Steel thickness (h_st) constrained to 10–12 mm range
- Environmental chamber temperature range: -20 to 150°C
- Water tank temperature range: -50 to 1300°C
- Loading speed fixed at 0.09 mm/min for all tests
- Interfacial stiffness (K_a) constrained to 167.4–896.1 MPa/mm
- Interfacial shear stress (τ_f) constrained to 8.04–31.45 MPa
- Interfacial energy (G_u) constrained to 0.17–2.30 MPa·mm
- Mesh size limitations: Adhesive layer (1×1 mm), Fe-SMA (2×0.6 mm), Steel plate (2×2.86 mm)
- Element type constraints: C3D8R for steel/Fe-SMA, COH3D8 for adhesive layer
- Out-of-plane constraint applied to steel plate in numerical modeling
- Population size constrained to 15 for RF and 20 for BPNN in optimization
- Iteration number fixed at 200 for all intelligent optimization algorithms
- Damage initiation criterion limited to quadratic nominal stress criterion
- Damage propagation criterion constrained to B-K criterion
- Analysis limited to linear epoxy-based adhesives
- Debonding failures (not Fe-SMA fracture) are the primary failure mode in Fe-SMA-bonded structures
- SHAP analysis shows minimal effect of σ_fu, E_s, and h_st on bond strength
- Substantial K_a values degrade interface ductility and increase stress concentration

10_1016_j_simpat_2018_04_001.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Non-pneumatic mechanical elastic wheel (MEW) for vehicle applications
- **Material / Medium:** 
  - Elastic ring: Steel (density 7.850×10³ kg/m³, Young's modulus 1.98×10⁵ MPa, Poisson's ratio 0.30)
  - Hub: Steel (density 7.850×10³ kg/m³, Young's modulus 2.05×10⁵ MPa, Poisson's ratio 0.29)
  - Hinge group: Steel (density 7.850×10³ kg/m³, Young's modulus 2.10×10⁵ MPa, Poisson's ratio 0.28)
  - Rubber layer: Incompressible hyperelastic material (density 0.920×10³ kg/m³, Poisson's ratio 0.49, Mooney-Rivlin parameters C₁₀=0.88, C₀₁=-0.18)
  - Cord ply: Reinforcing fibers (density 1.060×10³ kg/m³, Mooney-Rivlin parameters C₁₀=0.97, C₀₁=-0.42)
- **Application & Importance:** 
  - Eliminates puncture and blowout risks associated with pneumatic tires
  - Statically indeterminate structure maintains functionality when partial hinge groups fail
  - Provides guidance for optimization of MEW and other non-pneumatic tire structures
  - Analyzes grounding characteristics, stress distribution, and dynamic behaviors under rolling conditions
- **Geometry / Domain:** 
  - Integrated wheel-tire structure with hub, elastic outer wheel, and hinge groups
  - Elastic outer wheel contains five evenly distributed elastic rings embedded in rubber layer
  - Free (undeformed) radius: 470.20 mm; loaded radius: 450.18 mm; effective rolling radius: 464.13 mm
  - Circular structure with 12 hinge groups connecting hub to elastic outer wheel
  - Deforms elliptically under load with flattened contact region and bent hinge groups in contact area
  - Non-contact region maintains tension in hinge groups for load distribution
10_1016_j_simpat_2018_04_001.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**
  - Wheel fixed in all directions except z-direction for footprint analysis
  - Translation degrees of freedom free in x and z directions for rolling analysis
  - Rotation degree of freedom free about y-axis for rolling analysis
  - Rigid surface defined to represent road contact
  - Hard contact used for normal interaction of contact interfaces
  - Embedded element constraint for elastic rings in rubber layer
  - Hinge connector applied to simulate mutual rotation of hinges

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Axial force of 10,000 N applied at hub center (rated load)
  - Radial loads ranging from 2.9 kN to 17.2 kN for static testing
  - Vertical loads of 8 kN and 14 kN for dynamic testing
  - Constant horizontal velocity of 60 km/h for steady rolling
  - Angular velocity varied from 34 to 38 rad/s to determine free rolling state
  - Initial friction coefficient of 0.6
  - Free (undeformed) radius of 470.20 mm; loaded radius of 450.18 mm

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Surface-to-surface contact with small slip algorithm
  - Coulomb friction model for tangential force determination
  - Penalty function method for normal force determination
  - Rebar model describing nonlinear mechanical characteristics of cord ply
  - Reference node at hub center for force application

- **Simulation Type:**
  - 3D nonlinear finite element analysis
  - Steady-state transport technology in Abaqus/Standard
  - Four analysis steps: finite element modeling, model validation, footprint analysis, and steady-state rolling analysis
  - Nonlinear material properties using Mooney-Rivlin model for rubber components
  - Large deformation analysis between wheel and road
  - Quasi-static analysis for static loading conditions
  - Total nodes: 204,783; total elements: 170,834
  - C3D8R solid element type used for meshing elastic outer ring, hinge groups, and hub
10_1016_j_simpat_2018_04_001.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:**
  - Steady-state rolling behavior of non-pneumatic mechanical elastic wheel (MEW)
  - Contact mechanics between wheel and rigid surface
  - Large deformation characteristics of elastic components
  - Stress distribution in elastic rings and hinge groups
  - Ground contact pressure and friction stress distribution
  - Nonlinear material response of rubber components

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**
  - Normal pressure distribution in contact region (0.62-0.72 MPa maximum stress)
  - Friction stress distribution (CSHEAR1 values ranging from -0.02 to 0.07)
  - Footprint dimensions (250-276 mm length, 152-168 mm width)
  - Equivalent stress in elastic rings (up to 88.97 MPa)
  - Maximum equivalent stress in hinge groups (254.8 MPa at 60 km/h, 483.4 MPa at 120 km/h)
  - Longitudinal force vs. slip ratio characteristics
  - Load-deflection relationship (radial load vs. wheel deformation)
  - Deformation magnitude of elastic ring (up to 2.098 mm)
  - Angular velocity at free rolling state (35.92 rad/s)

- **Optimization Goal:**
  - Enhance load-carrying capacity by increasing cross-section area of middle elastic ring
  - Improve stress distribution to prevent failure at hinge group connection points
  - Optimize structural parameters to minimize high-stress regions in critical components
  - Maximize durability while maintaining non-pneumatic safety advantages
  - Achieve optimal grounding characteristics across various rolling conditions (static, free rolling, driving, braking)
  - Balance stress distribution to prevent premature wear in contact zone
10_1016_j_simpat_2018_04_001.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**
  - Free (undeformed) radius constrained to 470.20 mm
  - Loaded radius constrained to 450.18 mm
  - Effective rolling radius constrained to 464.13 mm at free rolling state
  - Five elastic rings must be evenly distributed along the circumference of the elastic outer wheel
  - Twelve hinge groups required to connect hub to elastic outer wheel
  - Structure must maintain elastic deformation capability while supporting load

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - Maximum equivalent stress in hinge groups must remain below material yield strength (483.4 MPa at 120 km/h)
  - Maximum stress concentration constrained to the connection between hinge group and elastic outer wheel
  - Middle elastic ring experiences higher stress than other four groups, requiring cross-sectional area adjustment
  - Rotational speed affects maximum normal stress (0.62-0.72 MPa range from 0-120 km/h)
  - Longitudinal force must remain within saturation limits at high slip ratios
  - Angular velocity constrained to 35.92 rad/s for free rolling state

- **Process/Manufacturing:**
  - Hinge group bolt connection identified as "weak link" in the structure
  - Material properties constrained by Mooney-Rivlin model parameters (C₁₀=0.88, C₀₁=-0.18 for rubber layer)
  - Numerical simulations did not consider temperature effects on mechanical properties
  - Constant friction coefficient (0.6) used instead of variable friction characteristics
  - Fatigue performance of hinge groups requires further investigation beyond current study
  - FE model required simplifications (chamfers and hub holes removed, hinge group simplified to 3-link structure)

10_1007_s00170_024_14629_x.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Selective Laser Melting (SLM) process for AlSi10Mg alloy, focusing on molten pool characteristics, microstructure formation, and mechanical properties
- **Material / Medium:** AlSi10Mg powder alloy with composition: 10.6% Si, 0.45% Mg, ≤0.55% Fe, ≤0.1% Zn, ≤0.45% Mn, ≤0.15% Ti, balance Al; powder size range 15–53 μm; average particle size 24.09 μm; D10=11.27 μm, D50=21.54 μm, D90=40.30 μm; theoretical density 2.68 g/cm³
- **Application & Importance:** Optimization of SLM process parameters to achieve high density (≥99.6%) and superior mechanical properties for AlSi10Mg parts; understanding relationship between volumetric energy density (VED), molten pool morphology, and final part properties
- **Geometry / Domain:** Cubic samples (10 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm); tensile specimens with gauge length 10 mm, width 5 mm, thickness 2 mm; powder layer thickness 0.02–0.04 mm; molten pool dimensions varying with process parameters; microstructure showing fine grain zone (FGZ), coarse grain zone (CGZ), and heat affected zone (HAZ)
10_1007_s00170_024_14629_x.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** 
  - Boundary condition: k∂T/∂n - 2AP/πR² exp(-2r²/R²) + h(T-T₀) + εσ(T⁴-T₀⁴) = 0
  - Powder layer represented by hexahedral elements, solid metal represented by tetrahedral elements
  - Molten pool area defined where temperature exceeds 600°C (material melting point)
  - Powder layer thickness represented by white dashed line in cross-section
  - AlSi10Mg powder modeled as continuous medium
  - Vaporization and solid-gas coupling ignored in simulation
  - Effective thermal conductivity of powder set to one tenth of solid material conductivity
  - Laser beam heat flux simulated by Gaussian distribution on surface

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Laser power: 330 W, 350 W, 370 W
  - Scanning speed: 1200 mm/s, 1300 mm/s, 1400 mm/s
  - Hatch spacing: 0.17 mm, 0.19 mm, 0.21 mm
  - Layer thickness: 0.02 mm, 0.03 mm, 0.04 mm
  - Volumetric Energy Density (VED): 33.40-80.88 J/mm³
  - Absorptivity: 0.09
  - Laser beam radius: 0.06 μm
  - Ambient temperature: 25°C
  - Platform preheated to 100°C during printing preparation
  - Inert protective gas: 99% high-purity Argon with oxygen content ≤1‰

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Molten pool metallurgical bonding with lower metal layers
  - Thermal conductivity of powder layer much lower than solid material
  - Liquid diffusion throughout molten pool before solidification
  - Etching with Keller's reagent (1 mL HF, 1.5 mL HCl, 2.5 mL HNO3, 95 mL H2O) for microstructure analysis
  - "Chessboard" laser scanning strategy used for sample fabrication

- **Simulation Type:**
  - Transient thermal analysis using Finite Element Method (FEM)
  - 3D domain (x, y, z dimensions)
  - ANSYS software implementation
  - Heat transfer governed by equation: ρc∂T/∂t = Q + ∂/∂x(k∂T/∂x) + ∂/∂y(k∂T/∂y) + ∂/∂z(k∂T/∂z)
  - Initial temperature condition: T(x, y, z, t)t=0 = T₀
  - Material properties temperature-dependent
  - Laser heat source modeled as Gaussian distribution
10_1007_s00170_024_14629_x.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** 
  - Thermal behavior and heat transfer dynamics in molten pool during SLM process
  - Phase transformation (powder melting and solidification)
  - Microstructure evolution including fine grain zone (FGZ), coarse grain zone (CGZ), and heat affected zone (HAZ) formation
  - Pore formation mechanisms (irregular defective pores at low VED vs. spherical pores at high VED)
  - Solidification behavior under different cooling rates and thermal gradients

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**
  - Relative density (99.6% maximum for No. 5 sample)
  - Volumetric Energy Density (VED) values (33.40-80.88 J/mm³)
  - Molten pool dimensions (length, width, depth) with specific measurements: 179.66-249.27 μm depth, 195.23-351.27 μm width
  - Width-to-depth ratio of molten pool (3.6-5.2 range)
  - Peak temperature (1500-2800°C range observed)
  - Liquid phase time
  - Mechanical properties: yield strength (Rp0.2) 169.87-222.88 MPa, ultimate tensile strength (Rm) 395.78-436.81 MPa, elongation (A) 4.06-7.75%
  - Density measurements (2.598-2.670 g/cm³ range)
  - Microstructure characteristics including cellular-dendritic morphology and phase composition

- **Optimization Goal:**
  - Maximize relative density (achieved 99.6% at VED=64.10 J/mm³)
  - Maximize mechanical properties (achieved tensile strength 436.81 MPa, yield strength 222.88 MPa, elongation 7.75%)
  - Determine optimal process parameter combination: scanning speed 1300 mm/s, laser power 350 W, hatch spacing 0.21 mm, layer thickness 0.02 mm (VED=64.10 J/mm³)
  - Achieve optimal VED range of 60-70 J/mm³ for best density and mechanical properties
  - Minimize defects (pores) by controlling VED to prevent both irregular pores (low VED) and spherical pores (high VED)
  - Achieve fine microstructure with uniform distribution of alloying elements for solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening
10_1007_s00170_024_14629_x.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**
  - Cubic samples dimension: 10 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm
  - Tensile specimen geometry: gauge length 10 mm, width 5 mm, thickness 2 mm
  - Powder particle size range: 15-53 μm
  - Single-layer powder thickness constrained to be less than 0.05 mm
  - Equipment forming space: 250 mm × 250 mm × 325 mm maximum
  - Laser scanning strategy: "Chessboard" pattern with specific orientation

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - Material melting point: 600°C (threshold for molten pool definition)
  - Oxygen content in protective gas: ≤1‰ to prevent oxidation
  - Platform preheating temperature: 100°C to avoid warpage
  - Optimal VED range: 60-70 J/mm³ (with maximum density at 64.10 J/mm³)
  - Maximum achievable relative density: 99.6% (No. 5 sample)
  - Process parameter ranges: scanning speed 1200-1400 mm/s, laser power 330-370 W, hatch spacing 0.17-0.21 mm, layer thickness 0.02-0.04 mm
  - VED lower limit: 33.40 J/mm³ (caused irregular pores)
  - VED upper limit: 80.88 J/mm³ (caused spherical pores)

- **Process/Manufacturing:**
  - Equipment: EOSINT M280 (EOS®, Germany) with maximum scanning speed of 7000 mm/s
  - Protective gas: 99% high-purity Argon
  - Post-processing: samples separated from platform by WEDM after fabrication
  - Powder characteristics: spherical pre-alloyed AlSi10Mg with average particle size 24.09 μm
  - Orthogonal experimental design: L9-3⁴ (4 factors at 3 levels)
  - Manufacturing challenge: thin powder layer thickness poses accuracy challenges for powder roller and increases time consumption
  - "Balling" effect occurs at low laser power and high scanning speed
  - Keyhole porosity increases with decreasing laser power
  - Platform preheating required to avoid thermal expansion-induced warpage and deformation

10_1007_s12008_024_01898_9.key_1:
- **Subject:** Lower suspension arm (control arm) for automotive vehicles
- **Material:** Five-layer carbon/epoxy composite laminate with properties: axial modulus 131.6 GPa, transverse modulus 10.8 GPa, shear modulus G12 5.65 GPa, shear modulus G23 3.38 GPa, Poisson's ratio m12 0.28, Poisson's ratio m23 0.59, density 1540 kg/m³
- **Application:** To replace metallic suspension arms with composite alternatives for weight reduction while maintaining structural integrity; optimization aims to minimize stress concentrations in X-direction (SX), Y-direction (SY), and von Mises stress to increase service life
- **Geometry:** Complex curved structure with multiple holes; modeled with SHELL181-4-node shell elements; thickness varied between 10-20 mm; five layers with fiber orientations ranging from -60° to 90°; meshed with 1 mm element size; coordinate system defined with X, Y, Z axes and local element coordinate system with s,u, t,v, r,w directions
10_1007_s12008_024_01898_9.key_2:
- **Boundary conditions:** SHELL181-4-node shell elements used for 3D meshing; element size of 1 mm (determined through convergence study with adaptive sizing between 1-4 mm showing 5% convergence accuracy); model geometry defined by connecting essential locations using lines and splines; volume divided into 5 layers with specific thickness and different fiber orientations
- **Loads:** Loads applied to the suspension arm (exact values not specified in text); analysis measures resulting stress along X-direction (SX), stress along Y-direction (SY), and von Mises stress as primary outputs
- **Interactions:** Five-layer composite structure with varying fiber orientations; different thickness values (10-20 mm) tested with different fiber angle combinations ranging from -60° to 90° across layers
- **Simulation type:** 3D static finite element analysis; conducted using ANSYS APDL; simulation parameter ranges: thickness from 10 mm to 20 mm, fiber orientations from -60° to 90° for five layers; 50 distinct models simulated with different thickness and fiber orientation combinations
10_1007_s12008_024_01898_9.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Structural stress distribution in composite laminates under static loading conditions
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Maximum stress in X-direction (SX), maximum stress in Y-direction (SY), and von Mises stress
- **Optimization Goal:** Multi-objective minimization of SX, SY, and von Mises stress to reduce stress concentration and improve stress distribution, thereby increasing service life of the composite suspension arm
10_1007_s12008_024_01898_9.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Thickness constrained to three discrete values (10 mm, 15 mm, 20 mm); fiber orientations for all five layers constrained to range between -60° and 90°; five-layer composite structure with fixed total thickness for each optimization case; element size constrained to 1 mm (determined through mesh convergence study with adaptive sizing between 1-4 mm)
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Optimization targets minimization of three stress metrics (SX, SY, von Mises) as the primary performance criteria; sensitivity analysis shows negative relationship between thickness and stress values (increasing thickness reduces stress)
- **Process/Manufacturing:** Carbon/epoxy composite material with fixed mechanical properties (axial modulus 131.6 GPa, transverse modulus 10.8 GPa, etc.); SHELL181-4-node shell elements required for 3D modeling; optimization conducted separately for each thickness level with fiber angles as the only variables; GA parameters constrained to population size 500, 500 generations, crossover probability 0.95, mutation probability 0.05

10_1007_s00202_025_02970_7.key_1:
- Traveling wave rotary ultrasonic motor stators with T-shaped tooth structure
- Phosphor bronze (115 GPa Young's modulus, 8780 kg/m³ density, 0.33 Poisson's ratio); PZT-8 piezoelectric ceramic (7650 kg/m³ density, 0.3 Poisson's ratio); epoxy resin (0.7 GPa Young's modulus, 3500 kg/m³ density, 0.43 Poisson's ratio); PTFE friction layer; aluminum alloy rotor; carbon steel spring plates and bearings
- Optimization of stator vibration characteristics to increase frequency separation between working mode and interference modes while enhancing working mode amplitude for improved motor performance and efficiency
- Circular ring structure with 72 T-shaped teeth; outer diameter 60 mm; inner diameter 45 mm; tooth center angle 4°; overall height 3.8 mm; piezoelectric ceramic thickness 0.5 mm; epoxy bonding layer 0.05 mm; T-shaped tooth dimensions: H2=2 mm, H3=0.9 mm, H4=0.3 mm, H5=2.3 mm
10_1007_s00202_025_02970_7.key_2:
- Fixed supports at bolt hole positions
- Inner ring of stator fixed with outer ring free
- 100 Vpp sinusoidal AC voltage applied to one phase
- V1=100sin w, V2=0, V3=0 voltage configuration
- Preload of 50 N between stator and rotor
- Two AC signals with 90-degree phase difference
- Frequency range of 38–56 kHz for simulations
- Frequency range of 43–49 kHz for experimental measurements
- Structural damping rate of 0.2%
- Frictional contact between stator teeth and rotor surface
- Inverse piezoelectric effect for energy conversion
- Epoxy resin bonding between elastic matrix and piezoelectric ceramic
- Modal analysis with solution order of 70
- Harmonic response analysis
- 3D modeling of stator structure
- Linear vibration analysis regime
10_1007_s00202_025_02970_7.key_3:
- Modal vibration characteristics and harmonic response of stator structure
- Modal frequencies of B08, B09, and B010 modes; vibration amplitude in micrometers; frequency separation between working mode (B09) and interference modes (B08 and B010); resonance frequency; working mode amplitude
- Maximize frequency difference between working mode (B09) and adjacent interference modes (B08, B010) while maximizing working mode amplitude under constant driving voltage; increase frequency separation by 8.2% and 4.7% respectively while increasing working mode amplitude by 16.1%
10_1007_s00202_025_02970_7.key_4:
- Geometric constraints: H1, H3, H4, H5, and A parameters varied within ±0.2 mm from initial dimensions; piezoelectric ceramic thickness fixed at 0.5 mm; epoxy thickness fixed at 0.05 mm; outer diameter fixed at 60 mm; 72 teeth with 4° center angle; T-shaped tooth formed by removing portion of rectangle at lower end
- Performance constraints: Objective function G1 constrained to 0.1-0.125 range; structural damping rate of 0.2% in harmonic analysis; frequency range limited to 38-56 kHz for simulations; driving voltage fixed at 100 Vpp; preload maintained at 50 N; minimum frequency separation required between working mode (B09) and interference modes (B08, B010) to prevent modal aliasing
- Manufacturing constraints: Phosphor bronze elastic matrix for low damping and wear; PZT-8 piezoelectric ceramic for high piezoelectric coefficient and mechanical strength; epoxy resin bonding between elastic matrix and ceramic; T-shaped tooth designed for easier processing with standard milling tools; rotor material selected as hard aluminum alloy for low density and inertia; PTFE friction layer required on rotor surface after surface roughening; base and case made from aluminum alloy; spring plates and bearings made from carbon steel

10_1016_j_nucengdes_2025_113948.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Two segmented asymmetrical thermoelectric generators (TEGs) - specifically inverted circular truncated cone and circular-X types - for heat pipe cooled nuclear reactor applications
- **Material / Medium:** P-type and N-type Bi₂Te₃ (low-temperature segment), CoSb₃ (high-temperature segment), copper electrodes, solder layer, ceramic substrate; potassium heat pipes in experimental setup
- **Application & Importance:** Thermal-to-electric energy conversion in heat pipe reactor systems for deep space/deep sea exploration; optimizing power generation efficiency while managing thermal stress to prevent interface fatigue and failure in high-temperature reactor environments
- **Geometry / Domain:** Asymmetrical thermoelectric legs with variable cross-sections; inverted circular truncated cone (0.5-1.1 mm minimum radius) and circular-X configurations; 3D models include P-type and N-type legs, copper electrodes, and ceramic substrate; minimum cross-sectional radius (0.5-1.1 mm) and height ratios of segmented materials as key design parameters
10_1016_j_nucengdes_2025_113948.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**
  - Constant wall temperature boundary condition at high-temperature and low-temperature ends
  - Heat transfer to external environment considered as zero (adiabatic)
  - High-temperature and low-temperature ends fixed, other boundaries free
  - Temperature ranges: 793.15K, 893.15K, 993.15K, 1093.15K, 1193.15K
  - Minimum cross-sectional radius range: 0.5-1.1 mm
  - External resistance range: 0-0.14 Ω
  - Contact conductivity range: 0.01-100 × 10⁹ S/m²
  - Surface roughness range: 0.01-100 μm

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Six electrical heating rods in experimental setup
  - Potassium heat pipes arranged parallelly to transfer heat
  - Thermal input through heat pipes
  - External electrical load resistance
  - Contact electrical resistance (0.01-100 × 10⁹ S/m²)
  - Contact thermal resistance (surface roughness 0.01-100 μm)

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - P-type and N-type thermoelectric legs with copper electrodes, solder layer, and ceramic substrate
  - Electrical and thermal contacts added at thermal and electrical interfaces
  - Thermal expansion multiphysics field coupling solid heat transfer and solid mechanics
  - External circuit connection with load resistance (R_L)
  - Contact interfaces between thermoelectric legs and electrodes
  - Thermal contact resistance at interfaces due to surface roughness

- **Simulation Type:**
  - Steady-state analysis method
  - Three-dimensional modeling using COMSOL Multiphysics 5.6
  - Control variable method (changing one factor at a time)
  - Thermoelectric and mechanical coupling analysis
  - 3D finite element simulation with refined mesh (28,615-28,954 domain elements)
10_1016_j_nucengdes_2025_113948.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:**
  - Thermoelectric conversion (Seebeck, Peltier, and Thomson effects)
  - Thermal stress distribution and mechanical deformation
  - Coupled thermoelectric-mechanical behavior
  - Heat transfer through solid materials with temperature-dependent properties
  - Electrical current flow with contact resistance effects

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**
  - Output power (W)
  - Output voltage (V)
  - Output current (A)
  - Thermoelectric conversion efficiency (%)
  - Internal resistance (Ω)
  - Maximum von Mises stress (10⁸ Pa)
  - Temperature gradient across thermoelectric materials
  - Contact resistance effects on performance
  - Temperature distribution within device

- **Optimization Goal:**
  - Maximize thermoelectric conversion efficiency while minimizing thermal stress at critical interfaces
  - For inverted circular truncated cone TEG: Achieve optimal hot end to cold end cross-sectional ratio of 0.83 (minimum radius 1.0 mm) to reduce maximum stress with minimal efficiency loss
  - For circular-X TEG: Achieve minimum cross-sectional radius of 1.0 mm to shift maximum stress from hot end to minimum cross-section while maintaining higher efficiency than cylindrical design
  - Improve structural stability by shifting thermal stress from hot end interfaces to cold end or minimum cross-section to prevent interface fatigue and failure in high-temperature reactor applications
10_1016_j_nucengdes_2025_113948.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**
  - Minimum cross-sectional radius constrained between 0.5 mm and 1.1 mm
  - Ratio of upper to lower cross-sections must not be less than 0.8 to prevent sharp efficiency decrease
  - Optimal hot end to cold end cross-sectional ratio of 0.83 (minimum radius 1.0 mm) for inverted circular truncated cone TEG
  - Optimal cross-sectional radius of 1.0 mm for circular-X TEG to shift maximum stress from hot end to minimum cross-section

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - Maximum von Mises stress value of 4.13 × 10⁸ Pa for inverted circular truncated cone TEG with minimum cross-sectional radius of 1 mm
  - Operating temperature range from 793.15 K to 1193.15 K
  - Output power decreases by 94%-97% and efficiency decreases by 78%-85% when surface roughness increases from 0.01 μm to 100 μm
  - Output power increases by 1200%-3500% and efficiency increases by 920%-2380% when contact conductivity increases from 0.01 × 10⁹ S/m² to 100 × 10⁹ S/m²
  - Maximum conversion efficiency reaches 10.84% at ΔT = 600 K for circular-X TEG with R = 1.0 mm

- **Process/Manufacturing:**
  - Micrometer-scale rough surfaces between thermoelectric material and electrode reduce actual contact area and increase contact gap
  - Need to shift thermal stress from hot end to cold end to adapt to welding process

10_1016_j_finel_2015_11_001.key_1:

- **Material / Medium:** 
  - Mold insert: Uddeholm Impax Supreme (AISI P20) with temperature-dependent magnetic properties (α, β, γ coefficients)
  - Core materials: EPCOS Ferrite N27 and Höganäs Somaloy
  - Coil: Copper windings (50.6A at 11230Hz for pancake; 52.4A at 11700Hz for bulk)
  - Molded material: ABS with no-flow temperature of 111°C (glass transition temperature 94°C)
  - Other components: Stainless steel (core encasement), cement (coil encasement), water cooling
- **Application & Importance:** Rapid mold surface heating to prevent frozen layer development during filling, enable molding of thin features, avoid weld lines, and improve surface finish; heating must reach above 120°C at cavity surface while maintaining cycle time efficiency
- **Geometry / Domain:** 
  - Axisymmetric domain with cavity, coil, core, cooling channels, and moldbase
  - Bulk setup features eight windings inside ferrite core encasement
  - Pancake setup uses Litz wire in spiral path processed on Somaloy core
  - Skin depth effects require fine meshing in magnetic materials (δ = 1/√(πfμσ))
  - Boundary conditions: vanishing magnetic field at outer boundaries (A̅θ = 0), heat transfer coefficient of 1000 W/m²K at metal-metal interfaces, 260 W/m²K at mold halves interface
10_1016_j_finel_2015_11_001.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**
  - Electromagnetic: Vanishing magnetic field at outer boundary (A̅θ = 0) and at axis of rotation
  - Thermal: Adiabatic boundary at axis of rotation
  - Thermal: Heat transfer coefficient of 1000 W/m²K at metal-metal interfaces
  - Thermal: Heat transfer coefficient of 260 W/m²K at mold halves interface (y=10mm for pancake, y=44mm for bulk) due to 0.1mm air gap
  - Initial temperature: 25°C room temperature
  - Time step: 0.1s for thermal solution using implicit Euler formulation

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Pancake setup: 50.6A current at 11230Hz frequency
  - Bulk setup: 52.4A current at 11700Hz frequency
  - Heat source from induced Eddy currents (Q̇ = 0.5σ|J̄e|²)
  - Heating cycle: 7s on/19s off for pancake; 6s on/37s off for bulk
  - Cyclic heating/cooling until steady state reached (5 cycles required)

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Coil encasement (cement) insulating copper windings
  - Core encasement (stainless steel) containing flux concentrator
  - Magnetic mold tool steel (Uddeholm Impax Supreme) on top of flux concentrator
  - Cooling channel with water in opposing mold half
  - Thermal coupling between electromagnetic solution (heat source) and thermal solution

- **Simulation Type:**
  - 2D Axisymmetric finite element model
  - Transient electromagnetic-thermal coupled analysis
  - Non-linear magnetic properties using modified Fröhlich equation
  - Iterative procedure for fictitious linear permeability
  - Linear triangular elements (23,925 elements/12,063 nodes for bulk; 25,702/12,896 for pancake)
  - Time-harmonic electromagnetic approximation with transient thermal solution
  - Skin depth meshing requirement (at least three skin depths of fine mesh)
10_1016_j_finel_2015_11_001.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:**
  - Electromagnetic field distribution (Maxwell's equations with time-harmonic assumption)
  - Eddy current generation and Joule heating (Q̇ = 0.5σ|J̄e|²)
  - Transient heat conduction with temperature-dependent magnetic properties
  - Non-linear B-H curve behavior using modified Fröhlich equation (B = H/(α + β|H| + γ|H|) + μ₀H)
  - Cyclic heating/cooling behavior until reaching steady state

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**
  - Temperature distribution in mold insert (Figs. 7, 10)
  - Maximum temperature at cavity surface (P2 location)
  - Temperature at center of insert (P1 location)
  - Comparison between simulation and experimental temperature measurements
  - Power induced in the insert (773.0 W for pancake, 1177.8 W for bulk)
  - Fictitious linear permeability distribution (Figs. 9, 12)
  - Magnetic flux density and field lines (Figs. 9, 12)
  - Time to reach cyclic steady state (5 cycles required)

- **Optimization Goal:**
  - Achieve cavity surface temperature above 120°C (exceeding ABS no-flow temperature of 111°C)
  - Compare heating uniformity between bulk and pancake configurations
  - Validate simulation accuracy against experimental temperature measurements
  - Determine appropriate linear permeability values for non-linear materials (200-300 for insert, 500 for Somaloy, 1000 for ferrite)
  - Minimize temperature difference between simulation and experiment (achieved with <5°C error at P1)

  - Bulk setup must fit behind mold insert despite being "fairly large"

  - Cement insulation required around coil windings for electrical protection
  - Molded parts constrained to 15mm length and 3mm width dimensions
  - Maximum allowable temperature gradient must not cause weld lines in injection molding process

10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2020_105604.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Electrical discharge texturing (EDT) surface topography prediction model considering multi-discharge phenomenon; simulates progressive surface texture development due to sequential spark discharges on work material surface; focuses on crater formation, overlap, and surface roughness parameter prediction.

- **Material / Medium:** Work materials: Ti-6Al-4V, M300 steel, SS 304; temperature-dependent thermo-physical properties (density, thermal conductivity, specific heat); latent heat of melting considered; kerosene dielectric medium; heat convection coefficient h = 4.26 × 10³ W/m².K for kerosene (k = 0.145 W/m.K, characteristic length x = 500 μm, flow velocity v = 1 m/s).

- **Application & Importance:** Predicts surface roughness parameters (Sa, Ra) under different operating conditions; accounts for stochastic spark distribution in location, energy level, and chronological order; validates against experimental data with 6-17.5% prediction error for Ti-6Al-4V and M300 steel; enables understanding of how discharge current and pulse on-time affect surface texture.

- **Geometry / Domain:** Meshed rectangular block dimensions 400 × 400 × 300 μm³; top surface area 400 × 400 μm²; fine mesh size 4 × 4 × 4 μm³; coarse mesh size 4 × 4 × 10 μm³; craters modeled as hemi-ellipsoidal shapes; spark radius (r_g) calculated as r_g(t) = 0.0945Q⁰·⁶⁷t⁰·²⁹¹ for t_on < 100 μs and r_g(t) = 0.3609Q⁰·⁶⁷ for t_on ≥ 100 μs; discharge power Q = UI.
10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2020_105604.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**
  - Initial condition: at t = 0, T₀ = 298 K (ambient temperature)
  - Boundary condition during pulse on-time: heat flux applied within spark radius r_g, heat convection applied outside spark radius
  - Boundary condition during pulse off-time: heat convection applied from entire top surface
  - Elements with temperature exceeding evaporation temperature (T_evap) are flagged to prevent further heat flux application
  - Meshed rectangular block dimensions: 400 × 400 × 300 μm³
  - Top surface area: 400 × 400 μm²
  - Fine mesh size: 4 × 4 × 4 μm³; Coarse mesh size: 4 × 4 × 10 μm³
  - Element type: DC3D8 (8-node linear heat transfer brick)

- **Loads / Excitations:**

  - Discharge current (I), gap voltage (V), pulse on-time (t_on) as input parameters
  - Energy level fraction (e) with random value between 0.6 and 1
  - Cathode energy fraction (F_C) values: 0.109 for E = 0-50 mJ, 0.187 for E = 50-100 mJ, 0.256 for E > 100 mJ
  - Plasma flushing efficiency (PFE) = 0.1093 + 2.238×10⁻²×I - 8.441×10⁻⁴×t_on - 4.67×10⁻⁵×I×t_on + 4.912×10⁻⁶×t_on²
  - Heat convection coefficient h = 4.26×10³ W/m²·K (for kerosene dielectric)
  - Spark radius equation: r_g(t) = 0.0945Q⁰·⁶⁷t⁰·²⁹¹ for t_on < 100 μs and r_g(t) = 0.3609Q⁰·⁶⁷ for t_on ≥ 100 μs (Q = UI)
  - Total time period t_total and time step t_step (with minimum and maximum values)

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Heat conduction within solid work material
  - Heat convection at top surface
  - No radiation heat loss considered
  - Sequential spark application on dynamically changing surface (each new spark acts on the instantaneous textured surface from previous sparks)
  - Crater overlap conditions: no overlap (center-to-center distance > sum of crater radii), touching boundaries (center-to-center distance = sum of crater radii), and overlap (center-to-center distance < sum of crater radii)
  - Maximum crater overlap when center-to-center distance = R_C1 + r_g (R_C2 - r_g overlap distance)

- **Simulation Type:**

  - 3D finite element simulation
  - Multi-spark simulation with stochastic distribution in location, energy level, and chronological order
  - Implemented in ABAQUS with user-defined subroutines (DFLUX, USDFLD)
  - Time step-based progression until t = t_total
  - Element type DC3D8 (8-node linear heat transfer brick)

- **Loads / Excitations:** Thrust force (150-1200 N); feed rate (0.075, 0.188, 0.300, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 mm/rev); cutting speed (45 m/min, 65 m/min, 2250 rpm); active backup force applied to counteract push-out delamination; depth of cut (0.1, 0.2, 0.3 mm/rev)
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Tool-workpiece contact at cutting edge; fiber-matrix interface interaction; friction between tool rake face and material; peel-up delamination at entry surface; push-down delamination at exit surface; chip formation at fiber/matrix interface; different damage mechanisms based on fiber orientation (0°: high compression/bending; 90°: mode I fracture; 45°: fiber stretching/shearing; -45°: fiber pull-out)

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Delamination factor (F_d = D_max/D_nom); thrust force (150-1200 N); torque (0.29-0.3 N-m); Stress-XX distribution (up to 800 MPa); matrix damage distribution; fiber fracture patterns; cutting force and feed force; Tsai Wu failure criteria values; surface roughness; chip formation characteristics; damage progression at 35μm scale
- **Optimization Goal:** Minimize delamination (60-80% reduction achievable with active backup force); reduce thrust force (directly correlated with delamination extent); optimize drill point angles (90°, 104°, 118°); minimize surface roughness; improve hole quality and part performance; reduce delamination factor (target values: twist drill-2.86, jodrill-2.53, trepanning tool-2.03); optimize feed rate (0.075-1.0 mm/rev) and spindle speed parameters for minimal damage

- **Material / Medium:** Discontinuous diffusion coefficient β(x) with β₁ = 1 in Ω₁ and β₂ = 10 or 100 in Ω₂
- **Application & Importance:** Modeling electrokinetic flow and mass transfer through semipermeable membranes in material sciences, biomedical, and chemical engineering
- **Geometry / Domain:** Bounded convex polygonal domain in ℝ² with polygonal interface Γ separating Ω into Ω₁ and Ω₂
- **Boundary Conditions:** u = 0 on ∂Ω; [u] = 0 and [β∂u/∂n] = g(x,t) ≠ 0 on interface Γ
- **Mesh Characteristics:** Adaptive triangular mesh with higher element density around interface; initial mesh size h = 0.1
- **Time Discretization:** Backward Euler method with time step k = 0.5 × h for convergence studies
- **Tolerance Parameters:** Mesh adaptation tolerance ϵ = 0.01 or 0.03 for different test cases
- **Test Cases:** Straight interface (Figs. 1-3) and polygonal (square) interface (Figs. 4-6) at time t = 0.01
- **Solution Behavior:** Numerical solution exhibits peak values at interface regions as shown in 3D surface plots
10_1016_j_apnum_2020_03_001.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** u = 0 on ∂Ω_T; [u] = 0 on interface Γ; [β∂u/∂n] = g(x,t) on interface Γ; u(x,0) = u₀(x) in Ω
- **Loads / Excitations:** Source function f(x,t,u) satisfying Lipschitz condition; nonzero flux jump function g(x,t) with g ≠ 0; initial condition u₀(x) ∈ H¹(Ω)
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Polygonal interface Γ separating domain Ω into subdomains Ω₁ and Ω₂; discontinuous diffusion coefficient β(x) with β₁ = 1 in Ω₁ and β₂ = 10 or 100 in Ω₂
- **Simulation Type:** Transient two-dimensional semilinear parabolic interface problem; adaptive finite element method with backward Euler time discretization; linearized fully discrete scheme; space-time adaptive algorithm with tolerance values ϵ = 0.01 or 0.03
10_1016_j_apnum_2020_03_001.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Semilinear parabolic interface problem with discontinuous diffusion coefficient; modeling electrokinetic flow and mass transfer through semipermeable membranes
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Energy error (Err); a posteriori error estimator (η); effective index (Q_ind = η/Err); experimental order of convergence (EOC); number of triangles (N_K); number of vertices (N_v); discrete solution distribution
- **Optimization Goal:** Adaptive mesh refinement to equidistribute error with tolerance values (ϵ = 0.01 or 0.03); concentrate mesh density around interface Γ; achieve optimal convergence rate for error estimator (EOC approaching 1); minimize computational cost while maintaining solution accuracy within specified tolerance
10_1016_j_apnum_2020_03_001.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Domain Ω must be bounded convex polygonal in ℝ² with Lipschitz boundary; interface Γ must be polygonal; each triangle in mesh must be entirely in Ω₁, entirely in Ω₂, or intersect Γ at most at two vertices; mesh refinement uses bisection algorithm without coarsening
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Diffusion coefficient β(x) must be positive (β₁, β₂ ∈ ℝ⁺); source function f must satisfy Lipschitz condition with C_L > 0; flux jump g ≠ 0 must be nonzero; initial condition u₀(x) ∈ H¹(Ω); g and ∂g/∂t ∈ L²(0,T; L²(Γ)); bilinear form must be continuous and coercive; time step constrained to k = 0.5 × h for convergence studies
- **Process/Manufacturing:** Tolerances ε_time and ε_space set equal (ε = 0.01 or 0.03); all estimator constants taken as 1; parameter γ₁ = 0.5 used in adaptive algorithm; mesh coarsening not implemented in numerical experiments; computations performed using FreeFem++ software; domain must be convex for analysis validity

10_1016_j_engstruct_2025_120616.key_1:

• Material / Medium: 316L stainless steel with properties: 8000 kg/m³ density, 440 MPa yield stress, 180,000 MPa Young's modulus, 0.25 Poisson's ratio; powder particle size 13-50 μm

• Application & Importance: Energy absorption in aerospace, automotive, and marine engineering; designed as lightweight protective structures for landing pads, crashworthy seats, satellite shields, and automotive energy-absorbing components

• Geometry / Domain: Unit cell width fixed at 5 mm with heights of 2.5 mm (aspect ratio 0.5), 5 mm (aspect ratio 1.0), and 7.5 mm (aspect ratio 1.5); strut diameter 0.7 mm; FHS structures incorporate FCCZ diagonal reinforcement while HS structures are conventional honeycomb; relative volume fractions: FHS0.5 (29.9%), FHS1.0 (24.1%), FHS1.5 (21.7%), HS0.5 (16.5%), HS1.0 (11.3%), HS1.5 (9.5%)
10_1016_j_engstruct_2025_120616.key_2:

• Loads / Excitations: Pendulum impact velocity of 3 m/s; Drop-weight impact velocity of 4.52 m/s; Compressive stress applied along Z-axis direction; Impact hammer as loading mechanism; Compressive strain levels of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 in simulation studies

• Interactions / Interfaces: General contact with friction coefficient of 0.4; Surface-to-surface contact between impactor and lattice structure; Tangential friction coefficient of 0.2; Lattice structure tied to rigid plate; Hard normal contact conditions; Friction coefficient of 0.2 between impactor and structure

10_1016_j_jcsr_2025_109640.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Shear key double-layer grouting connection (SK-DGC) for modular steel structural joints
- **Material / Medium:** Q355B steel (6-20 mm thickness, E_s: 193-218 GPa, f_y: 346-472 MPa, ε_y: 0.18-0.23%, f_u: 520-618 MPa, δ: 12.2-26.8%); Cementitious grout (compressive strength: 45.0 MPa, tensile strength: 3.0 MPa, elastic modulus: 37,202 MPa)
- **Application & Importance:** Seismic-resistant connection for modular steel structures providing faster assembly efficiency, greater installation tolerance, non-invasive decoration preservation, and superior mechanical properties compared to traditional connections
- **Geometry / Domain:** T-shaped full-scale joints with 200×200×10 mm square tube columns, 194×150×6×9 mm H-shaped beams; Double-layer grouting with nested sleeves (small sleeve inside column, large sleeve outside); Semicircular shear keys (R=4 mm) spaced 40 mm apart; Grouting holes at bottom and overflow holes at top; Modular units: 6 m length, 4 m width, 3 m height
10_1016_j_jcsr_2025_109640.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Column base hinged to ground steel beam allowing in-plane rotation; Beam end hinged to support chain rod allowing in-plane translation and rotation; Pin beneath column bottom base supports only dead load; No out-of-plane bracing required; Axial pressure maintained at constant 675 kN (axial compression ratio 0.2); Displacement control with 11 loading stages (0.25%, 0.5%, 0.75%, 1.0%, 1.5%, 2.0%, 2.5%, 3.0%, 4.0%, 5.0%, 6.0% drift ratios); Test termination criteria include horizontal load decrease to 0.85 of maximum value, structural failure, significant local deformation, or inability to maintain axial pressure
- **Loads / Excitations:** Axial compression load of 675 kN; Horizontal cyclic displacement-controlled loading with 2 cycles per stage; Push direction defined as lower beam part under tension; Pull direction defined as upper beam part under tension
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Double-layer grout filling space between module column, large sleeve, and small sleeve; Semicircular shear keys (R=4 mm) welded on inner column wall, inner/outer large sleeve, and outer small sleeve; Grouting holes at bottom and overflow holes at top of column/sleeve; Welded connections between beam flange and column clapboard; Contact between beam and column connection components
- **Simulation Type:** Quasi-static testing; 3D nonlinear finite element analysis; Abaqus model using eight-node solid elements (C3D8R); Displacement-controlled loading; Concrete damaged plasticity (CDP) model for grout; Nonlinear material behavior with large deformation considerations
10_1016_j_jcsr_2025_109640.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Seismic behavior of modular steel structural joints under cyclic loading; Hysteresis characteristics; Ductility performance; Energy dissipation mechanisms; Failure modes including column wall tearing and beam flange buckling; Nonlinear structural response under displacement-controlled quasi-static testing
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Bending moment vs. drift ratio (hysteresis and skeleton curves); Yield bending moment (115.1-181.1 kN·m); Maximum bending moment (123.2-194.8 kN·m); Initial rotational stiffness (9,248-15,347 kN·m/rad); Ductility coefficient (1.96-3.26); Equivalent viscous damping coefficient (0.36-0.59); Energy dissipation (40.97-47.94 kJ); Classification as semi-rigid joints (S_j,ini/S_pinned: 7.80-16.27); Classification as full-strength (M_max/M_p: 1.04-1.06) or partial-strength joints (M_max/M_p: 0.69-0.78)
- **Optimization Goal:** Maximize seismic performance while minimizing construction cost; Reduce column wall tearing through increased wall thickness; Maintain appropriate ductility (target μ > 2.0); Achieve balanced push-pull behavior through symmetric grouting; Reduce axial compression ratio to improve drift capacity; Optimize parameters with minimal seismic impact (grout strength, sleeve thickness, shear key dimensions) to lower costs while maintaining required mechanical performance
10_1016_j_jcsr_2025_109640.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Modular unit dimensions limited to 6 m length × 4 m width × 3 m height due to transportation constraints; Column section constrained to SHS 200×200×10 mm; Beam section constrained to H 194×150×6×9 mm; Shear key radius fixed at 4 mm with spacing of 40 mm; RBS beam section reduction must comply with JGJ 99-2015 specifications; Modular column constructed from U-shaped plate + flat plate rather than finished square pipe due to shear key welding requirements; Grouting holes must be positioned at bottom with overflow holes at top
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Axial compression ratio constrained to maximum 0.2 (675 kN) to maintain drift ratio requirements; Test termination occurs when horizontal load decreases to 0.85 of maximum value; Ductility coefficient must exceed 1.96-3.26 to meet seismic performance requirements; Yield strength safety factor must maintain structural integrity at drift ratios up to 6%; Column wall tearing must be controlled to prevent structural failure; Connection must maintain semi-rigid joint classification (S_j,ini/S_pinned ≥ 7.80) and either full-strength (M_max/M_p ≥ 1.04) or partial-strength (M_max/M_p ≥ 0.69) classification
- **Process/Manufacturing:** Steel material limited to Q355B grade with thicknesses from 6-20 mm; Grout must meet GB 50448-2015 cementitious grout specifications (45.0 MPa compressive strength); Welding must accommodate two full-length welds on beam connection side of module column; Shear keys must be semicircular and welded at equal intervals; Grouting process requires sequential installation of lower column, connector, and upper column followed by grout injection until overflow; Asymmetric grouting connection causes push-pull imbalance and should be avoided; Column wall thickness must be sufficient to prevent tearing while maintaining cost efficiency
