- **Material / Medium:** Thermoplastic Polyurethane (TPU) with Young's modulus E = 32 MPa, density ρ = 1.22 × 10⁻³ g/cm³, Poisson's ratio λ = 0.47; Hei-Cast 8400 silicone rubber filler (30 A hardness) with Young's modulus E = 1.15 MPa, density ρ = 1.1 × 10⁻³ g/cm³, Poisson's ratio λ = 0.45.

- **Application & Importance:** Energy absorption in aerospace, transportation, and civil engineering applications; protection of internal structures (e.g., fuel tanks, electronics); reusable energy-absorbing structures with elastic recovery properties.

- **Geometry / Domain:** Cylindrical structure with outer diameter D_out = 120 mm, inner diameter d_in = 60 mm, thickness t = 30 mm; 19 tessellation patterns (11 "(i)" and 10 "(ii)" variants); four radial layers with variable heights; cross-section formed by circular mapping of 2D tessellation patterns; loading cases: (I) TCOM alone under lateral compression; (II) TCOM with 5 mm wall-thickness filler inserted at center.
10_1016_j_compstruct_2025_119182.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Bottom rigid plate fixed; top rigid plate displacement-controlled; D_out = 120 mm, d_in = 60 mm; friction coefficient of 0.3 between rigid plates and metamaterial; hard contact condition; filler with 5 mm wall thickness inserted in center for loading case II; four radial layers with variable heights (h₁=4.5 mm, h₂=6.5 mm, h₃=8.5 mm, h₄=10.5 mm) for variable height design.

- **Loads / Excitations:** Displacement-controlled loading at 20 mm/min rate; lateral compression up to 36 mm (30% of D_out); axial compression with 50 mm displacement control for honeycomb comparison; rotation angle α = 1°, 3°, 5°; translation distance d = 5 mm, 7.5 mm, 10 mm between design planes.

- **Interactions / Interfaces:** General contact between metamaterial and rigid plates; filler inserted in central cavity with 5 mm wall thickness; tie constraint between TCOM and solid cylinder in protection testing; friction coefficient of 0.3 specified for contact surfaces.

- **Simulation Type:** ABAQUS/EXPLICIT finite element analysis; quasi-static lateral compression; S4R shell elements for meshing; linear elastic material model; 3D structural analysis; experimental validation with 3D-printed TPU specimens.
10_1016_j_compstruct_2025_119182.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Mechanical deformation of thick-wall cylindrical origami metamaterials under lateral compression; energy absorption behavior during quasi-static loading; structural response including force-displacement characteristics and deformation patterns.

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Specific Energy Absorption (SEA) in J/g; Energy Absorption (EA) in J; force-displacement curves; shape-maintenance performance (e = 1 - b²/a² where a and b are semi-major and semi-minor axes of fitting ellipse); force protection performance (maximum stress σ_c_max around protected object); crushing force efficiency (CFE); equivalent plateau stress.

- **Optimization Goal:** To develop a programmable inverse design tool that predicts the geometric parameters (rotation angle α: 1°-5°, translation distance d: 5-10 mm) and tessellation pattern type (1 of 19 configurations) that achieves a user-specified SEA value; to balance energy absorption capacity with protection performance in cylindrical origami metamaterials.
10_1016_j_compstruct_2025_119182.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Outer diameter D_out = 120 mm; inner diameter d_in = 60 mm; total thickness t = 30 mm; four radial layers with variable heights (h₁=4.5 mm, h₂=6.5 mm, h₃=8.5 mm, h₄=10.5 mm) for variable height design; uniform layer height of 7.5 mm for equal height design; rotation angle α constrained to 1°, 3°, 5°; translation distance d constrained to 5 mm, 7.5 mm, 10 mm; 36 circumferential tessellated units; maximum compression distance of 36 mm (30% of D_out).

- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Maximum strain during loading does not exceed TPU elasticity limit; displacement loading rate of 20 mm/min; loading displacement constrained to s_max = 30% of D_out (36 mm); linear elastic material behavior assumed for both TPU and silicone rubber; contact with friction coefficient of 0.3 between rigid plates and metamaterial; general contact with hard contact condition.

- **Process/Manufacturing:** Specimens manufactured via 3D printing (Bambu Lab P1P) using TPU material; filler manufactured via 3D printing using Hei-Cast 8400 silicone rubber; wall thickness of test specimen constrained to 1.0 mm; experimental specimens have 18 circumferential tessellated units for energy absorption testing and 36 units for protection testing; four layers in total for all specimens; geometric constraints to maintain minimum distortion of tessellated units during circular mapping; 21 possible tessellation patterns (11 "(i)" and 10 "(ii)" variants) with only 19 used in parametric study (excluding "3.3.3.3.6" variants due to lack of concentric circle "neutral axis").

10_1016_j_renene_2025_123459.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Unitized Regenerative Fuel Cell (URFC) with focus on Porous Transport Layer (PTL) under clamping pressure effects

- **Material / Medium:**
  - O-PTL (Oxygen side): Titanium felt
  - H-PTL (Hydrogen side): Carbon paper
  - PEM (Proton Exchange Membrane)
  - O-CL (Oxygen Catalytic Layer), H-CL (Hydrogen Catalytic Layer)
  - O-GC (Oxygen Gas Channel), H-GC (Hydrogen Gas Channel)
  - O-BP (Oxygen Bipolar Plate), H-BP (Hydrogen Bipolar Plate)

- **Application & Importance:**
  - Optimization of PTL structural properties to enhance URFC performance
  - Improvement of water-gas transport characteristics under different operating modes
  - Enhancement of round-trip efficiency in bidirectional energy conversion
  - Reduction of contact resistance while maintaining adequate gas diffusion

- **Geometry / Domain:**
  - Two-dimensional finite element model of PTL deformation under clamping pressure
  - Three-dimensional unitized regenerative fuel cell model with straight channel (50 mm length, 1 mm width)
  - PTL structural parameters: porosity (ε_O-PTL, ε_H-PTL) ranging 0.3-0.7, thickness (H_O-PTL, H_H-PTL) ranging 0.3-0.6 mm
  - Clamping pressure range: 0-3 MPa
  - Layered structure with deformation under compression (O-PTL shows less deformation than H-PTL)
  - Six labeled surfaces in 3D model (Surface 1-6) representing different components and interfaces
10_1016_j_renene_2025_123459.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**
  - Electric current at Surface 1: normali normals = normali 0 true( EC true) / − normali 0 true( F C true)
  - Electric ground at Surface 2: ϕ normals = 0
  - Gas species concentration at Surface 3: C_O2_in = 0, C_H2O(g)_in = 0 (EC mode) / C_O2_in = P_in − 100% · P_sat/RT, C_H2O(g)_in = RH · P_sat/RT (FC mode)
  - Gas species concentration at Surface 5: C_H2_in = 0, C_H2O(g)_in = 0 (EC mode) / C_H2_in = P_in − 100% · P_sat/RT, C_H2O(g)_in = RH · P_sat/RT (FC mode)
  - Zero flux at Surfaces 4 & 6: −n · D_normali · ∇c_normali = 0
  - Laminar inlet velocity at Surface 3: v_a,in = 0.2 m/s (EC mode) / v_a,in = ξ_a i_0 A_act/(4F C_O2,in A_ch) (FC mode)
  - Laminar inlet velocity at Surface 5: v_c,in = 0 m/s (EC mode) / v_c,in = ξ_c i_0 A_act/(2F C_H2,in A_ch) (FC mode)
  - Pressure outlet at Surfaces 4 & 6: p_a = p_c = 1 atm
  - Constant temperature at Surfaces 3 & 5: T_in = 353 K
  - Constant wall temperature at Surfaces 1 & 2: T_0 = 353 K
  - Heat flow outlet at Surfaces 4 & 6: −n · q = 0
  - Liquid water saturation at Surface 3: s_a,in = 0.9 (EC mode) / s_a,in = 0.1 (FC mode)
  - Liquid water saturation at Surface 5: s_c,in = 0
  - Zero flux for liquid water at Surfaces 4 & 6: −n · D_normali · ∇s = 0
  - Symmetric constraints applied to side walls in 2D model
  - Contact pairs between bipolar plates and PTL

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Clamping pressure: 1 MPa, 2 MPa, and 3 MPa applied to bipolar plates
  - Current density: 1.5 A/cm² (EC mode), 0.8 A/cm² (FC mode)
  - Inlet gas velocities: 0.2 m/s (EC mode oxygen side), 0 m/s (EC mode hydrogen side)
  - Operating temperature: 353 K

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Contact interface between O-BP and O-PTL (titanium felt)
  - Contact interface between H-BP and H-PTL (carbon paper)
  - Fluid-structure interaction due to clamping pressure affecting PTL properties
  - Multiphysics coupling between mechanical deformation and electrochemical performance
  - Contact resistance at BP/PTL interfaces dependent on clamping pressure
  - Asymmetric mechanical behavior between O-PTL and H-PTL under clamping pressure

- **Simulation Type:**
  - Two-dimensional finite element model (2D FEM) for mechanical deformation analysis
  - Three-dimensional two-phase electrochemical model for performance analysis
  - Steady-state flow assumption (laminar flow)
  - Multiphysics coupling of solid mechanics, electrochemistry, two-phase flow, and heat transfer
  - "Water-gas-electric-heat-force" coupling regime
  - Grid independence verified with 16,286 elements for 2D model and 66,000 elements for 3D model
  - Response surface methodology (RSM), artificial neural network (ANN), and NSGA-II for optimization
10_1016_j_renene_2025_123459.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** 
  - Multiphysics coupling of mechanical deformation, water-gas transport, electrochemical reactions, and thermal behavior
  - Two-phase flow dynamics (liquid water and gas) in porous media
  - Structural deformation of PTL under clamping pressure
  - Electrochemical performance in both electrolysis (EC) and fuel cell (FC) modes
  - Contact resistance variations due to compression

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** 
  - Voltage in EC mode (V_EC) at 1.5 A/cm²
  - Voltage in FC mode (V_FC) at 0.8 A/cm²
  - Input power density (W_EC = V_EC·i) in electrolysis mode
  - Output power density (W_FC = V_FC·i) in fuel cell mode
  - Round-trip efficiency (RTE)
  - Liquid water saturation distribution
  - Oxygen concentration distribution
  - Effective conductivity of PTL
  - Effective permeability of PTL
  - Porosity distribution
  - Contact resistance between BP and PTL

- **Optimization Goal:** 
  - Minimize input voltage in EC mode while maximizing output voltage in FC mode
  - Maximize round-trip efficiency (14.13% improvement achieved)
  - Increase input power density (4.08% improvement achieved)
  - Increase output power density (9.47% improvement achieved)
  - Optimize PTL structural parameters (ε_O-PTL, ε_H-PTL, H_O-PTL, H_H-PTL) and clamping pressure (Fc) for balanced performance across both operational modes
10_1016_j_renene_2025_123459.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**
  - O-PTL porosity (ε_O-PTL) constrained to range 0.3-0.7
  - H-PTL porosity (ε_H-PTL) constrained to range 0.3-0.7
  - O-PTL thickness (H_O-PTL) constrained to range 0.3-0.6 mm
  - H-PTL thickness (H_H-PTL) constrained to range 0.3-0.6 mm
  - Channel width fixed at 1 mm with length of 50 mm (50× longer than width)
  - 2D simplification applied since assembly stress doesn't propagate in flow direction
  - Box-Behnken Design parameters with specific discrete values for optimization

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - Clamping pressure constrained to 0-3 MPa range
  - Operating temperature fixed at 353 K (80°C)
  - Electrolysis mode evaluated at 1.5 A/cm² current density
  - Fuel cell mode evaluated at 0.8 A/cm² current density
  - Maximum voltage deviation <0.05% for 3D model mesh independence (66,000 elements)
  - Maximum stress deviation <0.03% for 2D model mesh independence (16,286 elements)
  - Excessive clamping pressure (>3 MPa) may significantly reduce porosity under ribs, hindering bubble separation
  - Study limited to low-to-medium current density operation

- **Process/Manufacturing:**
  - O-PTL material constrained to titanium felt
  - H-PTL material constrained to carbon paper
  - PTL assumed to be elastic with isotropic transport properties
  - Clamping pressure assumed uniformly distributed on bipolar plate surfaces
  - Bending stress effects neglected in analysis
  - Hygrothermal effects on solid mechanics neglected
  - Study limited to specific material properties of titanium felt (O-PTL) and carbon paper (H-PTL)
  - No consideration of manufacturing tolerances or variations in PTL production
  - Model assumes steady-state laminar flow conditions

10_1016_j_fusengdes_2025_114807.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Main heater and primary mixer components in high-temperature PbLi loop for CFETR COOL blanket system
- **Material / Medium:** PbLi fluid (300°C–700°C operating range); structural materials: N08810 (main heater), N06625, S31600 stainless steel (≤550°C), tungsten; nickel-based alloys used for sections >550°C
- **Application & Importance:** Critical components operating at maximum temperature (700°C) requiring thermal-mechanical analysis to ensure structural integrity; main heater heats PbLi to 700°C (1 MW capacity), primary mixer cools from 700°C to 550°C
- **Geometry / Domain:** Main heater: three 310 mm inner diameter shells (28 mm wall thickness, 2800 mm total length) with 12 baffle plates per shell and 60 heating rods; primary mixer: two designs with shell inner diameters 127-170 mm, wall thickness 15-16 mm, length 600-690 mm; design one features nozzle with 10 small holes, design two includes internal tube with helical structure
10_1016_j_fusengdes_2025_114807.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**
  - Gravity: 9806.6 mm/s² (Standard Earth Gravity)
  - Pressure: 2.0 MPa applied to fluid-solid interface (conservative estimate)
  - Remote displacements used instead of saddle and spring hanger assemblies for main heater support
  - One saddle fully constrained in all DOF, other saddle allowing displacement along z-axis
  - Spring hanger connection assemblies with displacements set along y-axis and z-axis based on thermal expansion
  - For primary mixer: circumferential constraint at both ends with radial freedom; one end fixed axially, other free axially
  - Heat dissipation: -558.25 W/m² on main heater outer surface, -732.794 W/m² on primary mixer outer surface

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Main heater total heat power: 1.2 MW (operating power 1 MW)
  - Heating rod heat flux: 287,542.8059 W/m² (middle/lower shells), 158,148.5433 W/m² (upper shell)
  - Main heater inlet: 533°C temperature, 32 kg/s mass flow rate
  - Primary mixer hot inlet: 700°C, 32 kg/s
  - Primary mixer cold inlet: 300°C (19.2 kg/s), with cases analyzing 350°C, 400°C, and 450°C
  - Fluid inlet boundary conditions specified for mass flow rate and temperature

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - One-way fluid-structure coupling between CFD and FEA
  - Fluid-solid interface as heat transfer boundary
  - Shared topology with co-nodal mesh on common surfaces
  - Temperature field from CFD used as thermal load in FEA
  - Deformable coupling for remote displacements

- **Simulation Type:**
  - Steady-state analysis (Time: 1 in multiple figures)
  - 3D modeling (evident from all visualizations)
  - Thermal-mechanical analysis with stress linearization
  - ASME VIII-2 and ASME III-5 stress evaluation standards
  - CFD for temperature field calculation followed by FEA for stress field
10_1016_j_fusengdes_2025_114807.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:**
  - Thermal-hydraulic behavior of PbLi fluid (300°C–700°C range)
  - One-way coupled thermal-mechanical stress analysis
  - Structural deformation under thermal gradients and pressure loading
  - Stress distribution in critical regions using von-Mises and maximum principal stress criteria

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**
  - Equivalent (von-Mises) stress distributions with maximum values (e.g., 38.783 MPa for main heater primary stress)
  - Linearized stress components (Pm, PL, Pb, Q) along critical paths
  - Temperature fields for both PbLi and structural components
  - Allowable stress limits based on ASME standards at operating temperatures
  - Stress margins against 3S, 1.5S, and Sm criteria
  - Outlet temperature distribution uniformity (maximum temperature difference requirement <40°C)

- **Optimization Goal:**
  - Achieve structural integrity by meeting ASME VIII-2 and ASME III-5 stress evaluation criteria
  - Reduce thermal stress in regions exceeding allowable limits (e.g., heating rods with 57.6% overstress)
  - Improve primary mixer outlet temperature uniformity (reduce temperature difference to <40°C)
  - Optimize through structural design modifications, material selection (N06625 vs. tungsten), and increasing cold PbLi inlet temperature
  - Ensure safe operation at maximum 700°C while maintaining PbLi loop functionality
10_1016_j_fusengdes_2025_114807.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**
  - Main heater shell inner diameter: 310 mm, wall thickness: 28 mm, length: 2800 mm
  - Main heater nozzle inner diameter: 65 mm, length: 250/685 mm
  - Main heater baffle diameter: 308 mm, spacing: 200 mm
  - Main heater heating rod outer diameter: 25 mm, thickness: 3.5 mm
  - Primary mixer design one: shell inner diameter 127 mm, wall thickness 16 mm, length 600 mm
  - Primary mixer design two: shell inner diameter 170 mm, wall thickness 15 mm, length 690 mm
  - Final design modification: helical extended by 260 mm, outlet nozzle extended by 200 mm
  - Heating bundles have 0.5 mm gap between them and baffle plates in actual manufacturing

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - PbLi operating temperature range: 300°C–700°C
  - Material temperature limit: 900°C for N08810 (not exceeded in calculations)
  - ASME VIII-2 criteria: Pm ≤ S, PL+Pb ≤ 1.5S, PL+Pb+Q ≤ 3S
  - ASME III-5 criteria: Pm ≤ Smt, PL+Pb ≤ KS, PL+Pb/Kt ≤ St
  - Allowable stress values specific to each material at operating temperatures (e.g., N08810 at 700°C: S=33.6 MPa)
  - Outlet temperature difference requirement: <40°C (10% of 400°C temperature difference between hot and cold inlets)
  - Maximum operating pressure: 2.0 MPa (conservative estimate)

- **Process/Manufacturing:**
  - Heating bundles are not rigidly fixed to baffle plates but have 0.5 mm gap between them
  - Stress concentration around notches can be mitigated by localized smoothing during fabrication
  - Tungsten presents challenges during machining and welding
  - N06625 is easier to handle than tungsten
  - Baffle structure capable of safe operation for up to 3×10⁴ hours
  - Allowable stress margin as low as 1.45% for some components (baffle plate)

10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2025_110483.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Nano-cutting process of nanocrystalline Ni-based superalloy (NCNBS) using molecular dynamics simulations to analyze plastic deformation mechanisms
- **Material / Medium:** NCNBS workpiece (51% Ni, 32% Fe, 17% Cr) with FCC structure (lattice constant 3.52 Å); diamond cutting tool (lattice constant 3.57 Å); workpiece dimensions 299.2 Å × 140.8 Å × 140.8 Å with grain numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50
- **Application & Importance:** Understanding atomic-scale material removal mechanisms for ultra-precision manufacturing of turbine blade components where NCNBS exhibits superior high-temperature creep, corrosion, oxidation, and fatigue resistance
- **Geometry / Domain:** Diamond tool with 0° rake angle, 15° clearance angle, and 30 Å edge radius interacting with NCNBS workpiece; periodic boundary conditions along y-direction, non-periodic along x- and z-directions; workpiece contains boundary, thermostatic, and Newtonian atomic layers; cutting depths of 0.5-3 nm and velocities of 50-400 m/s investigated
10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2025_110483.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Periodic boundary condition along y-direction; non-periodic boundary conditions along x- and z-directions; workpiece structured as boundary, thermostatic, and Newtonian atomic layers; 297 K temperature; 1 fs timestep; NVT ensemble for 100 ps relaxation; NVE ensemble during cutting simulation; Berendsen thermostatic dynamics applied to thermostat atomic layer; Newtonian atomic layer follows classical Newtonian kinematics
- **Loads / Excitations:** Cutting depths of 0.5, 1, 2, and 3 nm; cutting velocities of 50, 100, 200, and 400 m/s; tool rake angle of 0°; tool clearance angle of 15°; tool edge radius of 30 Å; nanoindentation loads of 25, 50, and 75 mN (P_max)
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Workpiece atoms modeled using EAM potential; workpiece-tool interactions described by Morse potential; grain boundaries present in nanocrystalline workpieces; triple junctions at grain boundary intersections; dislocations including Perfect (1/2<110>), Shockley (1/6<112>), Frank (1/6<111>), Stair-rod (1/6<110>), and Hirth (1/3<100>); stacking faults (intrinsic/extrinsic) and twinning observed at machining surfaces and grain boundaries
- **Simulation Type:** Molecular dynamics simulation; 3D domain; transient (time-dependent) simulation; NVE ensemble employed throughout cutting simulation; LAMMPS software used for simulation; OVITO software used for visualization; 1 fs time step
10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2025_110483.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Contact-induced plastic deformation mechanisms during nano-cutting of nanocrystalline materials; atomic-scale material removal processes; grain boundary-mediated deformation; dislocation nucleation, motion, and interaction; stress/strain propagation; crystal structure transformation (FCC to HCP); temperature distribution in nanoscale cutting
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Cutting forces (tangential and thrust); friction coefficient; surface roughness (Ra); chip height (H_max) and pile-up height (h_max); number of chip atoms; FCC and HCP atom counts; total dislocation line length; von Mises stress (VMS) and von Mises shear strain (VMSS); temperature distribution; grain boundary behavior parameters; triple junction migration/rotation; atomic displacement patterns
- **Optimization Goal:** Reduce surface roughness and cutting forces through grain refinement; establish parameter selection frameworks for ultra-precision manufacturing; achieve surface roughness reduction of 14.05% and thrust force reduction of 17.27% via grain refinement; understand velocity-dependent dislocation suppression to minimize subsurface damage
10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2025_110483.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Workpiece dimensions fixed at 299.2 Å × 140.8 Å × 140.8 Å; grain numbers limited to 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50; cutting depths constrained to 0.5, 1, 2, and 3 nm; cutting velocities restricted to 50, 100, 200, and 400 m/s; tool edge radius fixed at 30 Å; tool rake angle fixed at 0°; tool clearance angle fixed at 15°; periodic boundary condition along y-direction only
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Maximum temperature reaching 1200 K in contact regions; simulation temperature maintained at 297 K; timestep fixed at 1 fs; maximum indentation loads of 25, 50, and 75 mN; cutting distance limited to 20 nm; Newtonian atomic layer used to ensure effective external heat transfer due to minimal dissipation in nanoscale cutting; stable cutting stage defined from 6 to 20 nm
- **Process/Manufacturing:** Workpiece composition constrained to 51% Ni, 32% Fe, and 17% Cr; potential functions for existing Ni-Fe-Cr ternary alloys cannot accurately simulate actual nano-cutting; energy minimization performed via conjugate gradient method; 100 ps relaxation period at 297 K under NVT ensemble required prior to cutting simulation; atomic relaxation time reduced at higher cutting velocities limiting dislocation slip mechanisms

10_1016_j_est_2024_115094.key_1:
- Shell-and-tube latent heat thermal energy storage (LHTES) system with I-shaped copper fins
- Phase Change Material: RT35 (melting temperature 300.15 K/27°C, latent heat 179 kJ/kg)
- Fin material: Copper (density 8920 kg/m³, thermal conductivity 401 W/m·K, specific heat 380 J/kg·K)
- Shell material: Plexiglas (density 1180 kg/m³, thermal conductivity 0.19 W/m·K, specific heat 1460 J/kg·K)
- PCM properties: density 760 kg/m³ (liquid)/870 kg/m³ (solid), thermal conductivity 0.24 W/m·K (liquid)/0.15 W/m·K (solid), specific heat 1800 J/kg·K (liquid)/2400 J/kg·K (solid)
- Geometric dimensions: base length R₂ = 54.5 mm, top length R₁ = 77 mm, fin length L_fin = 25 mm, thickness η = 2 mm, inner tube radius R_in = 36.5 mm, outer shell radius R_out = 95 mm
- System analyzed with parametric variations of dR₁/dR₂ ratio (where dR₁ = R_out - R₁, dR₂ = R_in + R₂) and α₁/α₂ curvature ratio
- Comparison with three conventional fin types: honeycomb, longitudinal, and circular
- Mesh independence established with 22,141 elements, time step of 0.2 s
- Performance metrics include melting time, total energy storage, mean power, energy per mass, and Nusselt number
- Temperature boundary condition: inner tube wall maintained at 35°C above PCM phase change temperature
- Outer shell defined as adiabatic boundary condition
10_1016_j_est_2024_115094.key_2:
- Inner tube wall: Constant temperature of 35 °C above PCM phase change temperature (62 °C total)
- Outer shell: Adiabatic boundary condition
- Initial state: PCM (RT35) in solid state
- Gravitational force: Acting in Y direction
- Domain: 2D cross-section of shell-and-tube heat exchanger
- Simulation type: Transient, 2D
- Mesh: 22,141 elements
- Time step: 0.2 s
- Mushy zone constant: C = 10^5
- Small number to avoid division by zero: ε = 10^-3
- PCM: Initially at solid state (27 °C or 300.15 K)
- Gravitational acceleration: Included in momentum equation
- Heat transfer mechanism: Conduction through fins and natural convection in melted PCM
- Material interfaces: Copper fins in contact with both PCM and inner tube
- Shell material: Plexiglas (insulating, minimizes heat losses)
- Domain geometry: Annular region with I-shaped copper fins between inner tube (R_in = 36.5 mm) and outer shell (R_out = 95 mm)
10_1016_j_est_2024_115094.key_3:
- Phase change process of RT35 PCM in shell-and-tube heat exchanger with I-shaped fins
- Heat conduction through copper fins and natural convection in melted PCM
- Transient thermal behavior during melting process
- Liquid fraction evolution over time
- Temperature distribution profiles at multiple time steps (100 s, 800 s, 1500 s, 3000 s)
- Streamlines/velocity profiles in melted PCM
- Total energy stored (E_total)
- Melting time (t_m)
- Mean power (P_m = E_total/t_m)
- Energy stored per mass (E_m)
- Nusselt number (Nu) to quantify heat transfer processes
- Minimize melting time while maximizing energy storage capacity
- Optimize fin geometry to enhance natural convection in PCM
- Achieve uniform temperature distribution throughout the heat exchanger
- Improve thermal performance compared to conventional fin designs (honeycomb, longitudinal, circular)
10_1016_j_est_2024_115094.key_4:
- Fixed inner tube radius R_in = 36.5 mm and outer shell radius R_out = 95 mm
- Fin dimensions constrained to base length R₂ = 54.5 mm, top length R₁ = 77 mm, fin length L_fin = 25 mm, thickness η = 2 mm
- Parametric study limited to specific dR₁/dR₂ ratios (0.5, 0.66, 0.75, 1, 1.33, 1.5, 2) and α₁/α₂ curvature ratios (0.6, 0.75, 0.8, 1, 1.25, 1.33, 1.66)
- Total system volume fixed at 23,699 mm² across all cases
- I-shaped fin design without connecting bar (modified from Wang et al.'s structure)
- PCM melting temperature fixed at 300.15 K (27°C)
- Inner tube wall temperature fixed at 62°C (35°C above PCM melting point)

- Initial condition: PCM in solid state at 27°C
- Gravitational force constrained to Y direction
- Mushy zone constant fixed at C = 10^5
- Small number ε = 10^-3 fixed to avoid division by zero
- Maximum temperature limited to 50°C as shown in temperature profiles
- Manufacturing requires "strict tolerances to maintain symmetry and structural strength"
- Technology roadmap includes constraints of welding, bending machine capabilities, and SLM technology
- Manufacturing processes limited to "punching, bending, or milling" with high precision requirements

- Design must fit within shell-and-tube heat exchanger configuration without interfering with fluid flow

10_1016_j_istruc_2025_108818.key_1:
- Kinked Connected Components (KCCs) for structural beam-column joints
- Q355b steel with elastic modulus Es = 2.06 × 10⁵ GPa, yield strength fy = 394 MPa, tensile strength fu = 525 MPa, elongation Ag = 21%, Poisson's ratio μs = 0.29
- Designed to enhance resistance to progressive collapse in building structures by improving ductility, enabling catenary action during large deformations, and preventing premature fracture in beam-column joints
- Rectangular plate (330 mm length, 100 mm width) with wave-shaped central section (90 mm length) and bolted connection parts (120 mm length each), featuring hKCC (4-32 mm), lKCC (40-110 mm), and tKCC (4, 6, 8 mm) parameters, with M16 bolts in 2×2 pattern
10_1016_j_istruc_2025_108818.key_2:
- Lower loading plate constrained in all degrees of freedom (U1=U2=U3=UR1=UR2=UR3=0)
- Upper loading plate constrained in all directions except vertical displacement (U1=U3=UR1=UR2=UR3=0)
- Unidirectional tensile loading applied through actuator with loading rate of 2 mm/min
- Displacement amplitude set to 80 mm to ensure specimens reach failure stage
- Surface-to-surface contact with Coulomb friction coefficient of 0.25 in tangential direction and hard contact in normal direction
- M16 8.8S high-strength bolts in 2×2 pattern connecting components
- Pinned connections at beam ends in progressive collapse simulations
- Vertical displacement protocols imposed at column apexes through displacement-controlled actuators
- ABAQUS/Explicit finite element model using C3D8R solid elements with 4 mm mesh size
- Ductile metal damage module defined based on stress triaxiality for fracture modeling
- Three-dimensional nonlinear analysis with material properties of Q355b steel (Es = 2.06 × 10⁵ GPa, fy = 394 MPa, fu = 525 MPa)
- Boundary conditions maintained throughout loading process as specified in FE model diagrams
10_1016_j_istruc_2025_108818.key_3:
- Tensile behavior including elastic deformation, yielding, strengthening, necking, and fracture of steel components under uniaxial loading with geometric nonlinearity and material plasticity
- Maximum force (F_max), displacement corresponding to maximum force (u_Fmax), load-displacement curves, initial stiffness, failure modes, deformation capacity, and stage-specific load/displacement values (elastic, straightening, strengthening, necking stages)
- Maximize both F_max (load-bearing capacity) and u_Fmax (deformation capacity) through optimal combinations of h_KCC (wave height) and l_KCC (wave length) for different t_KCC (thickness) values while avoiding premature wave part fracture
10_1016_j_istruc_2025_108818.key_4:
- Wave length constraint: 40 mm ≤ l_KCC ≤ 110 mm
- Wave height constraint: 4 mm ≤ h_KCC ≤ 32 mm
- Thickness options: t_KCC = 4, 6, or 8 mm
- Total specimen length: 330 mm, width: 100 mm
- Bolt pattern: 2 × 2 arrangement of M16 bolts with 17.5 mm diameter
- Must avoid premature fracture in wave part (failure should occur in bolted connection part)
- Minimum l_KCC of 50 mm required to prevent significant performance decline when h_KCC is large
- h_KCC/l_KCC ratio must be controlled to prevent wave part fracture
- Material constraint: Q355b steel for all components
- Manufacturing constraint: Cold-forming process using specialized mold
- Loading plates thickness: 32 mm to limit out-of-plane deformation
- For t_KCC = 4 mm, optimal l_KCC range: 60-70 mm; for t_KCC = 6 mm: 70-80 mm; for t_KCC = 8 mm: 95-105 mm
- Maximum wave height for practical use: 32 mm
- Minimum wave length for practical use: 40 mm (though performance degrades significantly at 40 mm with large h_KCC)

10_1016_j_postharvbio_2025_113586.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Collision-induced mechanical damage in Fuji apples during mechanized harvesting operations
- **Material / Medium:** 
  - Apple peel (density: 475.7 kg/m³, moisture content: 78 ± 2%, elastic modulus: 4.995 MPa, strength limit: 0.575 MPa)
  - Apple pulp (density: 799.1 kg/m³, moisture content: 85 ± 2%, elastic modulus: 2.115 MPa, strength limit: 0.379 MPa)

10_1007_s40430_023_04235_5.key_1:

- **Material / Medium:** Homogeneous plate (E = 74 GPa, ν = 0.3), discontinuities (E = 20 GPa, ν = 0.3), yield strength = 240 MPa for both
- **Application & Importance:** Damage-tolerant design assessment; determining how material irregularities affect plastic zone formation ahead of crack tips for fracture mechanics analysis
- **Geometry / Domain:** 100mm × 200mm rectangular plate with 30mm edge crack; discontinuities include elliptical (major axis 5-35mm), square (5-35mm), hexagonal (side 5-25mm), and octagonal (side 5-25mm); tensile load applied to top edge with bottom edge fixed
10_1007_s40430_023_04235_5.key_2:

- **Loads / Excitations:** Monotonic static tensile load applied to top edge; load range 0-120 MPa; maximum load of 120 MPa
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Elliptical (major axis 5-35mm), square (5-35mm), hexagonal (side 5-25mm), and octagonal (side 5-25mm) discontinuities; level set method used to track discontinuities; XFEM enrichment functions for crack and inclusion interfaces
- **Simulation Type:** Extended Finite Element Method (XFEM); 2D plane stress and plane strain conditions; Tresca and Von-Mises yield criteria; uniform mesh of 40 × 80 nodes; domain-based interaction integral approach for stress intensity factors
10_1007_s40430_023_04235_5.key_3:

- **Optimization Goal:** Characterize how material irregularities influence crack tip plastic zone formation; determine relationships between discontinuity parameters (size, position) and plastic zone extent; validate XFEM approach for modeling crack-inclusion interactions in fracture mechanics
10_1007_s40430_023_04235_5.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Rectangular plate dimensions fixed at 100mm × 200mm; initial edge crack length fixed at 30mm; discontinuity sizes constrained to elliptical (major axis 5-35mm), square (5-35mm), hexagonal (side 5-25mm), and octagonal (side 5-25mm); discontinuity positions constrained to minimum 30mm from crack; uniform 40 × 80 node mesh used for all simulations; maximum discontinuity position (h) limited to 70mm from crack
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Material properties fixed (homogeneous plate: E = 74 GPa, ν = 0.3; discontinuities: E = 20 GPa, ν = 0.3; yield strength = 240 MPa for both); load range limited to 0-120 MPa; analysis limited to small-scale yielding conditions; Tresca and Von-Mises yield criteria applied as the only failure theories; plane stress and plane strain conditions analyzed separately without transition modeling
- **Process/Manufacturing:** Limited to 2D modeling rather than 3D; monotonic loading only (no cyclic fatigue analysis); conventional FEM limitations (conformal meshing issues) addressed by using XFEM; analysis assumes idealized discontinuity geometries without manufacturing imperfections

10_1007_s42417_025_01853_2.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Vehicle suspension damper (twin-tube hydraulic damper) for automotive applications
- **Material / Medium:** 
  - Hydraulic oil with viscosity of 17 CP and density of 835 kg/m³
  - Nitrogen gas in compensation chamber with initial pressure of 0.45 MPa
  - Rubber bushing with initial stiffness of 560 N/mm
- **Application & Importance:** 
  - Rattle noise control in vehicle suspension systems

  - Direct impact on passenger comfort and safety as rattle noise deteriorates interior sound quality
- **Geometry / Domain:**
  - Twin-tube structure with rebound chamber, compression chamber, and compensation chamber
  - Piston diameter of 35 mm and rod diameter of 22 mm
  - Four valve systems: flow valve, rebound valve, compensation valve, and compression valve
  - Disc valves with irregular orifices on each valve system
  - Rubber bushing connecting rod to vehicle body

  - Evaluation frequency band for rattle noise: 100-200 Hz
10_1007_s42417_025_01853_2.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**

  - Fluid inlet boundary condition: velocity excitation with maximum flow rate corresponding to extreme operating condition
  - Fluid outlet boundary condition: zero pressure
  - Fluid assumed to be incompressible in CFD simulation
  - Initial gas pressure in compensation chamber: 0.45 MPa
  - Initial gas volume in compensation chamber: v₀
  - Sampling frequency: 5120 Hz, frequency resolution: 1 Hz, sampling duration: 15 s for vibration measurements
  - Minimum mesh element size: 0.015 mm near orifices in CFD simulation

- **Loads / Excitations:**

  - Pure electric mode operation during vehicle road test to eliminate engine noise
  - Sinusoidal motion of cylinder relative to piston for velocity characteristics testing
  - Operating velocities: 0.05 m/s (low-velocity condition) and 1.0 m/s (high-velocity condition)
  - Vibration acceleration sensor arranged at damper rod-end and steering knuckle

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Rubber bushing connects rod to vehicle body with force relationship Fu = KΔx + CΔẋ
  - Hydraulic force from two ends of chamber and preload acting on disc valves
  - Oil flow through four valve systems (flow, rebound, compensation, compression)
  - Pressure fluctuations within chambers during valve opening/closing processes
  - Relationship between pressure at inner radius and flow rate of disc valves: Qv = (π/6μt ln(rv2/rv1))xv³(pv − pvb)

- **Simulation Type:**
  - Transient mode solver with 100 steps for CFD simulation
  - Combination of parametric simulation and localized finite element simulation
  - 3D fluid domain for CFD simulation of orifices on disc valves
  - Time-domain simulation for vibration characteristics analysis
  - Two operating velocity conditions for sensitivity analysis: 0.05 m/s (before disc valve opening) and 1.0 m/s (after disc valve opening)
  - Evaluation frequency band for rattle noise: 100-200 Hz
  - RMS calculation of rod-end vibration acceleration in 100-200 Hz frequency band as evaluation metric
10_1007_s42417_025_01853_2.key_3:

  - Vibration characteristics of hydraulic damper under road excitation
  - Damping force-velocity relationship (velocity characteristics)
  - Fluid dynamics of hydraulic oil through irregular orifices in disc valves
  - Disc valve dynamics (opening/closing behavior) and associated pressure fluctuations
  - Structural vibration transmission from damper to vehicle body

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**
  - RMS of rod-end vibration acceleration in the 100-200 Hz frequency band
  - Time-domain vibration acceleration curves showing peak-to-trough differences
  - Damping force at operating velocities (0.05 m/s and 1.0 m/s)
  - Frequency-domain vibration characteristics in 100-200 Hz band
  - Subjective evaluation scores on 9-level scale (1-9, with higher scores indicating more severe rattle)
  - Rattle noise classification (Severe rattle, Slight rattle, No rattle)

- **Optimization Goal:**
  - Minimize RMS of rod-end vibration acceleration in 100-200 Hz frequency band to achieve "no rattle" condition (RMS < 1.20 m/s²)
  - Maintain damping force stability (variation < 15% at velocity ≤ 0.1 m/s; < 10% at velocity > 0.1 m/s)
  - Optimize stiffness properties of disc valves (flow, rebound, compensation, compression)

  - Gas pressure in compensation chamber (0.45 MPa initial) not optimized due to risk of idle stroke phenomenon
  - Preload not optimized as it changes disc valve opening moment which impacts core damper characteristics
  - Design parameters varied within 70-130% of initial values in DOE (7 levels: 70%, 80%, 90%, 100%, 110%, 120%, 130%)

  - Damping force variation must be <10% compared to original state when operating velocity > 0.1 m/s

  - Testing constraints: vehicle road test has complex procedures and high costs; damper rig test has difficulty accurately reflecting actual rattle noise conditions

10_1016_j_cma_2025_117972.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** 2D Auxetic Metamaterials, specifically re-entrant structures and orthotropic metamaterials. The analysis focuses on mechanical metamaterials with unique architectures producing properties not found in base materials.

- **Material / Medium:** Durable material fabricated by 3D printer Form 2, modeled using Neo-Hookean material model for quasi-static loading behavior. Material properties extracted from experimental test data of Type IV dog-bone-shaped samples per ASTM D638-14 standard.

- **Application & Importance:** Designing metamaterials with targeted mechanical properties (Poisson's ratio, Young's modulus, porosity, and stress distribution). Traditional methods fail to efficiently explore the vast 2D design space, necessitating advanced techniques for non-linear behavior design where data scarcity is problematic.

- **Geometry / Domain:** 2D re-entrant structures with ligament-based geometries where auxetic behavior is controlled by bending ligaments. Conventional designs have straight ligaments, but optimized designs feature curved ligaments to reduce stress concentration. The orthotropic case study includes more complex geometries from a 2D Orthotropic Metamaterial Dataset. Design generation uses path-finding methods on 20x20 grid maps with B-spline post-processing to create smooth transitions between ligaments and support beams. Designs are evaluated in quarter-unit cell configurations with boundary conditions applied through virtual points.
10_1016_j_cma_2025_117972.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Fixed X-displacement at left nodes (u₁ = 0); Fixed Y-displacement at down nodes (u₂ = 0); Right nodes linked to virtual point X (u₁ = −CellW ⋅ u₁,VP_X); Top nodes linked to virtual point Y (u₂ = −CellH ⋅ u₂,VP_Y); Virtual point X has u₂ = 0; Virtual point Y has u₁ = Strain_Y; Mesh uses CPS4R (four-node bilinear plane stress quadrilateral, reduced integration) and CPS3 (three-node triangular) elements; Designs analyzed in quarter-unit cell configuration.

- **Loads / Excitations:** Explicit dynamic step with load time of 1 s; Tabular amplitude for gradual loading application; 2% tensile strain for linear simulations; 20% tensile strain for non-linear simulations; Mass scaling factor of 1000 applied initially; 3D triangle shell elements with seed size 0.2 mm.

- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Boundary conditions applied through two virtual points; Movement coupled between virtual points and nodes on connection edges of neighboring unit cells; Simulation uses Neo-Hookean material model to capture quasi-static loading behavior.

- **Simulation Type:** Explicit dynamic simulation for non-linear cases; Linear static simulation for linear cases; 2D simulations of metamaterial unit cells; Non-linear large strain (20% tensile strain) and linear small strain (2% tensile strain) scenarios; Quasi-static loading behavior analysis.
10_1016_j_cma_2025_117972.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Non-linear mechanical behavior of 2D metamaterials under tensile loading; Stress distribution (von Mises stress); Displacement field; Strain field; Elastic deformation characteristics; Mechanical property relationships.

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Poisson's ratio (ν = -u₁/Strain_Y); Young's modulus (E = RF_Y/(CellW × CellT × Strain_Y)); Maximum von Mises stress (σ_vM = √(σ₁₁² - σ₁₁σ₂₂ + σ₂₂² + 3τ₁₂²)); Porosity (percentage of void in design); Stress field distribution; Displacement field in x and y directions; Strain field; Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) in high-stress areas; R² values for property prediction.

- **Optimization Goal:** Minimize maximum von Mises stress in high-stress concentration areas; Generate novel designs meeting specific target properties (Poisson's ratio, Young's modulus, porosity); Optimize stress distribution while maintaining targeted mechanical properties; Reduce stress concentration through RBF shape optimization; Improve prediction accuracy for mechanical properties in non-linear scenarios; Generate diverse designs beyond training dataset examples.
10_1016_j_cma_2025_117972.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** 20x20 grid map for path-finding design generation; Width at four evenly spaced points along path constrained between 1-6 units; Designs interpolated from 256x256 to 64x64 (re-entrant) and 25x25 to 32x32 (orthotropic); B-spline post-processing to ensure tangent connections between ligaments and support beams; Extra vertical nodes added to create smoother transitions between ligaments and support beams; Mesh generated with quad-dominated strategy using CPS4R and CPS3 elements; Unit cell analyzed in quarter-configuration.

- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Linear simulations constrained to 2% tensile strain; Non-linear simulations constrained to 20% tensile strain; Optimization stop criteria: maximum 10% change in Young's modulus or 0.05 change in Poisson's ratio; High-stress points defined as nodes with stress exceeding 99.5% of maximum; Simulation load time constrained to 1 second for explicit dynamic analysis; Mass scaling factor of 1000 applied initially for computational efficiency.

- **Process/Manufacturing:** Material fabricated using 3D printer Form 2; Material properties extracted from ASTM D638-14 standard tests on Type IV dog-bone samples; No contact considered in simulation; Boundary conditions applied through virtual points with coupled movement to connection edges; Simulation uses Neo-Hookean material model for quasi-static loading behavior.

10_1016_j_compfluid_2024_106425.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Detonation waves in reacting flows, specifically modeling the formation, propagation, and dynamic evolution of multidimensional detonation waves using numerical simulation.

- **Material / Medium:** Two-component reactive gas medium with monomolecular reaction kinetics (A → B) where A is the reaction reagent and B is the reaction product. The medium follows perfect gas equation of state with adiabatic index γ = 1.4. Ignition temperature T_ign = 0.26, specific energy yield q₀ = 1. Reaction rate determined by discrete ignition temperature model with time scales τ₀ = 10⁻¹ (slow reaction) and τ₀ = 4×10⁻³ (fast reaction).

- **Application & Importance:** To accurately simulate detonation waves without numerical artifacts (non-physical shock waves and weak detonation fronts) that commonly occur in traditional methods. The analysis demonstrates how the method can resolve the ZND (Zel'dovich, von Neumann, and Döring) detonation wave structure with subcell resolution even on coarse meshes, while handling the stiffness of chemical reactions without requiring physical process splitting methods.

- **Geometry / Domain:** Multiple configurations including one-dimensional planar detonation waves, two-dimensional cylindrical detonation waves (Ω = [-2, +4] × [-1, +1]), interaction with inert bubbles (single bubble and 6×3 lattice), detonation cellular structures (Ω = [0, 10] × [-1, +1]), and three-dimensional spherical detonation waves (Ω = [-1, +1]³). The solution depends primarily on the radial distance r from the origin in axisymmetric/spherical cases.
10_1016_j_compfluid_2024_106425.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** Free outflow boundary conditions on most domain boundaries; periodic boundary conditions on top and bottom boundaries (equivalent to solid wall conditions due to symmetry); exact solution boundary condition for detonation front on left boundary; solid wall condition at left boundary for reference solutions; boundaries specified as exact solution for detonation front from CJ conditions on left boundary with free outflow on right boundary.

- **Loads / Excitations:** Initial conditions defined by Chapman–Jouguet (CJ) conditions for stationary detonation waves; sinusoidal disturbance ∼|sin(nπx)| for detonation cellular structure formation; shock wave parameters (ρ, u, p) = (2.880323, 1.659610, 5.219111) for shock-bubble interaction problems; specific density, velocity, and pressure profiles for Riemann problems; bubble initial conditions with radius R = 0.5 and density ρ₀ = 0.2 (shock-bubble) or ρ₀ = 2.0 (detonation wave-bubble interaction).

- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Detonation wave interaction with inert bubbles (single bubble and 6×3 lattice); shock wave reflection from solid boundaries; Richtmyer-Meshkov instability at contact discontinuities; triple points of shock wave intersection; Mach shock wave formation; vortex street generation at bubble interfaces; diffraction of detonation waves on obstacles.

- **Simulation Type:** Transient non-stationary simulations; 1D, 2D, and 3D configurations; space-time adaptive ADER-DG finite element method with LST-DG predictor; a posteriori sub-cell ADER-WENO finite-volume limiting; no splitting or fractional time steps methods; Courant number C_F_L = 0.9 for detonation problems; local time step partitioning in reactive cells; high-order method (P^5, P^9, P^12 polynomials) with adaptive mesh refinement.
10_1016_j_compfluid_2024_106425.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Detonation wave formation, propagation, and dynamic evolution in reactive flows; shock wave diffraction and reflection; Richtmyer-Meshkov instability; vortex generation and evolution; chemical reaction kinetics with discrete ignition temperature model; conservation of mass, momentum and energy in compressible reactive flows; contact discontinuities and rarefaction waves.

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Density (ρ) distribution; pressure (p) distribution; flow velocity magnitude (v); mass concentration of reaction reagent (c₁); partial density of reagent (ρ₁ = ρc₁); troubled cells indicator (β); detonation front width (measured in subcells); percentage of troubled cells in spatial mesh; conservation of mass (c₁ + c₂ = 1); Zel'dovich chemical peak formation; subcell resolution of discontinuous components; flow symmetry preservation; comparison with reference solutions.

- **Optimization Goal:** Achieve accurate resolution of ZND detonation wave structure with subcell resolution on coarse meshes; eliminate non-physical artifacts (weak detonation fronts ahead of shock waves); maintain high accuracy for smooth solution components; reduce computational costs by avoiding global time step reduction through local time step partitioning; demonstrate method's ability to handle stiffness without physical process splitting methods.
10_1016_j_compfluid_2024_106425.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Simulations constrained to structured Cartesian meshes with specific sizes (100 cells for 1D detonation problems, 100×100 cells for 2D Riemann problems, 200×100 for shock-bubble interaction, 19×19×19 for 3D spherical explosion); domain geometries fixed for each problem type (e.g., Ω = [-2, +4] × [-1, +1] for shock-bubble interaction, Ω = [0, 10] × [-1, +1] for detonation cellular structure); limited to 1D, 2D, and 3D configurations with specific coordinate domains.

- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Maximum Courant number (CFL) constrained to 0.9 for detonation problems; without local adaptive time stepping, CFL must be ≤ 0.01-0.05 for strong stiffness problems to maintain solution admissibility; must maintain positivity of density and internal energy; must maintain non-negativity of mass concentrations; subcell resolution limited to 2N+1 subcells per element (e.g., 11 subcells for N=5); minimum detonation front width constrained to 1-2 subcells for weak stiffness and 2-4 subcells for strong stiffness cases.

- **Process/Manufacturing:** Local adaptive time step procedure limited to [α] ≤ 10 for strong stiffness cases and [α] ≤ 4 for weak stiffness cases; the method requires at least 100 cells in 1D for detonation wave simulation to achieve good results; number of troubled cells should be minimized (typically <5% in 1D, <10-16% in 2D/3D); a posteriori limiting constrained to ADER-WENO2 finite volume method; local adaptive time step procedure called in only 2-4 cells per time step for 1D strong stiffness problems; significant computational cost increase (20-100 times) when using global time step reduction for strong stiffness problems.

  - Material properties assumed temperature-dependent (e.g., silicon Young's modulus decreases from 129.62 GPa at 25°C to 128.43 GPa at 150°C)

10_1016_j_ijmecsci_2017_09_032.key_4:

10_1016_j_jmsy_2025_05_011.key_1:

- **Application & Importance:** Precision manufacturing of critical aero-engine components where pipe failure accounts for 50-60% of total aircraft failure rate; requires sheath deviation accuracy of ±0.5 mm and bending radius deviation ratio <1%; current manual production suffers from uncontrollable human factors affecting accuracy and efficiency
- **Geometry / Domain:** Multi-segment pipes with straight sections (S₁-S₈) and bending sections (B₁-B₅); multiple pipe types with different configurations (Type 1: 8 straight sections; Type 2: 4 straight sections; Type 3: 5 straight sections); bending radii of 20.0 mm; straight section lengths varying from 23.75-257.61 mm; processing involves multiple workstations including bending forming, grasping, measuring, cutting, and chamfering
10_1016_j_jmsy_2025_05_011.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:** 
  - Grasping limited to straight pipe sections only (S₁-S₈), not bending sections
  - Grasping point position O₁ must be on pipe centerline with perpendicular closure vector
  - Joint angle limits (θₘ(t) ∈ Ωₘ), maximum velocity (vₘ,max), maximum acceleration (aₘ,max), maximum jerk (jₘ,max), and maximum torque (τₘ,max) constraints
  - Manufacturing rhythm constraint: Tₜ ≤ Tₐ/T_b where Tₜ is manufacturing rhythm, Tₐ is available working time, and T_b is daily pipe quantity requirement
  - Collision constraint: no intersection between robot components, pipe, and environment data
  - Measuring constraints: pipe xy-coordinates must align with measuring box center, pipe surface should be parallel to xy-plane, and grasping angles φ must be between ±100° to ±120°

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Uniformly distributed weight load (w) along pipe axial direction
  - Contact forces at processing holes: feed force F_f divided into upward slip component F_τ = F_f cos α and forward force F_η = F_f sin α where α = 5° chamfer angle
  - Equivalent nodal force system from gravity: F = -wl/2, M₁ = wl²/2, M₂ = -wl²/2
  - Feed distance L = 55 mm, feedrate = 8 mm/s for insertion process
  - Three optimization objectives: time consumed (f₁), joint energy consumption (f₂), and pipe vibration (f₃)

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Elastic deformation model combining deformation value ε, static robot stiffness, and force components F_τ and F_η
  - Pipe deformation compensation using formula: pᵢ'(xᵢ, yᵢ) = (xᵢ, yᵢ + L/n × i, zᵢ + ε - ε/n × i)
  - Multi-camera measurement system requiring pipe xy-component to match focal center coordinate
  - Grasping constraints requiring gripper finger vectors to be perpendicular to pipe centerline

- **Simulation Type:**
  - Finite element analysis using Timoshenko beam elements for elastic spatial frame structures
  - Transient analysis of vibration with viscous damping model (F_c = c v_s)
  - Multi-objective optimization using improved NSGA-II algorithm with adaptive crossover probability
  - Xbar-s control chart analysis with subgroup size of 20 for stability evaluation
  - NURBS curve interpolation for path planning with S-shaped acceleration/deceleration feed rate planning
  - 3D collision checking using triangular mesh models and voxel maps for environment data
10_1016_j_jmsy_2025_05_011.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** 
  - Gravity-induced elastic deformation of flexible bending pipes using Timoshenko beam element analysis
  - Vibration behavior of pipes with viscous damping model (F_c = c v_s)
  - Kinematic motion of 6-axis robotic joints during path following
  - Collision avoidance between robot components, pipe, and manufacturing environment
  - Grasping posture and path planning with NURBS curve interpolation

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**
  - Time consumed (f₁): total trajectory time in seconds
  - Joint energy consumption (f₂): average acceleration in mm/s² (used as energy proxy)
  - Pipe vibration (f₃): maximum amplitude in mm at each workstation
  - Sheath deviation: perpendicular (d^v_i) and parallel (d^p_i) distance from design model
  - Bending radius accuracy: measured vs. ideal 20.0 mm radius
  - Process capability index (C_pk): calculated as (T_r - Δ̅)/(3s) with tolerance range T_r = ±0.5 mm
  - IGD (Inverted Generational Distance), 1/HV (Hypervolume), and SP (Spacing Metric) for algorithm performance

- **Optimization Goal:**
  - Minimize time consumed while meeting manufacturing rhythm constraints
  - Minimize joint energy consumption through smooth acceleration profiles
  - Minimize pipe vibration by reducing maximum amplitudes at workstations
  - Achieve Pareto optimal trade-offs between time, energy, and vibration using improved NSGA-II
  - Maintain sheath deviation within ±0.5 mm and bending radius deviation ratio below 1%
  - Ensure collision-free paths while satisfying kinematic constraints (joint limits, velocity, acceleration, jerk)
10_1016_j_jmsy_2025_05_011.key_4:

  - Rolling angle θ limited to 0° or 180° due to parallel gripper design
  - Sheath deviation must be within ±0.5 mm tolerance

10_1016_j_ceramint_2024_12_487.key_1:

10_1016_j_finel_2024_104278.key_1:

  - Al6061 (bi-material beams): E=69000 MPa, ν=0.3, ft=124.2 MPa, Gf=0.4968 N/mm, k=10, κ₀=18×10⁻⁴

  - 304 Stainless steel (bi-material beam): E=193000 MPa, ν=0.29, ft=240 MPa, Gf=4.0 N/mm, α=17.3×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹, kT=1.0 W/mK

10_1016_j_finel_2024_104278.key_2:

  - For bi-material beams: Simply supported boundary conditions with specified support positions
  - Convergence tolerance TOL = 10⁻⁶ for displacement and temperature changes between iterations

  - For cruciform specimen: Three BC sets with different thermal and mechanical loading combinations

  - Stainless steel/Borosilicate glass interface in the notched bi-material beam
  - Heat transfer across damage zones governed by q = -(1-d)kT∇T
  - Material interfaces where crack path evolution is studied (e.g., crack crossing interface vs. propagating along interface)
  - Adaptive mesh refinement at damage zones with element characteristic length h_e = √A_e

  - 2D plane stress analysis
  - Nonlinear analysis with damage evolution
  - Staggered solution scheme for thermo-mechanical problems
  - Adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) with QrefineR algorithm for quadrilateral elements
  - Polygonal elements (P4, P5, P6) treated with Laplace shape functions

10_1016_j_finel_2024_104278.key_3:

  - Elastic-damage behavior with non-decreasing internal damage variable
  - Thermo-elastic-damage coupling (when thermal effects are considered)

  - Mesh-dependent fracture behavior with incorporation of element characteristic length and fracture energy

  - Computational time comparison between different mesh strategies

  - Achieve accurate crack path prediction without prior knowledge of damage location
  - Minimize computation time compared to uniform fine mesh approaches (70,345 seconds vs. 9,934 seconds for AMR)

10_1016_j_finel_2024_104278.key_4:

- **Application & Importance:** Solving geometric inverse problems for heat source identification, electrical impedance tomography, acoustics, chemical reactions, and electromagnetics; reconstructing unknown boundaries in engineering applications governed by nonlinear Darcy's law, Ohm's law, or Fourier's law
- **Geometry / Domain:** 2D and 3D multiply-connected domains with various fixed shapes (L-shape, square, ∞-shape, star-shape, triangular) containing internal holes; initial domains include squares and disks; boundary evolves during optimization with volume constraint |Ω| = A; finite element discretization with triangular (2D) and tetrahedral (3D) meshes; examples include L-shaped domains with z = 2 and z = 8 in 3D cases

  - Volume constraint |Ω| = A where A > 0
  - Domain Ω satisfies ε-cone property
  - ∂u(Ω,p)/∂ν = -c on ∂Ω (c > 0, strictly positive constant)
  - Boundary condition for descent direction: ∂θ/∂ν = -l + (p-1)/p |∇u(Ω,p)|^p ν on ∂(Ω \ K)
  - Finite element boundary conditions: v_h|∂Ω = 0, v_h|∂K = 1

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Nonlinear p-Laplacian operator with 1 < p < ∞
  - Δₚu(Ω,p) = 0 in Ω \ K where Δₚ = div(|∇u(Ω,p)|^(p-2)∇u(Ω,p))

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Fixed domain (L-shape, square, ∞-shape, star-shape, triangular) containing internal hole (K)
  - Initial domain (square or disk) evolves toward target shape
  - Volume constraint maintained throughout optimization process

  - 2D and 3D cases
  - Shape optimization with gradient descent method
  - Finite element Galerkin discretization
  - Picard iterations procedure with tolerance τ = 10^-14
  - Algorithm parameters: β = 3, ε = 10^-4
  - Re-meshing strategy applied at each iteration to maintain mesh quality
  - 3D examples with L-shape domains of length z = 2 and z = 8
  - Volume constraint A = 1.2 for 3D cases
  - Steady-state analysis (no time dependence)
10_1016_j_cam_2025_116488.key_3:

  - Boundary and volume constraint satisfaction

  - Compare efficiency between distributed Eulerian derivative and boundary Eulerian derivative approaches

- Silicon anodes in various forms: nano-Si, micro-Si (2-8 μm), porous Si, Si-C composites, and Si/Li₂₁Si₅ composites
- Solid-state electrolytes: sulfides (Li₆PS₅Cl, Li₇P₃S₁₁, Li₃PS₄), oxides (LLZO/Li₇La₃Zr₂O₁₂, Li₃InCl₆), and polymers (PEO/LiTFSI)
- Cathode materials: LFP/LiFePO₄, NCM/LiNi₀.₈Mn₀.₁Co₀.₁O₂, LCO/LiCoO₂, and S/Li₂S
- Silicon theoretical specific capacity: 3578 mAh g⁻¹ (approximately 10× graphite's 372 mAh g⁻¹)
- Silicon volume expansion during lithiation: ~400%
- For 300 Wh kg⁻¹ energy density, required SSE thickness: <23 μm (LLZO), <74 μm (LPSCl), <92 μm (PEO), <43 μm (Li₃InCl₆)
- Si/Li₂₁Si₅ anode volume expansion: 18.8% compared to 117.9% for pure Si at 17.9 mAh cm⁻² areal capacity
- Si@B-C/rGO electrode capacity retention: >80% after 300 cycles at 1 A g⁻¹
- Si@SiO₂@LPO@C specific capacity: 2482.1 mAh g⁻¹ with 88.7% initial Coulombic efficiency
- LiₓSi | SSE | S full cell capacity retention: 85.4% after 200 cycles at 60°C, 76.3% after 500 cycles at 25°C
- Bilayer solid electrolyte framework: dense layer (~20 μm) and porous layer (~100 μm)
- Li-Cu-CNF 1D ion conductor conductivity: 10⁻³ S cm⁻¹ at 25°C
- Active material content in composite electrodes: typically 30-80% to manage stress from volume expansion
- Optimal solid-state electrolyte properties: broad electrochemical stability window, high room-temperature ionic conductivity, low electronic conductivity, robust mechanical attributes, chemical stability, and cost-effectiveness
- Micro-Si@Li₃PO₄@C initial Coulombic efficiency: 83.3% compared to 74.2% for micro-Si@Li₃PO₄
- Full cell with NCM111 cathode capacity: 129.2 mAh g⁻¹ at 0.2C after 100 cycles
- Pellet-type cell fabrication pressure: 300-400 MPa for densification
- Bipolar stacking enables high-voltage outputs by connecting cells in series with single current collector
- Required SSE ionic conductivity for high-energy density: >1 mS cm⁻¹
- Si anode particle size effects: nano-Si (higher surface area, better contact) vs. micro-Si (lower interface reactivity, more stable cycling)

10_1016_j_nxmate_2024_100371.key_4:
- Electrolyte thickness must not exceed 23 μm (LLZO), 74 μm (LPSCl), 92 μm (PEO), or 43 μm (Li₃InCl₆) to achieve 300 Wh kg⁻¹ energy density
- Active material content constrained to 30-80% in composite electrodes to manage stress from volume expansion
- SSE film thickness typically exceeds 200 μm for mechanical stability in pellet-type cells
- Solid electrolyte thickness must balance between <200 μm for energy density and >20 μm for structural integrity
- Silicon volume expansion constrained to ~400% during lithiation, causing mechanical deterioration
- Sulfide electrolytes have narrow electrochemical stability windows (1.7-2.7 V)
- Oxide electrolytes have wider stability windows (2.16-4.31 V for LATP)
- Polymer electrolytes (e.g., PEO) susceptible to oxidation above 4.0 V
- Sulfide electrolytes require specialized environments due to H₂S generation and moisture sensitivity
- Thin-film approaches limited to low mass loading (<0.23 mg cm⁻²), unsuitable for power batteries
- Manufacturing processes for sheet electrodes and SSE films confined to laboratory environments
- Processing must consider gas sensitivity, strength, stiffness, elasticity, and plasticity of sheet materials
- Electrode fabrication requires 300-400 MPa pressure for pellet-type cell densification
- Cold pressing of Si/Li₂₁Si₅ anode requires 400 MPa pressure
- Bipolar stacking limited to monomer cell voltages (e.g., 8.2 V demonstrated)
- Sulfide-based SSEs require processing in specialized environments due to moisture sensitivity
- Multiple synthesis steps should be avoided to reduce manufacturing complexity
- Phase-change materials face constraints from leakage and sluggish thermal diffusion
- Operating temperature constraints: 40-60°C for polymer electrolytes, 100°C for some SSBs
- Lithium dendrite formation limits maximum current density in certain configurations
- Interfacial resistance must be minimized while maintaining mechanical contact during volume changes
- Silicon particle size affects performance: nano-Si (higher surface area) vs micro-Si (more stable cycling)
- External pressure must be optimized to balance interfacial contact without causing mechanical damage
- Areal capacity constrained by volume expansion effects, with demonstrated values up to 17.9 mAh cm⁻²

10_1016_j_istruc_2025_109210.key_1:
- Piled raft foundation system for high-rise buildings, specifically the Messe Torhaus structure in Frankfurt, Germany
- Soil layers: 2.5 m Quaternary sand (E=75 MPa, φ=32.5°, ν=0.25, ρ=1800 kg/m³) over 97.5 m Frankfurt clay (E=45+tanh((z-30)/15+1)×0.7z MPa, φ=20°, c=20 kPa, ν=0.15, ρ=1900 kg/m³)
- Raft foundation: 17.5 m × 24.5 m dimensions, E=34000 MPa, ν=0.2, γ=25 kN/m³
- Bored piles: 20 m length, diameters of 0.7 m, 0.9 m, and 1.1 m, E=10-36 GPa in parametric studies, ν=0.2, γ=25 kN/m³
- Soil domain: 100 m × 80 m × 100 m modeled volume
- Pile configurations: 30, 42, and 56 piles with variable spacing to maintain equal load distribution
- Interface friction coefficient: 0.75tan(φ) between soil and structural elements
- 90 different parametric combinations analyzed with varying pile diameter, number, and elastic modulus
- Maximum allowable settlement: 87.5 mm (5% of raft width per Eurocode 7)
- Optimized solution parameters: Pile diameter=1.1 m, pile count=30, elastic modulus=33.18 GPa
- Soil-pile-raft interaction modeled using surface-to-surface contact with penalty friction formulation
- Foundation system validated against Patil et al. (2022) load-settlement curve for P1 pile
- Settlement values ranged from 42.13 mm to 56.16 mm across all 90 combinations
- Number of piles identified as most influential factor (67.95% contribution to deformation)
- Pile diameter variation (0.7-1.1 m) affected settlement by 3.11-12.81%
- Pile count variation (30-56) affected settlement by 11.47-20.77%
- Pile elastic modulus variation (10-36 GPa) affected settlement by 5.18-8.49%
10_1016_j_istruc_2025_109210.key_2:
- Soil domain boundaries: 100 m × 80 m × 100 m volume with horizontal and vertical deformations constrained on side surfaces and bottom
- Base surface fixed in all directions based on assumption that lower soil boundary does not move
- Side surfaces restrict horizontal displacements while allowing vertical displacements to maintain natural soil spreading behavior
- Loads applied as pressure on raft foundation system with equivalent loads considered for piles
- Incremental loading applied through nine distinctive load steps
- Applied load range from 0 to 3 MN as shown in load-settlement curves
- Surface-to-surface contact method used for all pile-soil and raft-soil interactions
- Raft foundation bottom surface and pile outer surfaces defined as master surfaces, soil as slave surface
- Penalty friction formulation with coefficient of 0.75tan(φ) used for pile-soil contact behavior
- Pile tip interaction with soil defined as hard contact in normal direction
- Raft-soil contact defined by combination of hard contact and frictional contact allowing separation or sliding
- Soil profile: 2.5 m quaternary sand over 97.5 m Frankfurt clay with depth-dependent modulus
- Mohr-Coulomb material model used for soil analysis
- Nonlinear static three-dimensional finite element analysis performed
- 90 different parametric combinations analyzed with varying pile diameter, number, and elastic modulus
- Geostatic equilibrium state achieved prior to loading to represent natural stress distribution
- Boundary conditions established to minimize peripheral edge effects while allowing free development of deformations under loading
10_1016_j_istruc_2025_109210.key_3:

- Maximum deformation values (in mm) along raft diagonal lines
- Deformation values of critical piles (Pno 1, Pno 5, Pno 22, etc.)

- Achieve optimal balance between structural safety (settlement control) and economic efficiency

10_1016_j_soildyn_2024_109016.key_1:
- Fiber-reinforced elastomeric isolators (FREIs) for seismic isolation applications, specifically unbonded (UFREI) and partially bonded (PBFREI) configurations
- Rubber compounds: NR-EPDM (Natural Rubber and Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer) with shear modulus G = 0.70 MPa and damping ratio ξ = 8.49%; glass fiber fabric layers (600 g/m² bidirectional fabric ±45°, dry thickness 0.45 mm, final thickness 0.50 mm after vulcanization) with Young's modulus E = 1350 MPa and Poisson's ratio ν = 0.2; friction coefficient μ = 0.85 between isolator and supports in unbonded configuration
- Seismic isolation of low-rise masonry buildings requiring horizontal period Tₕ ≥ 0.8 s under 2 MPa vertical pressure, with focus on high-damping performance (damping ratio ≥ 6%) and cost reduction compared to traditional steel-reinforced isolators
- Circular geometry with 200 mm base diameter (b), 60 mm total rubber thickness (tᵣ,ₜₒₜ), and varying rubber layer thicknesses (2 mm, 4 mm, 6 mm); first shape factor S between 8.34-25.00 and aspect ratio R between 2.68-3.10; cyclic shear testing up to 200% tᵣ,ₜₒₜ with sinusoidal motion at 0.2 Hz frequency under 2 MPa vertical pressure
10_1016_j_soildyn_2024_109016.key_2:
- Bottom support: Fixed base
- Top support: Free to move in vertical and horizontal directions
- Unbonded configuration: Penalty surface-interaction with friction coefficient μ = 0.85 between isolator and supports
- Partially bonded configuration: Tie constraint for circular area (45 mm diameter) at lower and upper rubber pads; penalty contact elsewhere
- Vertical loading: Monotonically loaded to design load (2 MPa vertical pressure) and maintained during shear test
- Horizontal loading: Sinusoidal motion at 0.2 Hz frequency with displacement amplitudes of 100%, 150%, and 200% of total rubber thickness (tᵣ,ₜₒₜ)
- Rubber-fiber interface: Bonding strength of 4.5 N/mm (65% of minimum requirement)
- 3D FE model: Eight-node brick elements (C3D8RH) for rubber; 4-node doubly curved shell elements for fiber fabric
- Analysis type: Transient dynamic analysis with two fully reversed cycles for numerical simulations; three fully reversed cycles for experimental tests
- Vertical pressure: 2 MPa maintained during horizontal displacement application
- Shear strain levels: 100%, 150%, and 200% tᵣ,ₜₒₜ for cyclic shear testing
10_1016_j_soildyn_2024_109016.key_3:
- Dynamic response of fiber-reinforced elastomeric isolators under cyclic shear loading, including hyperelastic and viscoelastic behavior of rubber compounds and rollover deformation in unbonded configurations
- Horizontal stiffness (k_h), vertical stiffness (k_v), horizontal frequency (f_h), horizontal period (T_h), damping ratio (ξ), shear modulus (G), force-displacement hysteresis loops, stress-strain relationships, and energy dissipation (W_d)
- Minimize horizontal stiffness while maintaining high damping ability (target damping ratio ≥10%), achieve horizontal period T_h ≥0.8 s under 2 MPa vertical pressure, develop simplified analytical model with <10% error compared to 3D FE models, and optimize isolator geometry (shape factor S and aspect ratio R) for best seismic performance
10_1016_j_soildyn_2024_109016.key_4:

- Maximum 20% deviation in shear modulus/damping ratio between 0.1 Hz and 2 Hz frequencies
- Maximum +80%/-20% deviation at lowest temperature (-10°C/-15°C) compared to 23°C

- Maximum 20% deviation in properties after aging compared to unaged specimens
