10_1016_j_finel_2024_104247.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** Linear elasticity benchmark problems: Timoshenko cantilever beam, infinite plate with centered hole, and Single Edge Notched Tension (SENT) specimen
- **Material / Medium:** 
  - Cantilever beam: Young's modulus E = 3×10⁷ Pa, Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3, applied load P = 100 N
  - Infinite plate: Young's modulus E = 210 GPa, Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3, remote surface traction T = 1000 Pa
  - SENT specimen: Young's modulus E = 5.5 GPa, Poisson's ratio ν = 0.25, remote surface traction P = 100 MPa
- **Application & Importance:** Validation of the Overset Improved Element-Free Galerkin-Finite Element Method (Ov-IEFG-FEM) for solving linear elasticity problems with improved computational efficiency and accuracy, particularly in regions with high stress gradients (e.g., crack tips)
- **Geometry / Domain:**
  - Cantilever beam: Length L = 4.8 m, width D = 1.2 m, clamped left edge with parabolic shear load on right edge
  - Infinite plate: Modeled as 10×10 m quarter-plate, hole radius R = 1 m, symmetry constraints on x=0 and y=0 axes
  - SENT specimen: Full dimensions 0.2 m × 0.05 m, modeled as 0.05 m × 0.1 m half-specimen, initial crack length 0.025 m
10_1016_j_finel_2024_104247.key_2:
- **Boundaries & Constraints:**
  - Timoshenko cantilever beam: Left edge fixed with prescribed displacements u_x = -P(2+ν)y/6EI(y²-D²/4), u_y = PνL²/EIy²; right edge subjected to parabolic shear load distribution
  - Infinite plate with centered hole: Symmetry constraints (u_x = 0 along x=0 axis, u_y = 0 along y=0 axis) on quarter model
  - SENT specimen: Top edge subjected to remote surface traction; half of bottom edge constrained vertically; lower right corner kinematically constrained to avoid rigid body motions
  - Ov-IEFG-FEM interface: Displacement continuity enforced via u = ū_IEFG at nodes in background mesh and u = ū_FEM on IEFG boundary

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Timoshenko cantilever beam: Parabolic shear load t_xy = P/2I(D²/4-y²) with total applied load P = 100 N
  - Infinite plate with centered hole: Uniform horizontal remote surface traction σ_xx^∞ = T = 1000 Pa
  - SENT specimen: Remote uniform surface traction P = 100 MPa applied at top edge

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Ov-IEFG-FEM method features reciprocal transfer of kinematic information between overlapping domains
  - IEFG domain imposes displacements on FEM background mesh at nodes enclosed by S_IEFG→FEM
  - FEM background mesh imposes displacements on IEFG boundary Γ_IEFG via high-order local reconstruction
  - Penalty method used for displacement constraints on Γ_IEFG

- **Simulation Type:**
  - Linear static analysis for all benchmark problems
  - 2D plane stress conditions for Timoshenko cantilever beam and infinite plate with hole
  - 2D plane strain conditions for SENT specimen
  - Convergence analysis using normalized energy norm-based error
  - Comparison of FEM, IEFG, and Ov-IEFG-FEM approaches with varying mesh/node densities
10_1016_j_finel_2024_104247.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Linear elasticity problems with focus on displacement fields and stress distributions in solid mechanics

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**
  - Displacement components (u_x, u_y) along specified paths
  - Stress components (σ_xx, σ_yy, τ_xy) at critical locations
  - Mode-I stress intensity factor (K_I) for fracture mechanics analysis
  - Normalized energy norm-based error (E_norm) for convergence analysis
  - Computation time/CPU time for different numerical approaches
  - Comparison with analytical solutions for validation

- **Optimization Goal:**
  - Reduce computational cost while maintaining accuracy by restricting higher-order IEFG calculations to regions requiring enhanced precision
  - Achieve seamless coupling between FEM and IEFG domains without prescribed topological relationships
  - Provide over five-fold reduction in computation time compared to standard IEFG-based solutions while maintaining similar accuracy
  - Enable efficient handling of problems with localized high-stress gradients (e.g., near crack tips) without extensive mesh refinement throughout the entire domain
10_1016_j_finel_2024_104247.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:**
  - Distance between Γ_IEFG and S_IEFG→FEM must be 1.5-3 times the average background mesh element size
  - Separation distance between S_rec and Γ_IEFG must be at least one element size of the background mesh
  - Patch domain Ω_IEFG must be positioned in regions with high stress gradients (e.g., near crack tips or clamped boundaries) to be effective
  - Method validated specifically for benchmark geometries: Timoshenko cantilever beam (4.8m×1.2m), infinite plate quarter-model (10m×10m with 1m hole radius), and SENT specimen (0.05m×0.1m half-model)

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - Limited to linear elasticity problems only (not applicable to nonlinear behavior)
  - Effectiveness depends on problem characteristics: most beneficial for problems with localized high-stress gradients (e.g., crack tips) where error is dominated by a small region
  - Less effective for problems with significant displacement gradients throughout the entire domain (e.g., cantilever beam where no single region dominates the error)
  - Convergence rates are problem-dependent: E_norm ≈ O(N^-0.69) for cantilever beam, E_norm ≈ O(N^-0.64) for infinite plate with hole
  - Plane stress conditions for beam and plate problems, plane strain for SENT specimen

- **Process/Manufacturing:**
  - Iterative coupling between FEM and IEFG domains typically requires ~10 iterations for convergence
  - Computational cost is dominated by IEFG calculations in Ω_IEFG (support domain node determination and shape function computation)
  - Method requires careful positioning of patch domain Ω_IEFG to capture regions of interest
  - Accuracy of K_I calculation depends on proper placement of IEFG patch domain near crack tip
  - Comparisons are limited to cases with similar node counts across methods for equitable evaluation
  - The approach is constrained to 2D analysis as presented in the benchmark problems

10_1016_j_jobe_2022_105346.key_1:

- **Geometry / Domain:** 812.8 mm long × 205 mm wide × 12.7 mm thick splice plate with 20 × 20.7 mm diameter holes; two bolt columns with 95 mm spacing between columns, 63.5 mm spacing within columns, 76.2 mm edge distance; sinusoidal bearing pressure distribution along hole borders with P(x) = Pmax cos(πx/2R)
10_1016_j_jobe_2022_105346.key_2:

- **Loads / Excitations:** Sinusoidal bearing pressure distribution along hole borders with P(x) = Pmax cos(πx/2R); Pmax = 4F/(πD·t); 84 kN force per flange plate hole in plate longitudinal direction; Radial load F applied to bolt holes; Forces applied to holes half-perimeters with positive sign in X-direction (plate length direction)
- **Interactions / Interfaces:** Force transmission through bolt shear (non-preloaded connection); Contact between bolts shank and holes half-perimeter; Two bolt columns with 95 mm spacing; Bolt spacing of 63.5 mm within columns; 76.2 mm edge distance to plate boundaries
- **Simulation Type:** 2D plane stress model with triangular quadratic finite elements (STRI65); Linear elastic topology optimization with SIMP method; Non-linear FEA for validation; Density-based optimization approach; MMA solver; Energy Stiffness Measure Minimization objective function; Mesh convergence studies with structured mesh, free mesh, and free mesh with partitions
10_1016_j_jobe_2022_105346.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:** Linear elastic structural behavior during optimization phase; Non-linear material behavior including plasticity and ultimate capacity during validation phase; Stress distribution in steel plates with bolt holes; Displacement under tension loading; Topology optimization of steel connection plates
- **Target Outputs (Metrics):** Von Mises stress distribution; Peak stress (σMax) at most stressed location; Reference stress (σRef) at non-optimisable annulus outer perimeter; Displacement maps in longitudinal direction; Force-displacement relations; Ultimate capacity in kN; Volume fraction reduction percentage; Yield and ultimate stress exceedance areas; Energy Stiffness Measure; Mesh convergence parameters
- **Optimization Goal:** Minimize volume fraction (achieve maximum volume reduction) while maintaining structural capacity; Energy Stiffness Measure Minimization parametrized to target volume fractions; Ensure reference stress does not exceed yield strength (345 MPa) or ultimate strength (450 MPa) in elastic analysis; Maintain at least 840 kN ultimate capacity matching Eurocode-based joint capacity; Achieve 45% volume reduction while preserving original joint capacity as validated by non-linear analyses
10_1016_j_jobe_2022_105346.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space:** Non-optimisable domain including beam contact surfaces and annuli around bolts (20.7 mm interior diameter, 49.7 mm exterior diameter); Plate dimensions: 812.8 mm long × 205 mm wide × 12.7 mm thick; 20 × 20.7 mm diameter holes; Two bolt columns with 95 mm spacing; Bolt spacing of 63.5 mm within columns; 76.2 mm edge distance; Volume fraction lower boundary of 20-25% (below 30% volume fraction causes practical connection issues); Minimal external diameter = 2r_ext,min; Double-symmetry modeling constraint
- **Performance/Physics Limits:** Yield strength limit of 345 MPa (reference stress must not exceed in elastic analysis); Ultimate strength limit of 450 MPa (absolute maximum stress threshold); Joint capacity requirement of 840 kN (without safety factors); Maximum validated volume reduction of 45% (to 55% volume fraction) to maintain joint capacity; Reference stress must remain below yield strength for structural safety; Ultimate capacity must exceed joint capacity for practical application; Linear elastic optimization to 50% volume fraction exceeds safety needs when validated with non-linear analysis
- **Process/Manufacturing:** A325 steel bolts with 19.1 mm diameter in 20.7 mm holes; Non-preloaded connection (force transmission through bolt shear); Mesh requirements with ~2.5 mm node spacing to avoid shear locking; Use of triangular quadratic finite elements (STRI65); Compliance with Eurocode 3 structural design standards; Manufacturing constraints requiring minimum 30% volume fraction for structural connectivity; Standard bolt spacing and edge distances per construction practices; Sinusoidal pressure distribution along hole borders matching real-world load transfer mechanisms

10_1016_j_dt_2023_07_008.key_1:

10_1016_j_compscitech_2024_110864.key_1:
- **Identity & Domain:** 3D angle-interlock tubular woven composites (3DATWC) for axial compression performance analysis
- **Material Properties:**
  - Carbon fibers (SYT49S–12K): Tensile modulus 230 GPa, Tensile strength 4900 MPa, Density 1.79 g/cm³, Diameter 7 μm, Elongation 2.1%
  - Epoxy resin (ZTC-02A/ZTC-02B): Tensile modulus 2.0–2.5 GPa, Tensile strength 60–80 MPa, Density 1.12–1.14 g/cm³
- **Specimen Dimensions:** Φ 20mm diameter, 30mm height, wall thickness ranging from 2.01mm to 3.02mm depending on structure
- **Manufacturing Process:** Vacuum Assisted Resin Transfer Molding (VARTM) with 100:80 wt ratio of epoxy resin to curing agent
- **Curing Parameters:** 90 °C for 2 h, 110 °C for 1 h, and 130 °C for 4 h
- **Pre-treatment:** Fabric pre-dried at 100 °C for 1 h; resin degassed at 60 °C for 1 h
- **Testing Conditions:** Quasi-static compression at 2 mm/min loading rate
- **Structural Variations:**
  - Structure O: 0:1 warp lining yarn to warp binder yarn ratio
  - Structure F: 1:1 to 5:1 warp lining yarn to warp binder yarn ratios (F1-F5)
  - Structure S: 1:1 to 5:1 warp lining yarn to warp binder yarn ratios with inner weft layer replaced (S1-S5)
  - Structure T: 3:1 to 5:1 ratios with surface constraint yarn (T1-T3)
  - Structure T+: 3:1 to 5:1 ratios with increased weft density (T+1-T+3)
- **Fiber Volume Fraction:** Ranges from 32.57% (F5) to 47.11% (T+1)
- **Elastic Modulus Values:** 5.52-5.93 GPa for F structures, 7.88-10.92 GPa for T structures, 7.05-8.28 GPa for S structures
- **Test Repetition:** Minimum three repeated tests per sample
- **Weaving Equipment:** Single shuttle loom for fabric production
- **Weft Spacing:** 15 mm for standard structures, 12 mm for T+ structures
- **Yarn Configuration:** 56 columns of warp yarns in all 3DATWFs
- **Structural Comparison Metrics:** Ultimate load, plateau average load, ultimate stress, elastic modulus, energy absorption, specific energy absorption
10_1016_j_compscitech_2024_110864.key_2:
- **Boundary Conditions & Constraints:**
  - Quasi-static compression tests performed on INSTRON testing system (model 5969)
  - Cylindrical specimen height of 30 mm
  - Loading rate of 2 mm/min
  - Minimum three repeated tests per sample configuration
  - Fixed bottom boundary condition during compression testing
  - Top surface displacement-controlled loading

- **Loads / Excitations:**
  - Axial compressive load applied along the tubular specimen's longitudinal axis
  - Load range extending to ultimate load values up to 75,000 N for optimized structures

- **Interactions / Interfaces:**
  - Surface-based cohesive behavior defining yarn-matrix interface contact
  - Imperfect bonding interface between yarn and matrix
  - Warp binder yarns providing constraint to warp lining yarns
  - Weft yarns constraining warp yarn movement during compression
  - Fiber waviness angle of 10° considered in FEM analysis
  - Damaged yarn assumed to retain 90% of original performance in FEM

- **Simulation Type:**
  - Experimental: Quasi-static compression testing
  - FEM: Nonlinear analysis with progressive damage
  - 3D geometric models established for finite element analysis
  - Matrix modeled as elastic-plastic material using Von Mises yield criterion
  - Yarn modeled as unidirectional fiber-reinforced composite with linear elastic and transversely isotropic characteristics
  - Damage initiation defined by ductile and shear damage criteria for matrix
  - Hashin's quadratic failure criteria applied to yarn failure
  - Interface failure modeled using generalized method of cells approach
10_1016_j_compscitech_2024_110864.key_3:
- **Physics Solved:**
  - Axial compression mechanical behavior of 3D angle-interlock tubular woven composites
  - Progressive damage evolution including buckling, lodging, and cracking
  - Interfacial failure between yarn and matrix
  - Stress distribution in warp and weft yarns during compression
  - Energy absorption mechanisms during axial compression

- **Target Outputs (Metrics):**

  - Plateau average load (PAL)
  - Ultimate stress (US)
  - Elastic modulus (EM)
  - Total energy absorption (EA)
  - Specific energy absorption (SEA)

  - Maximize ultimate stress (77.46% increase achieved)
  - Maximize elastic modulus (142.55% increase achieved)
  - Maximize total energy absorption (119.06% increase achieved)
  - Maximize specific energy absorption (77.39% increase achieved)
  - Optimize structural parameters including proportion of warp lining yarn, layers of weft yarn, surface constraint yarn, and weft density
  - Reduce fiber waviness and improve interfacial properties to enhance axial compressive performance
10_1016_j_compscitech_2024_110864.key_4:
- **Geometric/Design Space Constraints:**
  - Fixed specimen dimensions: Φ 20mm diameter, 30mm height
  - Constant 56 columns of warp yarns across all structures
  - Wall thickness constrained between 2.01mm (S1) and 3.02mm (T+3)
  - Maximum warp lining yarn proportion limited by structural stability (beyond F3, performance degrades)
  - Weft spacing constrained to 15mm for standard structures and 12mm for T+ structures
  - Limited ability to increase weft density due to structural constraints

- **Performance/Physics Limits:**
  - Fiber waviness angle constrained to 10° in FEM analysis, significantly affecting compression performance
  - Interface strength threshold required for adequate axial compressive strength
  - Performance degradation occurs when warp lining yarn proportion exceeds structural constraint capacity
  - Ultimate load cannot exceed material strength limits (up to ~75,000 N in optimized structures)
  - Maximum usable warp lining yarn proportion before buckling and shear failure modes dominate (F5 shows poor performance)
  - Constraint on warp yarns must be sufficient to prevent performance reduction when increasing warp lining yarn proportion

- **Process/Manufacturing Constraints:**
  - Single shuttle loom manufacturing limitation affecting structural possibilities
  - Specific curing parameters required: 90°C for 2h, 110°C for 1h, 130°C for 4h
  - Resin preparation requirements: 100:80 wt ratio of epoxy to curing agent
  - Mandatory pre-treatment: preform drying at 100°C for 1h before resin impregnation
  - Resin degassing requirement: 60°C for 1h to remove all bubbles
  - Mandrel movement constraints during weaving process (forward/backward motion to prevent collisions)
  - Yarn damage during weaving process (assumed 10% performance loss in FEM)
  - Fiber straightness limitations during fabric preform preparation
  - Manufacturing process constraint: weft yarns must be "generally distributed in a parallel manner" due to beating-up of reed
  - Surface constraint yarn implementation limited to specific structural configurations (T and T+ structures)
